Ejemplo (incorrecto): Keep this between you and I.
Ejemplo (correcto): Keep this between you and me.

keyPoints: Los nombres propios llevan mayúscula.
Los sustantivos incontables como “advice” y “furniture” no tienen forma plural.
Usa pronombres de objeto después de las preposiciones.
Los pronombres reflexivos terminan en -self o -selves.
Los pronombres posesivos como “hers” y “theirs” no llevan apóstrofo.

yo.title: Noun àti pronoun
yo.short: Àwọn irú noun, countable àti uncountable noun, plural, àti bí a ṣe ń lo pronoun dáadáa.

sections.heading: Àwọn irú noun
sections.text:
Common noun jẹ́ orúkọ gbogbogbò, proper noun sì jẹ́ orúkọ ẹnì kan pàtó tàbí ibì kan pàtó. Proper noun máa ń gba capital letter (lẹ́tà ńlá). Concrete noun ń dárúkọ ohun tí o lè rí tàbí fọwọ́ kàn. Abstract noun ń dárúkọ èrò tàbí ìmọ̀lára. Collective noun ń dárúkọ àkójọ kan.
Àpẹẹrẹ: The city is busy. (common noun)
Àpẹẹrẹ: Nairobi is busy. (proper noun)
Àpẹẹrẹ: Her honesty surprised us. (abstract noun)
Àpẹẹrẹ: A herd of cattle crossed the road. (collective noun)

sections.heading: Countable àti uncountable noun
sections.text:
Countable noun (noun tí a lè kà) ní ìrísí singular (ẹyọ kan) àti plural (ju ẹyọ kan lọ). Èyí tó pọ̀ jù lọ nínú wọn máa ń fi -s tàbí -es kún un, ṣùgbọ́n àwọn kan máa ń yí padà pátápátá. Èdè Yorùbá sábà máa ń lo “àwọn” láti fi plural hàn, ṣùgbọ́n èdè Gẹ̀ẹ́sì sábà máa ń yí ìparí noun padà. Uncountable noun (noun tí a kò lè kà) kò ní plural nínú Standard English. Lára wọn ni advice, information, furniture, equipment àti luggage. Láti kà wọ́n, lo phrase kan ṣáájú noun náà.
Àpẹẹrẹ: one child, two children
Àpẹẹrẹ (àṣìṣe): She gave me many advices.
Àpẹẹrẹ (ó tọ́): She gave me a lot of advice.
Àpẹẹrẹ (ó tọ́): She gave me two pieces of advice.

sections.heading: Pronoun
sections.text:
Pronoun ń gbà wá lọ́wọ́ títún noun sọ. Subject pronoun ń tọ́ka sí ẹni tàbí ohun tó ń ṣe iṣẹ́ náà. Object pronoun ń tọ́ka sí ẹni tàbí ohun tí a ń ṣe iṣẹ́ náà sí. Possessive pronoun ń fi ẹni tó ni nǹkan hàn. Reflexive pronoun ń tọ́ka padà sí subject (olùwà) gbólóhùn náà. Èdè Yorùbá sábà máa ń lo “ó” kan náà fún he, she àti it nígbà tí wọ́n bá jẹ́ subject, ṣùgbọ́n èdè Gẹ̀ẹ́sì ní ọ̀rọ̀ ọ̀tọ̀ fún ọ̀kọ̀ọ̀kan, nítorí náà yan èyí tó tọ́.
Àpẹẹrẹ: She called him. (subject, lẹ́yìn náà object)
Àpẹẹrẹ: This pen is mine. (possessive)
Àpẹẹrẹ: Thabo taught himself to swim. (reflexive)

Possessive pronoun kì í gba apostrophe rárá. Preposition máa ń gba object pronoun.
Àpẹẹrẹ (àṣìṣe): Keep this between you and I.
Àpẹẹrẹ (ó tọ́): Keep this between you and me.

keyPoints: Proper noun máa ń gba capital letter.
Uncountable noun bíi advice àti furniture kò ní ìrísí plural.
Lo object pronoun lẹ́yìn preposition.
Reflexive pronoun máa ń parí pẹ̀lú -self tàbí -selves.
Possessive pronoun bíi hers àti theirs kò ní apostrophe.

ig.title: Nouns na pronouns
ig.short: Ụdị nouns, countable na uncountable nouns, plurals, na otú e si eji pronouns nke ọma.

sections.heading: Ụdị nouns
sections.text:
Common noun bụ aha n’ozuzu, proper noun bụkwa aha otu onye ma ọ bụ otu ebe a kapịrị ọnụ. Proper nouns na-amalite na capital letter (mkpụrụedemede ukwu). Concrete noun na-akpọ aha ihe ị nwere ike ịhụ ma ọ bụ imetụ aka. Abstract noun na-akpọ aha echiche ma ọ bụ mmetụta. Collective noun na-akpọ aha ìgwè.
Ihe atụ: The city is busy. (common noun)
Ihe atụ: Nairobi is busy. (proper noun)
Ihe atụ: Her honesty surprised us. (abstract noun)
Ihe atụ: A herd of cattle crossed the road. (collective noun)

sections.heading: Countable na uncountable nouns
sections.text:
Countable nouns (nouns a na-agụ ọnụ) nwere ụdị singular (maka otu) na ụdị plural (maka karịrị otu). Ihe ka ọtụtụ n’ime ha na-agbakwunye -s ma ọ bụ -es, mana ụfọdụ na-agbanwe kpamkpam. Uncountable nouns (nouns a naghị agụ ọnụ) enweghị plural na standard English. Ndị a gụnyere advice, information, furniture, equipment na luggage. Iji gụọ ha, tinye ìgwè okwu n’ihu noun ahụ.
Ihe atụ: one child, two children
Ihe atụ (nke na-ezighị ezi): She gave me many advices.
Ihe atụ (nke ziri ezi): She gave me a lot of advice.
Ihe atụ (nke ziri ezi): She gave me two pieces of advice.

sections.heading: Pronouns
sections.text:
Pronouns na-eme ka anyị ghara ikwughachi noun. Subject pronouns na-eme omume ahụ. Object pronouns bụ ndị omume ahụ na-emetụta. Possessive pronouns na-egosi onye nwe ihe. Reflexive pronouns na-ezo aka na subject nke ahịrịokwu ahụ. N’asụsụ Igbo, otu pronoun “ọ” (ma ọ bụ “o”) na-anọchi anya “he”, “she” na “it”, mana Bekee na-eji okwu atọ, ya mere lezie anya ka ị họrọ nke dabara.
Ihe atụ: She called him. (subject, sochie object)
Ihe atụ: This pen is mine. (possessive)
Ihe atụ: Thabo taught himself to swim. (reflexive)

Ọ dịghị mgbe possessive pronoun na-enwe apostrophe. Mgbe preposition gasịrị, a na-eji object pronoun.
Ihe atụ (nke na-ezighị ezi): Keep this between you and I.
Ihe atụ (nke ziri ezi): Keep this between you and me.

keyPoints: Proper nouns na-amalite na capital letters.
Uncountable nouns dị ka advice na furniture enweghị ụdị plural.
Jiri object pronouns mgbe prepositions gasịrị.
Reflexive pronouns na-ejedebe na -self ma ọ bụ -selves.
Possessive pronouns dị ka hers na theirs enweghị apostrophe.

ha.title: Nouns (sunaye) da pronouns (wakilan suna)
ha.short: Nau’o’in nouns, nouns masu ƙidayuwa da marasa ƙidayuwa, jam’i, da yadda ake amfani da pronouns daidai.

sections.heading: Nau’o’in nouns
sections.text:
Common noun (suna na gama-gari) suna ne na gaba ɗaya, proper noun (suna na musamman) kuma sunan wani mutum ko wuri ne na musamman. Proper nouns suna farawa da babban harafi (capital letter). Concrete noun yana ba da sunan abin da za ka iya gani ko taɓawa. Abstract noun yana ba da sunan wani tunani ko abin da ake ji a zuciya. Collective noun yana ba da sunan wani rukuni.
Misali: The city is busy. (common noun)
Misali: Nairobi is busy. (proper noun)
Misali: Her honesty surprised us. (abstract noun)
Misali: A herd of cattle crossed the road. (collective noun)

sections.heading: Countable nouns da uncountable nouns
sections.text:
Countable nouns (masu ƙidayuwa) suna da siffar tilo (singular) da ta jam’i (plural). Yawancinsu suna ƙara -s ko -es, amma wasu suna canzawa gaba ɗaya. Uncountable nouns (marasa ƙidayuwa) ba su da jam’i a standard English (daidaitaccen Turanci). Daga cikinsu akwai advice, information, furniture, equipment da luggage. Don ƙirga su, ka yi amfani da wani phrase (rukunin kalmomi) kafin noun ɗin.
Misali: one child, two children
Misali (ba daidai ba): She gave me many advices.
Misali (daidai): She gave me a lot of advice.
Misali (daidai): She gave me two pieces of advice.

sections.heading: Pronouns
sections.text:
Pronouns suna hana mu maimaita noun. Subject pronouns suna yin aikin. Object pronouns suna karɓar aikin. Possessive pronouns suna nuna mallaka. Reflexive pronouns suna komawa kan subject (mai yin aikin) na jimlar.
Misali: She called him. (subject, sannan object)
Misali: This pen is mine. (possessive)
Misali: Thabo taught himself to swim. (reflexive)

Possessive pronoun ba ya taɓa ɗaukar apostrophe. Prepositions suna ɗaukar object pronouns.
Misali (ba daidai ba): Keep this between you and I.
Misali (daidai): Keep this between you and me.

keyPoints: Proper nouns suna farawa da manyan haruffa (capital letters).
Uncountable nouns kamar advice da furniture ba su da siffar jam’i.
Ka yi amfani da object pronouns bayan prepositions.
Reflexive pronouns suna ƙarewa da -self ko -selves.
Possessive pronouns kamar hers da theirs ba su da apostrophe.

en.title: Verbs and the simple tenses
en.short: What verbs do, regular and irregular forms, and the simple present, past and future.

sections.heading: What a verb does
sections.text:
A verb shows an action or a state. Every complete sentence needs one. Tense is the form of the verb that shows time.

Each verb has main forms: the base form, the past form and the past participle. Regular verbs add -ed for both the past and the past participle. Irregular verbs change in other ways, and you must learn them.
Example: walk, walked, walked (regular)
Example: go, went, gone (irregular)
Example: write, wrote, written (irregular)

sections.heading: The simple present
sections.text:
Use this tense for habits, general truths and regular events. With “he”, “she”, “it” or a singular noun, the verb adds -s or -es.
Example: Water boils at 100 °C at sea level.
Example: Wanjiru walks to school every day.

For questions and negatives, use “do” or “does”, and then the base form of the verb.
Example: Does she like rice?
Example: He does not eat meat.

sections.heading: The simple past and future
sections.text:
Use the simple past for a finished action at a finished time. For questions and negatives, use “did” with the base form.
Example: Kofi visited Accra last week.
Example (wrong): Did he went home?
Example (right): Did he go home?

For the future, English often uses “will” or “be going to” with the base form. People often use “will” for a decision made at that moment. They often use “be going to” for a plan made earlier.
Example: I will help you with that bag.
Example: We are going to visit Durban in June.

keyPoints: Tense is the verb form that shows time.
Regular verbs add -ed, but irregular verbs must be learned.
In the simple present, he, she and it take a verb ending in -s or -es.
After do, does and did, use the base form of the verb.
The simple past describes a finished action at a finished time.

pcm.title: Verbs and the simple tenses
pcm.short: Wetin verbs dey do, regular and irregular forms, and the simple present, past and future.

sections.heading: Wetin verb dey do
sections.text:
Verb dey show action or state. Every complete sentence need one. Tense na the form of the verb wey dey show time.

Each verb get main forms: the base form, the past form and the past participle. Regular verbs dey add -ed for both the past and the past participle. Irregular verbs dey change in other ways, and you must learn them. Pidgin dey often show time with small words like “dey”, “don” and “go”, and the verb no dey change. Standard English dey often change the verb itself.
Example: walk, walked, walked (regular)
Example: go, went, gone (irregular)
Example: write, wrote, written (irregular)

sections.heading: The simple present
sections.text:
Use this tense for habits, general truths and regular events. With “he”, “she”, “it” or singular noun, the verb dey add -s or -es. Pidgin dey use “dey” for habit, like “Wanjiru dey waka go school every day”. Standard English no need that small word here, but the verb must add the -s.
Example: Water boils at 100 °C at sea level.
Example: Wanjiru walks to school every day.

For questions and negatives, use “do” or “does”, and then the base form of the verb. Pidgin fit ask with “She like rice?” and say no with “He no dey chop meat”. Standard English need the “does” for both.
Example: Does she like rice?
Example: He does not eat meat.

sections.heading: The simple past and future
sections.text:
Use the simple past for action wey don finish at time wey don finish. For questions and negatives, use “did” with the base form. Pidgin fit say “Kofi go Accra last week” and the verb no change, but Standard English must use the past form.
Example: Kofi visited Accra last week.
Example (wrong): Did he went home?
Example (correct): Did he go home?

For the future, English dey often use “will” or “be going to” with the base form. People dey often use “will” for decision wey dem make that same moment. Dem dey often use “be going to” for plan wey dem don make before. Pidgin dey use “go” for the future, like “I go help you”, but for Standard English, “go” na movement.
Example: I will help you with that bag.
Example: We are going to visit Durban in June.

keyPoints: Tense na the verb form wey dey show time.
Regular verbs dey add -ed, but you must learn irregular verbs.
For the simple present, he, she and it dey take verb wey end with -s or -es.
After do, does and did, use the base form of the verb.
The simple past dey describe action wey don finish at time wey don finish.

fr.title: Les verbes et les temps simples
fr.short: Le rôle des verbes, les formes régulières et irrégulières, et le présent, le passé et le futur simples.

sections.heading: Le rôle d’un verbe
sections.text:
Un verbe indique une action ou un état. Toute phrase complète en a besoin d’un. Le temps (tense) est la forme du verbe qui indique le moment.

Chaque verbe a des formes principales : la base verbale (base form), la forme du passé (past form) et le participe passé (past participle). Les verbes réguliers ajoutent -ed pour le passé et pour le participe passé. Les verbes irréguliers changent d’une autre façon, et tu dois les apprendre.
Exemple : walk, walked, walked (régulier)
Exemple : go, went, gone (irrégulier)
Exemple : write, wrote, written (irrégulier)

sections.heading: Le simple present (présent simple)
sections.text:
Utilise ce temps pour les habitudes, les vérités générales et les événements réguliers. Avec “he”, “she”, “it” ou un nom au singulier, le verbe ajoute -s ou -es.
Exemple : Water boils at 100 °C at sea level.
Exemple : Wanjiru walks to school every day.

Pour les questions et les phrases négatives, utilise “do” ou “does”, puis la base verbale.
Exemple : Does she like rice?
Exemple : He does not eat meat.

sections.heading: Le simple past (prétérit) et le futur
sections.text:
Utilise le simple past pour une action terminée à un moment terminé. Pour les questions et les phrases négatives, utilise “did” avec la base verbale.
Exemple : Kofi visited Accra last week.
Exemple (faux) : Did he went home?
Exemple (correct) : Did he go home?

Pour le futur, l’anglais utilise souvent “will” ou “be going to” avec la base verbale. On utilise souvent “will” pour une décision prise sur le moment. On utilise souvent “be going to” pour un projet décidé plus tôt.
Exemple : I will help you with that bag.
Exemple : We are going to visit Durban in June.

keyPoints: Le temps est la forme du verbe qui indique le moment.
Les verbes réguliers ajoutent -ed, mais les verbes irréguliers doivent être appris.
Au simple present, “he”, “she” et “it” sont suivis d’un verbe terminé par -s ou -es.
Après “do”, “does” et “did”, utilise la base verbale.
Le simple past décrit une action terminée à un moment terminé.

ar.title: الأفعال والأزمنة البسيطة
ar.short: وظيفة الأفعال، والصيغ القياسية والشاذة، والمضارع والماضي والمستقبل البسيط.

sections.heading: وظيفة الفعل
sections.text:
الفعل يدل على حدث أو حالة. وكل جملة تامة تحتاج إلى فعل. والزمن ⁦(tense)⁩ هو صيغة الفعل التي تدل على الوقت.

لكل فعل صيغ رئيسية: الصيغة الأساسية ⁦(base form)⁩، وصيغة الماضي ⁦(past form)⁩، واسم المفعول ⁦(past participle)⁩. وتضيف الأفعال القياسية ⁦(regular verbs) -ed⁩ في صيغة الماضي واسم المفعول معًا. أما الأفعال الشاذة ⁦(irregular verbs)⁩ فتتغير بطرق أخرى، ويجب أن تحفظها.
مثال: ⁦walk, walked, walked⁩ (قياسي)
مثال: ⁦go, went, gone⁩ (شاذ)
مثال: ⁦write, wrote, written⁩ (شاذ)

sections.heading: المضارع البسيط
sections.text:
استخدم هذا الزمن ⁦(simple present)⁩ للعادات والحقائق العامة والأحداث المنتظمة. ومع ⁦“he”⁩ أو ⁦“she”⁩ أو ⁦“it”⁩ أو اسم مفرد، يضيف الفعل ⁦-s⁩ أو ⁦-es⁩.
مثال: ⁦Water boils at 100 °C at sea level⁩.
مثال: ⁦Wanjiru walks to school every day⁩.

وفي الأسئلة والنفي، استخدم ⁦“do”⁩ أو ⁦“does”⁩، ثم الصيغة الأساسية للفعل.
مثال: ⁦Does she like rice⁩?
مثال: ⁦He does not eat meat⁩.

sections.heading: الماضي والمستقبل البسيطان
sections.text:
استخدم الماضي البسيط ⁦(simple past)⁩ لفعل منتهٍ في وقت منتهٍ. وفي الأسئلة والنفي، استخدم ⁦“did”⁩ مع الصيغة الأساسية.
مثال: ⁦Kofi visited Accra last week⁩.
مثال (خطأ): ⁦Did he went home⁩?
مثال (صحيح): ⁦Did he go home⁩?

وللمستقبل، كثيرًا ما تستخدم الإنجليزية ⁦“will”⁩ أو ⁦“be going to”⁩ مع الصيغة الأساسية. وكثيرًا ما يستخدم الناس ⁦“will”⁩ لقرار يُتخذ في اللحظة نفسها. وكثيرًا ما يستخدمون ⁦“be going to”⁩ لخطة وُضعت من قبل.
مثال: ⁦I will help you with that bag⁩.
مثال: ⁦We are going to visit Durban in June⁩.

keyPoints: الزمن ⁦(tense)⁩ هو صيغة الفعل التي تدل على الوقت.
تضيف الأفعال القياسية ⁦-ed⁩، أما الأفعال الشاذة فيجب حفظها.
في المضارع البسيط، يأتي مع he وshe وit فعل ينتهي بـ ⁦-s⁩ أو ⁦-es⁩.
بعد do وdoes وdid، استخدم الصيغة الأساسية للفعل.
يصف الماضي البسيط فعلًا منتهيًا في وقت منتهٍ.

sw.title: Vitenzi na njeo sahili
sw.short: Kazi ya vitenzi, maumbo ya kawaida na yasiyo ya kawaida, na njeo sahili za wakati uliopo, uliopita na ujao.

sections.heading: Kazi ya kitenzi
sections.text:
Kitenzi (verb) huonyesha kitendo au hali. Kila sentensi kamili inahitaji kitenzi. Njeo (tense) ni umbo la kitenzi linaloonyesha wakati.

Kila kitenzi kina maumbo makuu: umbo la msingi (base form), umbo la wakati uliopita (past form) na past participle (umbo linalotumiwa baada ya “have” na “be”). Vitenzi vya kawaida (regular verbs) huongeza -ed kwa umbo la wakati uliopita na kwa past participle. Vitenzi visivyo vya kawaida (irregular verbs) hubadilika kwa njia nyingine, na lazima uvijifunze.
Mfano: walk, walked, walked (cha kawaida)
Mfano: go, went, gone (si cha kawaida)
Mfano: write, wrote, written (si cha kawaida)

sections.heading: Wakati uliopo sahili (simple present)
sections.text:
Tumia njeo hii kwa tabia, ukweli wa jumla na matukio ya mara kwa mara. Pamoja na “he”, “she”, “it” au nomino ya umoja, kitenzi huongeza -s au -es.
Mfano: Water boils at 100 °C at sea level.
Mfano: Wanjiru walks to school every day.

Kwa maswali na sentensi kanushi, tumia “do” au “does”, kisha umbo la msingi la kitenzi.
Mfano: Does she like rice?
Mfano: He does not eat meat.

sections.heading: Wakati uliopita sahili na wakati ujao
sections.text:
Tumia simple past (wakati uliopita sahili) kwa kitendo kilichokwisha katika wakati uliokwisha. Kwa maswali na sentensi kanushi, tumia “did” pamoja na umbo la msingi.
Mfano: Kofi visited Accra last week.
Mfano (si sahihi): Did he went home?
Mfano (sahihi): Did he go home?

Kwa wakati ujao, Kiingereza mara nyingi hutumia “will” au “be going to” pamoja na umbo la msingi. Watu mara nyingi hutumia “will” kwa uamuzi unaofanywa wakati huo huo. Mara nyingi hutumia “be going to” kwa mpango uliofanywa mapema.
Mfano: I will help you with that bag.
Mfano: We are going to visit Durban in June.

keyPoints: Njeo ni umbo la kitenzi linaloonyesha wakati.
Vitenzi vya kawaida huongeza -ed, lakini vitenzi visivyo vya kawaida lazima vijifunzwe.
Katika simple present, “he”, “she” na “it” huchukua kitenzi kinachoishia kwa -s au -es.
Baada ya “do”, “does” na “did”, tumia umbo la msingi la kitenzi.
Simple past hueleza kitendo kilichokwisha katika wakati uliokwisha.

pt.title: Os verbos e os tempos simples
pt.short: O que fazem os verbos, as formas regulares e irregulares, e o presente, o passado e o futuro simples.

sections.heading: O que faz um verbo
sections.text:
Um verbo indica uma ação ou um estado. Todas as frases completas precisam de um. O tempo verbal (tense) é a forma do verbo que indica o tempo.

Cada verbo tem formas principais: a forma base (base form), a forma de passado (past form) e o particípio passado (past participle). Os verbos regulares acrescentam -ed tanto no passado como no particípio passado. Os verbos irregulares mudam de outras maneiras, e tens de os aprender.
Exemplo: walk, walked, walked (regular)
Exemplo: go, went, gone (irregular)
Exemplo: write, wrote, written (irregular)

sections.heading: O presente simples
sections.text:
Usa este tempo, o presente simples (simple present), para hábitos, verdades gerais e acontecimentos regulares. Com “he”, “she”, “it” ou um nome no singular, o verbo acrescenta -s ou -es.
Exemplo: Water boils at 100 °C at sea level.
Exemplo: Wanjiru walks to school every day.

Nas perguntas e nas negativas, usa “do” ou “does”, seguido da forma base do verbo.
Exemplo: Does she like rice?
Exemplo: He does not eat meat.

sections.heading: O passado simples e o futuro
sections.text:
Usa o passado simples (simple past) para uma ação terminada num momento terminado. Nas perguntas e nas negativas, usa “did” com a forma base.
Exemplo: Kofi visited Accra last week.
Exemplo (errado): Did he went home?
Exemplo (certo): Did he go home?

Para o futuro, o inglês usa muitas vezes “will” ou “be going to” com a forma base. Usa-se muitas vezes “will” para uma decisão tomada nesse momento. Usa-se muitas vezes “be going to” para um plano feito antes.
Exemplo: I will help you with that bag.
Exemplo: We are going to visit Durban in June.

keyPoints: O tempo verbal é a forma do verbo que indica o tempo.
Os verbos regulares acrescentam -ed, mas os irregulares têm de ser aprendidos.
No presente simples, “he”, “she” e “it” levam um verbo terminado em -s ou -es.
Depois de “do”, “does” e “did”, usa a forma base do verbo.
O passado simples descreve uma ação terminada num momento terminado.

es.title: Los verbos y los tiempos simples
es.short: Qué hacen los verbos, las formas regulares e irregulares, y el presente, el pasado y el futuro simples.

sections.heading: Qué hace un verbo
sections.text:
Un verbo muestra una acción o un estado. Toda oración completa necesita uno. El tiempo verbal (tense) es la forma del verbo que muestra el tiempo.

Cada verbo tiene formas principales: la forma base (base form), la forma de pasado (past form) y el participio pasado (past participle). Los verbos regulares añaden -ed tanto para el pasado como para el participio pasado. Los verbos irregulares cambian de otras maneras, y tienes que aprenderlos.
Ejemplo: walk, walked, walked (regular)
Ejemplo: go, went, gone (irregular)
Ejemplo: write, wrote, written (irregular)

sections.heading: El presente simple
sections.text:
Usa este tiempo para hábitos, verdades generales y hechos habituales. Con “he”, “she”, “it” o un sustantivo singular, el verbo añade -s o -es.
Ejemplo: Water boils at 100 °C at sea level.
Ejemplo: Wanjiru walks to school every day.

Para las preguntas y las negaciones, usa “do” o “does”, y luego la forma base del verbo.
Ejemplo: Does she like rice?
Ejemplo: He does not eat meat.

sections.heading: El pasado simple y el futuro
sections.text:
Usa el pasado simple para una acción terminada en un tiempo terminado. Para las preguntas y las negaciones, usa “did” con la forma base.
Ejemplo: Kofi visited Accra last week.
Ejemplo (incorrecto): Did he went home?
Ejemplo (correcto): Did he go home?

Para el futuro, el inglés suele usar “will” o “be going to” con la forma base. La gente suele usar “will” para una decisión tomada en ese momento. Suele usar “be going to” para un plan hecho antes.
Ejemplo: I will help you with that bag.
Ejemplo: We are going to visit Durban in June.

keyPoints: El tiempo verbal es la forma del verbo que muestra el tiempo.
Los verbos regulares añaden -ed, pero los irregulares hay que aprenderlos.
En el presente simple, “he”, “she” e “it” llevan un verbo terminado en -s o -es.
Después de “do”, “does” y “did”, usa la forma base del verbo.
El pasado simple describe una acción terminada en un tiempo terminado.

yo.title: Verb àti àwọn simple tense
yo.short: Iṣẹ́ verb, ìrísí regular àti irregular, àti simple present, past àti future.

sections.heading: Iṣẹ́ verb
sections.text:
Verb (ọ̀rọ̀ ìṣe) ń fi iṣẹ́ kan tàbí ipò kan hàn. Gbogbo gbólóhùn tó pé ló nílò rẹ̀. Tense ni ìrísí verb tó ń fi àsìkò hàn. Èdè Yorùbá máa ń lo àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ bíi “ti”, “ń” àti “yóò” ṣáájú verb láti fi àsìkò hàn, àti láti fi hàn bóyá iṣẹ́ náà ti parí tàbí ó ṣì ń lọ lọ́wọ́. Èdè Gẹ̀ẹ́sì náà máa ń lo irú àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ bẹ́ẹ̀ nígbà mìíràn, bíi “will”, ṣùgbọ́n ó tún máa ń yí verb náà fúnra rẹ̀ padà, bíi walk àti walked.

Verb kọ̀ọ̀kan ní àwọn ìrísí pàtàkì: base form (ìrísí ìpìlẹ̀), past form àti past participle. Regular verb máa ń fi -ed kún un fún past àti past participle. Irregular verb máa ń yí padà ní àwọn ọ̀nà mìíràn, o sì gbọ́dọ̀ kọ́ wọn.
Àpẹẹrẹ: walk, walked, walked (regular)
Àpẹẹrẹ: go, went, gone (irregular)
Àpẹẹrẹ: write, wrote, written (irregular)

sections.heading: Simple present
sections.text:
Lo tense yìí fún àṣà, òtítọ́ gbogbogbò àti àwọn ohun tó ń ṣẹlẹ̀ déédéé. Pẹ̀lú “he”, “she”, “it” tàbí singular noun (noun ẹyọ kan), verb náà máa ń fi -s tàbí -es kún un.
Àpẹẹrẹ: Water boils at 100 °C at sea level.
Àpẹẹrẹ: Wanjiru walks to school every day.

Fún ìbéèrè àti negative (gbólóhùn tó ní “not”), lo “do” tàbí “does”, lẹ́yìn náà base form verb náà.
Àpẹẹrẹ: Does she like rice?
Àpẹẹrẹ: He does not eat meat.

sections.heading: Simple past àti future
sections.text:
Lo simple past fún iṣẹ́ tó ti parí ní àsìkò tó ti parí. Fún ìbéèrè àti negative, lo “did” pẹ̀lú base form.
Àpẹẹrẹ: Kofi visited Accra last week.
Àpẹẹrẹ (àṣìṣe): Did he went home?
Àpẹẹrẹ (ó tọ́): Did he go home?

Fún future (ọjọ́ iwájú), èdè Gẹ̀ẹ́sì sábà máa ń lo “will” tàbí “be going to” pẹ̀lú base form. Àwọn ènìyàn sábà máa ń lo “will” fún ìpinnu tí a ṣe ní àkókò náà gan-an. Wọ́n sábà máa ń lo “be going to” fún ètò tí a ti ṣe tẹ́lẹ̀.
Àpẹẹrẹ: I will help you with that bag.
Àpẹẹrẹ: We are going to visit Durban in June.

keyPoints: Tense ni ìrísí verb tó ń fi àsìkò hàn.
Regular verb máa ń fi -ed kún un, ṣùgbọ́n a gbọ́dọ̀ kọ́ irregular verb.
Nínú simple present, he, she àti it máa ń gba verb tó parí pẹ̀lú -s tàbí -es.
Lẹ́yìn do, does àti did, lo base form verb náà.
Simple past ń ṣàpèjúwe iṣẹ́ tó ti parí ní àsìkò tó ti parí.

ig.title: Verbs na simple tenses
ig.short: Ihe verbs na-eme, ụdị regular na irregular, na simple present, past na future.

sections.heading: Ihe verb na-eme
sections.text:
Verb na-egosi omume ma ọ bụ ọnọdụ. Ahịrịokwu ọ bụla zuru ezu chọrọ verb. Tense bụ ụdị verb na-egosi oge.

Verb ọ bụla nwere isi ụdị ya: base form (ụdị ntọala), past form (ụdị oge gara aga) na past participle. Regular verbs na-agbakwunye -ed maka ma past form ma past participle. Irregular verbs na-agbanwe n’ụzọ ndị ọzọ, ị ga-amụtarịrị ha.
Ihe atụ: walk, walked, walked (regular)
Ihe atụ: go, went, gone (irregular)
Ihe atụ: write, wrote, written (irregular)

sections.heading: Simple present
sections.text:
Jiri tense a maka omume a na-emekarị (habits), eziokwu n’ozuzu na ihe na-eme oge niile. Mgbe subject bụ “he”, “she”, “it” ma ọ bụ singular noun (noun maka otu), verb na-agbakwunye -s ma ọ bụ -es.
Ihe atụ: Water boils at 100 °C at sea level.
Ihe atụ: Wanjiru walks to school every day.

Maka ajụjụ na ahịrịokwu na-agọnarị ihe (negatives), jiri “do” ma ọ bụ “does”, sochie ya base form nke verb ahụ.
Ihe atụ: Does she like rice?
Ihe atụ: He does not eat meat.

sections.heading: Simple past na future
sections.text:
Jiri simple past maka omume gwụchara agwụcha n’oge gafere agafe. Maka ajụjụ na negatives, jiri “did” na base form.
Ihe atụ: Kofi visited Accra last week.
Ihe atụ (nke na-ezighị ezi): Did he went home?
Ihe atụ (nke ziri ezi): Did he go home?

Maka oge dị n’ihu, Bekee na-ejikarị “will” ma ọ bụ “be going to” na base form. Ndị mmadụ na-ejikarị “will” maka mkpebi e mere n’oge ahụ. Ha na-ejikarị “be going to” maka atụmatụ e mere na mbụ.
Ihe atụ: I will help you with that bag.
Ihe atụ: We are going to visit Durban in June.

keyPoints: Tense bụ ụdị verb na-egosi oge.
Regular verbs na-agbakwunye -ed, mana a ga-amụtarịrị irregular verbs.
Na simple present, he, she na it na-eji verb na-ejedebe na -s ma ọ bụ -es.
Mgbe do, does na did gasịrị, jiri base form nke verb.
Simple past na-akọwa omume gwụchara agwụcha n’oge gafere agafe.

ha.title: Verbs (aikatau) da simple tenses
ha.short: Aikin verbs, siffofinsu na regular da irregular, da simple present, past da future.

sections.heading: Aikin verb
sections.text:
Verb (aikatau) yana nuna aiki ko wani yanayi. Kowace cikakkiyar jimla tana buƙatar guda ɗaya. Tense ita ce siffar verb da ke nuna lokaci.

Kowane verb yana da manyan siffofi: base form (siffa ta asali), past form (siffar lokacin da ya wuce) da past participle. Regular verbs suna ƙara -ed ga duka past form da past participle. Irregular verbs suna canzawa ta wasu hanyoyi, kuma dole ne ka koye su.
Misali: walk, walked, walked (regular)
Misali: go, went, gone (irregular)
Misali: write, wrote, written (irregular)

sections.heading: Simple present
sections.text:
Ka yi amfani da wannan tense don abin da mutum ya saba yi (habits), gaskiya ta gaba ɗaya da abubuwan da ke faruwa akai-akai. Tare da “he”, “she”, “it” ko singular noun (suna na tilo), verb yana ƙara -s ko -es.
Misali: Water boils at 100 °C at sea level.
Misali: Wanjiru walks to school every day.

Don tambayoyi da jimlolin korewa (negatives), ka yi amfani da “do” ko “does”, sannan base form na verb.
Misali: Does she like rice?
Misali: He does not eat meat.

sections.heading: Simple past da future
sections.text:
Ka yi amfani da simple past don aikin da ya ƙare a lokacin da ya wuce. Don tambayoyi da jimlolin korewa, ka yi amfani da “did” tare da base form.
Misali: Kofi visited Accra last week.
Misali (ba daidai ba): Did he went home?
Misali (daidai): Did he go home?

Don nan gaba, Turanci yakan yi amfani da “will” ko “be going to” tare da base form. Mutane sukan yi amfani da “will” don shawarar da aka yanke a daidai lokacin. Sukan yi amfani da “be going to” don shirin da aka yi tun da farko.
Misali: I will help you with that bag.
Misali: We are going to visit Durban in June.

keyPoints: Tense ita ce siffar verb da ke nuna lokaci.
Regular verbs suna ƙara -ed, amma dole ne a koyi irregular verbs.
A simple present, he, she da it suna ɗaukar verb mai ƙarewa da -s ko -es.
Bayan do, does da did, ka yi amfani da base form na verb.
Simple past yana bayyana aikin da ya ƙare a lokacin da ya wuce.

en.title: Adjectives and adverbs
en.short: How adjectives and adverbs describe, how to compare, and the correct order of adjectives.

sections.heading: Adjectives and comparison
sections.text:
An adjective describes a noun. It has three degrees. The positive degree simply describes. The comparative compares two things. The superlative compares three or more things.

Short adjectives add -er and -est. Most long adjectives use “more” and “most”. A few words are irregular. Never use “more” and -er together.
Example: tall, taller, tallest
Example: careful, more careful, most careful
Example: good, better, best
Example: bad, worse, worst
Example (wrong): This road is more safer.
Example (right): This road is safer.

sections.heading: The order of adjectives
sections.text:
When several adjectives come before a noun, English usually keeps a set order. Opinion comes first, then size, age, shape, colour, origin and material. The purpose of the object comes last, right before the noun. People rarely use more than three adjectives together.
Example: a beautiful old wooden chair
Example: a small round black pot

sections.heading: Adverbs
sections.text:
An adverb tells us more about a verb, an adjective or another adverb. It often answers a question such as how, when, where, how often or how much. Many adverbs end in -ly, but not all of them do.
Example: She sings beautifully. (how)
Example: We arrived yesterday. (when)
Example: They always eat together. (how often)
Example: The soup is very hot. (how much)

Students often confuse “good” and “well”. “Good” is normally an adjective, so it describes a noun. “Well” is normally an adverb, so it describes a verb. However, “well” is an adjective when it means healthy.
Example: Priya is a good singer.
Example: Priya sings well.
Example: I feel well today.

keyPoints: Use the comparative for two things and the superlative for three or more.
Never combine more with an -er adjective.
Adjective order: opinion, size, age, shape, colour, origin, material, purpose.
Many adverbs end in -ly, but words like very and always do not.
Good describes a noun, and well usually describes a verb.

pcm.title: Adjectives and adverbs
pcm.short: How adjectives and adverbs dey describe, how to compare, and the correct order of adjectives.

sections.heading: Adjectives and comparison
sections.text:
Adjective dey describe noun. E get three degrees. The positive degree dey just describe. The comparative dey compare two things. The superlative dey compare three or more things.

Short adjectives dey add -er and -est. Most long adjectives dey use “more” and “most”. Few words dey irregular. No ever use “more” and -er together. Pidgin dey compare with “pass”, like “this road safe pass that one”. Standard English dey change the adjective or add “more”.
Example: tall, taller, tallest
Example: careful, more careful, most careful
Example: good, better, best
Example: bad, worse, worst
Example (wrong): This road is more safer.
Example (correct): This road is safer.

sections.heading: The order of adjectives
sections.text:
When plenty adjectives come before noun, English dey usually keep one set order. Opinion dey come first, then size, age, shape, colour, origin and material. The purpose of the object dey come last, right before the noun. People no dey often use more than three adjectives together.
Example: a beautiful old wooden chair
Example: a small round black pot

sections.heading: Adverbs
sections.text:
Adverb dey tell us more about verb, adjective or another adverb. E dey often answer question like how, when, where, how often or how much. Many adverbs dey end with -ly, but no be all of them. Pidgin dey often repeat word to add force, like “hot well well”. Standard English dey use adverb like “very” for that kind place.
Example: She sings beautifully. (how)
Example: We arrived yesterday. (when)
Example: They always eat together. (how often)
Example: The soup is very hot. (how much)

Students dey often confuse “good” and “well”. “Good” na normally adjective, so e dey describe noun. “Well” na normally adverb, so e dey describe verb. But “well” na adjective when e mean healthy.
Example: Priya is a good singer.
Example: Priya sings well.
Example: I feel well today.

keyPoints: Use the comparative for two things and the superlative for three or more.
No ever join “more” with adjective wey end with -er.
Adjective order: opinion, size, age, shape, colour, origin, material, purpose.
Many adverbs dey end with -ly, but words like “very” and “always” no dey end so.
“Good” dey describe noun, and “well” dey usually describe verb.

fr.title: Les adjectifs et les adverbes
fr.short: Comment décrivent les adjectifs et les adverbes, comment comparer, et le bon ordre des adjectifs.

sections.heading: Les adjectifs et la comparaison
sections.text:
Un adjectif décrit un nom. Il a trois degrés. Le positif (positive) décrit simplement. Le comparatif (comparative) compare deux choses. Le superlatif (superlative) compare trois choses ou plus.

Les adjectifs courts ajoutent -er et -est. La plupart des adjectifs longs utilisent “more” et “most”. Quelques mots sont irréguliers. N’utilise jamais “more” et -er ensemble.
Exemple : tall, taller, tallest
Exemple : careful, more careful, most careful
Exemple : good, better, best
Exemple : bad, worse, worst
Exemple (faux) : This road is more safer.
Exemple (correct) : This road is safer.

sections.heading: L’ordre des adjectifs
sections.text:
Quand plusieurs adjectifs précèdent un nom, l’anglais garde généralement un ordre fixe. L’opinion vient d’abord, puis la taille, l’âge, la forme, la couleur, l’origine et la matière. L’usage de l’objet vient en dernier, juste avant le nom. On utilise rarement plus de trois adjectifs ensemble.
Exemple : a beautiful old wooden chair
Exemple : a small round black pot

sections.heading: Les adverbes
sections.text:
Un adverbe en dit plus sur un verbe, un adjectif ou un autre adverbe. Il répond souvent à une question comme comment, quand, où, à quelle fréquence ou à quel degré. Beaucoup d’adverbes se terminent par -ly, mais pas tous.
Exemple : She sings beautifully. (comment)
Exemple : We arrived yesterday. (quand)
Exemple : They always eat together. (à quelle fréquence)
Exemple : The soup is very hot. (à quel degré)

Les élèves confondent souvent “good” et “well”. “Good” est normalement un adjectif, donc il décrit un nom. “Well” est normalement un adverbe, donc il décrit un verbe. Cependant, “well” est un adjectif quand il signifie « en bonne santé ».
Exemple : Priya is a good singer.
Exemple : Priya sings well.
Exemple : I feel well today.

keyPoints: Utilise le comparatif pour deux choses et le superlatif pour trois choses ou plus.
Ne combine jamais “more” avec un adjectif en -er.
Ordre des adjectifs : opinion, taille, âge, forme, couleur, origine, matière, usage.
Beaucoup d’adverbes se terminent par -ly, mais des mots comme “very” et “always” non.
“Good” décrit un nom, et “well” décrit généralement un verbe.

ar.title: الصفات والظروف
ar.short: كيف تصف الصفات والظروف، وكيف تقارن، والترتيب الصحيح للصفات.

sections.heading: الصفات والمقارنة
sections.text:
الصفة ⁦(adjective)⁩ تصف الاسم. ولها ثلاث درجات. الدرجة العادية ⁦(positive)⁩ تصف فقط. وصيغة المقارنة ⁦(comparative)⁩ تقارن بين شيئين. وصيغة التفضيل ⁦(superlative)⁩ تقارن بين ثلاثة أشياء أو أكثر.

تضيف الصفات القصيرة ⁦-er⁩ و⁦-est⁩. ومعظم الصفات الطويلة تستخدم ⁦“more”⁩ و⁦“most”⁩. وقليل من الكلمات شاذ. ولا تستخدم ⁦“more”⁩ مع ⁦-er⁩ معًا أبدًا.
مثال: ⁦tall, taller, tallest⁩
مثال: ⁦careful, more careful, most careful⁩
مثال: ⁦good, better, best⁩
مثال: ⁦bad, worse, worst⁩
مثال (خطأ): ⁦This road is more safer⁩.
مثال (صحيح): ⁦This road is safer⁩.

sections.heading: ترتيب الصفات
sections.text:
عندما تأتي عدة صفات قبل اسم، تحافظ الإنجليزية عادةً على ترتيب ثابت. يأتي الرأي أولًا، ثم الحجم والعمر والشكل واللون والأصل والمادة. ويأتي الغرض من الشيء أخيرًا، قبل الاسم مباشرة. ونادرًا ما يستخدم الناس أكثر من ثلاث صفات معًا.
مثال: ⁦a beautiful old wooden chair⁩
مثال: ⁦a small round black pot⁩

sections.heading: الظروف
sections.text:
الظرف ⁦(adverb)⁩ يخبرنا بالمزيد عن فعل أو صفة أو ظرف آخر. وكثيرًا ما يجيب عن سؤال مثل: كيف، أو متى، أو أين، أو كم مرة، أو إلى أي مدى. وينتهي كثير من الظروف بـ ⁦-ly⁩، لكن ليس كلها.
مثال: ⁦She sings beautifully⁩. (كيف)
مثال: ⁦We arrived yesterday⁩. (متى)
مثال: ⁦They always eat together⁩. (كم مرة)
مثال: ⁦The soup is very hot⁩. (إلى أي مدى)

كثيرًا ما يخلط الطلاب بين ⁦“good”⁩ و⁦“well”⁩. فكلمة ⁦“good”⁩ صفة في العادة، ولذلك تصف اسمًا. وكلمة ⁦“well”⁩ ظرف في العادة، ولذلك تصف فعلًا. لكن ⁦“well”⁩ تكون صفة عندما تعني بصحة جيدة.
مثال: ⁦Priya is a good singer⁩.
مثال: ⁦Priya sings well⁩.
مثال: ⁦I feel well today⁩.

keyPoints: استخدم صيغة المقارنة لشيئين وصيغة التفضيل لثلاثة أشياء أو أكثر.
لا تجمع أبدًا بين more وصفة تنتهي بـ ⁦-er⁩.
ترتيب الصفات: الرأي، الحجم، العمر، الشكل، اللون، الأصل، المادة، الغرض.
ينتهي كثير من الظروف بـ ⁦-ly⁩، لكن كلمات مثل very وalways لا تنتهي به.
كلمة good تصف اسمًا، وكلمة well تصف عادةً فعلًا.

sw.title: Vivumishi na vielezi
sw.short: Jinsi vivumishi na vielezi vinavyoeleza, jinsi ya kulinganisha, na mpangilio sahihi wa vivumishi.

sections.heading: Vivumishi na ulinganishi
sections.text:
Kivumishi (adjective) hueleza nomino. Kina viwango vitatu. Kiwango cha kawaida (positive) hueleza tu. Kiwango cha ulinganishi (comparative) hulinganisha vitu viwili. Kiwango cha juu kabisa (superlative) hulinganisha vitu vitatu au zaidi.

Vivumishi vifupi huongeza -er na -est. Vivumishi virefu vingi hutumia “more” na “most”. Maneno machache hubadilika kwa njia isiyo ya kawaida. Usitumie kamwe “more” na -er pamoja.
Mfano: tall, taller, tallest
Mfano: careful, more careful, most careful
Mfano: good, better, best
Mfano: bad, worse, worst
Mfano (si sahihi): This road is more safer.
Mfano (sahihi): This road is safer.

sections.heading: Mpangilio wa vivumishi
sections.text:
Vivumishi kadhaa vinapokuja kabla ya nomino, Kiingereza kwa kawaida hufuata mpangilio maalum. Maoni huja kwanza, kisha ukubwa, umri, umbo, rangi, asili na malighafi. Kusudi la kitu huja mwisho, mara moja kabla ya nomino. Watu mara chache hutumia zaidi ya vivumishi vitatu pamoja.
Mfano: a beautiful old wooden chair
Mfano: a small round black pot

sections.heading: Vielezi
sections.text:
Kielezi (adverb) hutuambia zaidi kuhusu kitenzi, kivumishi au kielezi kingine. Mara nyingi hujibu swali kama vile vipi, lini, wapi, mara ngapi au kiasi gani. Vielezi vingi huishia kwa -ly, lakini si vyote.
Mfano: She sings beautifully. (vipi)
Mfano: We arrived yesterday. (lini)
Mfano: They always eat together. (mara ngapi)
Mfano: The soup is very hot. (kiasi gani)

Wanafunzi mara nyingi huchanganya “good” na “well”. “Good” kwa kawaida ni kivumishi, kwa hiyo hueleza nomino. “Well” kwa kawaida ni kielezi, kwa hiyo hueleza kitenzi. Hata hivyo, “well” ni kivumishi linapomaanisha kuwa na afya njema.
Mfano: Priya is a good singer.
Mfano: Priya sings well.
Mfano: I feel well today.

keyPoints: Tumia comparative kwa vitu viwili na superlative kwa vitu vitatu au zaidi.
Usichanganye kamwe “more” na kivumishi chenye -er.
Mpangilio wa vivumishi: maoni, ukubwa, umri, umbo, rangi, asili, malighafi, kusudi.
Vielezi vingi huishia kwa -ly, lakini maneno kama “very” na “always” hayaishii hivyo.
“Good” hueleza nomino, na “well” kwa kawaida hueleza kitenzi.

pt.title: Adjetivos e advérbios
pt.short: Como descrevem os adjetivos e os advérbios, como comparar e qual a ordem correta dos adjetivos.

sections.heading: Adjetivos e comparação
sections.text:
Um adjetivo descreve um nome. Tem três graus. O grau normal (positive) limita-se a descrever. O comparativo (comparative) compara duas coisas. O superlativo (superlative) compara três ou mais coisas.

Os adjetivos curtos acrescentam -er e -est. A maioria dos adjetivos longos usa “more” e “most”. Algumas palavras são irregulares. Nunca uses “more” e -er ao mesmo tempo.
Exemplo: tall, taller, tallest
Exemplo: careful, more careful, most careful
Exemplo: good, better, best
Exemplo: bad, worse, worst
Exemplo (errado): This road is more safer.
Exemplo (certo): This road is safer.

sections.heading: A ordem dos adjetivos
sections.text:
Quando vários adjetivos vêm antes de um nome, o inglês mantém normalmente uma ordem fixa. Primeiro vem a opinião, depois o tamanho, a idade, a forma, a cor, a origem e o material. A finalidade do objeto vem em último lugar, imediatamente antes do nome. Raramente se usam mais de três adjetivos juntos.
Exemplo: a beautiful old wooden chair
Exemplo: a small round black pot

sections.heading: Advérbios
sections.text:
Um advérbio diz-nos mais sobre um verbo, um adjetivo ou outro advérbio. Responde muitas vezes a uma pergunta como: como, quando, onde, com que frequência ou em que medida. Muitos advérbios terminam em -ly, mas nem todos.
Exemplo: She sings beautifully. (como)
Exemplo: We arrived yesterday. (quando)
Exemplo: They always eat together. (com que frequência)
Exemplo: The soup is very hot. (em que medida)

Os alunos confundem muitas vezes “good” e “well”. “Good” é normalmente um adjetivo, por isso descreve um nome. “Well” é normalmente um advérbio, por isso descreve um verbo. No entanto, “well” é um adjetivo quando significa saudável.
Exemplo: Priya is a good singer.
Exemplo: Priya sings well.
Exemplo: I feel well today.

keyPoints: Usa o comparativo para duas coisas e o superlativo para três ou mais.
Nunca combines “more” com um adjetivo em -er.
Ordem dos adjetivos: opinião, tamanho, idade, forma, cor, origem, material, finalidade.
Muitos advérbios terminam em -ly, mas palavras como “very” e “always” não.
“Good” descreve um nome, e “well” descreve normalmente um verbo.

es.title: Adjetivos y adverbios
es.short: Cómo describen los adjetivos y los adverbios, cómo comparar y el orden correcto de los adjetivos.

sections.heading: Los adjetivos y la comparación
sections.text:
Un adjetivo describe un sustantivo. Tiene tres grados. El grado positivo (positive) simplemente describe. El comparativo (comparative) compara dos cosas. El superlativo (superlative) compara tres o más cosas.

Los adjetivos cortos añaden -er y -est. La mayoría de los adjetivos largos usan “more” y “most”. Unas pocas palabras son irregulares. Nunca uses “more” y -er juntos.
Ejemplo: tall, taller, tallest
Ejemplo: careful, more careful, most careful
Ejemplo: good, better, best
Ejemplo: bad, worse, worst
Ejemplo (incorrecto): This road is more safer.
Ejemplo (correcto): This road is safer.

sections.heading: El orden de los adjetivos
sections.text:
Cuando varios adjetivos van delante de un sustantivo, el inglés suele mantener un orden fijo. Primero va la opinión, luego el tamaño, la edad, la forma, el color, el origen y el material. El propósito del objeto va al final, justo antes del sustantivo. Es raro usar más de tres adjetivos juntos.
Ejemplo: a beautiful old wooden chair
Ejemplo: a small round black pot

sections.heading: Adverbios
sections.text:
Un adverbio nos dice más sobre un verbo, un adjetivo u otro adverbio. A menudo responde a una pregunta como cómo, cuándo, dónde, con qué frecuencia o cuánto. Muchos adverbios terminan en -ly, pero no todos.
Ejemplo: She sings beautifully. (cómo)
Ejemplo: We arrived yesterday. (cuándo)
Ejemplo: They always eat together. (con qué frecuencia)
Ejemplo: The soup is very hot. (cuánto)

Los estudiantes suelen confundir “good” y “well”. “Good” es normalmente un adjetivo, así que describe un sustantivo. “Well” es normalmente un adverbio, así que describe un verbo. Sin embargo, “well” es un adjetivo cuando significa sano.
Ejemplo: Priya is a good singer.
Ejemplo: Priya sings well.
Ejemplo: I feel well today.

keyPoints: Usa el comparativo para dos cosas y el superlativo para tres o más.
Nunca combines “more” con un adjetivo terminado en -er.
Orden de los adjetivos: opinión, tamaño, edad, forma, color, origen, material, propósito.
Muchos adverbios terminan en -ly, pero palabras como “very” y “always” no.
“Good” describe un sustantivo, y “well” suele describir un verbo.

yo.title: Adjective àti adverb
yo.short: Bí adjective àti adverb ṣe ń ṣàpèjúwe, bí a ṣe ń fi nǹkan wéra, àti ètò tó tọ́ fún adjective.

sections.heading: Adjective àti ìfiwéra
sections.text:
Adjective (ọ̀rọ̀ àpèjúwe) ń ṣàpèjúwe noun (ọ̀rọ̀ orúkọ). Ó ní ìpele mẹ́ta. Positive degree kàn ń ṣàpèjúwe. Comparative ń fi nǹkan méjì wéra. Superlative ń fi nǹkan mẹ́ta tàbí jù bẹ́ẹ̀ lọ wéra.

Adjective kúkúrú máa ń fi -er àti -est kún un. Èyí tó pọ̀ jù lọ nínú àwọn adjective gígùn máa ń lo “more” àti “most”. Àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ díẹ̀ jẹ́ irregular (wọn kì í tẹ̀lé òfin yìí). Má ṣe lo “more” àti -er pọ̀ láéláé.
Àpẹẹrẹ: tall, taller, tallest
Àpẹẹrẹ: careful, more careful, most careful
Àpẹẹrẹ: good, better, best
Àpẹẹrẹ: bad, worse, worst
Àpẹẹrẹ (àṣìṣe): This road is more safer.
Àpẹẹrẹ (ó tọ́): This road is safer.

sections.heading: Ètò àwọn adjective
sections.text:
Nígbà tí adjective púpọ̀ bá wà ṣáájú noun, èdè Gẹ̀ẹ́sì sábà máa ń tẹ̀lé ètò kan pàtó. Opinion (èrò) ló máa ń kọ́kọ́ dé, lẹ́yìn náà size (ìtóbi), age (ọjọ́ orí), shape (ìrísí), colour (àwọ̀), origin (ibi tí nǹkan ti wá) àti material (ohun tí a fi ṣe é). Purpose (ohun tí a fi nǹkan náà ń ṣe) ló máa ń gbẹ̀yìn, ní kété ṣáájú noun náà. Àwọn ènìyàn kì í sábà lo ju adjective mẹ́ta lọ pọ̀.
Àpẹẹrẹ: a beautiful old wooden chair
Àpẹẹrẹ: a small round black pot

sections.heading: Adverb
sections.text:
Adverb (ọ̀rọ̀ àpọ́nlé) ń sọ ohun púpọ̀ sí i fún wa nípa verb, adjective tàbí adverb mìíràn. Nígbà púpọ̀, ó máa ń dáhùn ìbéèrè bíi báwo, ìgbà wo, ibo, ìgbà mélòó tàbí ìwọ̀n wo. Ọ̀pọ̀ adverb máa ń parí pẹ̀lú -ly, ṣùgbọ́n kì í ṣe gbogbo wọn.
Àpẹẹrẹ: She sings beautifully. (báwo)
Àpẹẹrẹ: We arrived yesterday. (ìgbà wo)
Àpẹẹrẹ: They always eat together. (ìgbà mélòó)
Àpẹẹrẹ: The soup is very hot. (ìwọ̀n wo)

Àwọn akẹ́kọ̀ọ́ sábà máa ń da “good” àti “well” pọ̀. “Good” sábà máa ń jẹ́ adjective, nítorí náà ó ń ṣàpèjúwe noun. “Well” sábà máa ń jẹ́ adverb, nítorí náà ó ń ṣàpèjúwe verb. Àmọ́, “well” jẹ́ adjective nígbà tó bá túmọ̀ sí pé ara ẹni le.
Àpẹẹrẹ: Priya is a good singer.
Àpẹẹrẹ: Priya sings well.
Àpẹẹrẹ: I feel well today.

keyPoints: Lo comparative fún nǹkan méjì, àti superlative fún nǹkan mẹ́ta tàbí jù bẹ́ẹ̀ lọ.
Má ṣe da more pọ̀ mọ́ adjective tó ní -er láéláé.
Ètò adjective: opinion, size, age, shape, colour, origin, material, purpose.
Ọ̀pọ̀ adverb máa ń parí pẹ̀lú -ly, ṣùgbọ́n àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ bíi very àti always kì í ṣe bẹ́ẹ̀.
Good ń ṣàpèjúwe noun, well sì sábà máa ń ṣàpèjúwe verb.

ig.title: Adjectives na adverbs
ig.short: Otú adjectives na adverbs si akọwa, otú e si atụnyere ihe, na usoro ziri ezi nke adjectives.

sections.heading: Adjectives na ntụnyere
sections.text:
Adjective na-akọwa noun. O nwere ogo atọ. Positive degree na-akọwa naanị. Comparative na-atụnyere ihe abụọ. Superlative na-atụnyere ihe atọ ma ọ bụ karịa.

Adjectives dị mkpụmkpụ na-agbakwunye -er na -est. Ihe ka ọtụtụ n’ime adjectives dị ogologo na-eji “more” na “most”. Okwu ole na ole bụ irregular. Ọ dịghị mgbe ị ga-eji “more” na -er ọnụ.
Ihe atụ: tall, taller, tallest
Ihe atụ: careful, more careful, most careful
Ihe atụ: good, better, best
Ihe atụ: bad, worse, worst
Ihe atụ (nke na-ezighị ezi): This road is more safer.
Ihe atụ (nke ziri ezi): This road is safer.

sections.heading: Usoro adjectives
sections.text:
Mgbe ọtụtụ adjectives bịara n’ihu noun, Bekee na-edebekarị otu usoro a kapịrị ọnụ. Opinion (echiche) na-ebu ụzọ, sochie size (nha), age (afọ), shape (ọdịdị), colour (agba), origin (ebe o si) na material (ihe e ji mee ya). Purpose (ihe e ji ihe ahụ eme) na-abịa n’ikpeazụ, ozugbo tupu noun ahụ. Ọ dị ụkọ ka ndị mmadụ jiri ihe karịrị adjectives atọ ọnụ.
Ihe atụ: a beautiful old wooden chair
Ihe atụ: a small round black pot

sections.heading: Adverbs
sections.text:
Adverb na-agwakwu anyị ihe banyere verb, adjective ma ọ bụ adverb ọzọ. Ọ na-azakarị ajụjụ dị ka how (otú), when (mgbe), where (ebe), how often (ugboro ole) ma ọ bụ how much (ruo ókè ole). Ọtụtụ adverbs na-ejedebe na -ly, mana ọ bụghị ha niile.
Ihe atụ: She sings beautifully. (how)
Ihe atụ: We arrived yesterday. (when)
Ihe atụ: They always eat together. (how often)
Ihe atụ: The soup is very hot. (how much)

Ụmụ akwụkwọ na-enwekarị mgbagwoju anya n’etiti “good” na “well”. “Good” na-abụkarị adjective, ya mere ọ na-akọwa noun. “Well” na-abụkarị adverb, ya mere ọ na-akọwa verb. Otú ọ dị, “well” bụ adjective mgbe ọ pụtara inwe ahụ ike.
Ihe atụ: Priya is a good singer.
Ihe atụ: Priya sings well.
Ihe atụ: I feel well today.

keyPoints: Jiri comparative maka ihe abụọ, jirikwa superlative maka ihe atọ ma ọ bụ karịa.
Ọ dịghị mgbe ị ga-eji “more” na adjective na-ejedebe na -er ọnụ.
Usoro adjectives: opinion, size, age, shape, colour, origin, material, purpose.
Ọtụtụ adverbs na-ejedebe na -ly, mana okwu dị ka “very” na “always” anaghị ejedebe otú ahụ.
“Good” na-akọwa noun, “well” na-akọwakarịkwa verb.

ha.title: Adjectives (siffofi) da adverbs (bayanau)
ha.short: Yadda adjectives da adverbs suke bayyanawa, yadda ake kwatantawa, da tsarin adjectives daidai.

sections.heading: Adjectives da kwatantawa
sections.text:
Adjective (siffa) yana siffanta noun. Yana da matakai uku. Positive degree yana siffantawa ne kawai. Comparative yana kwatanta abubuwa biyu. Superlative yana kwatanta abubuwa uku ko fiye.

Gajerun adjectives suna ƙara -er da -est. Yawancin dogayen adjectives suna amfani da “more” da “most”. Kalmomi kaɗan irregular ne. Kada ka taɓa haɗa “more” da -er tare.
Misali: tall, taller, tallest
Misali: careful, more careful, most careful
Misali: good, better, best
Misali: bad, worse, worst
Misali (ba daidai ba): This road is more safer.
Misali (daidai): This road is safer.

sections.heading: Tsarin adjectives
sections.text:
Idan adjectives da yawa suka zo kafin noun, Turanci galibi yana bin wani ƙayyadadden tsari. Ra’ayi (opinion) yana zuwa da farko, sannan girma (size), shekaru (age), sura (shape), launi (colour), asali (origin) da abin da aka yi shi da shi (material). Manufar abin (purpose) tana zuwa ta ƙarshe, daidai kafin noun. Ba kasafai mutane suke amfani da adjectives fiye da uku tare ba.
Misali: a beautiful old wooden chair
Misali: a small round black pot

sections.heading: Adverbs
sections.text:
Adverb (bayanau) yana ƙara mana bayani game da verb, adjective ko wani adverb. Sau da yawa yana amsa tambaya kamar yaya, yaushe, ina, sau nawa ko har wane mataki. Adverbs da yawa suna ƙarewa da -ly, amma ba duka ba ne.
Misali: She sings beautifully. (yaya)
Misali: We arrived yesterday. (yaushe)
Misali: They always eat together. (sau nawa)
Misali: The soup is very hot. (har wane mataki)

Ɗalibai sukan rikita “good” da “well”. “Good” a al’ada adjective ne, don haka yana siffanta noun. “Well” a al’ada adverb ne, don haka yana bayyana verb. Sai dai “well” adjective ne idan yana nufin lafiyayye (healthy).
Misali: Priya is a good singer.
Misali: Priya sings well.
Misali: I feel well today.

keyPoints: Ka yi amfani da comparative don abubuwa biyu, superlative kuma don abubuwa uku ko fiye.
Kada ka taɓa haɗa more da adjective mai -er.
Tsarin adjectives: opinion, size, age, shape, colour, origin, material, purpose.
Adverbs da yawa suna ƙarewa da -ly, amma kalmomi kamar very da always ba sa ƙarewa haka.
Good yana siffanta noun, well kuma galibi yana bayyana verb.

en.title: Prepositions and conjunctions
en.short: Using in, on and at, fixed preposition pairs, and joining ideas with conjunctions.

sections.heading: Prepositions of time and place
sections.text:
A preposition comes before a noun or pronoun and shows its link to another word. It often shows place, time or direction.

For time, use “at” for a clock time, “on” for a day or date, and “in” for a month, year or season. For place, “at” marks a point, “on” marks a surface, and “in” marks the inside of a space.
Example: The match starts at 4 o’clock.
Example: Her birthday is on Monday.
Example: We travel in July.
Example: Meet me at the bus stop.
Example: The book is on the table.
Example: The keys are in my bag.

sections.heading: Fixed pairs
sections.text:
Many verbs and adjectives take one particular preposition. Learn each pair together with the word.
Example: She is interested in music.
Example: He is good at maths.
Example: Our plan depends on the weather.

sections.heading: Conjunctions
sections.text:
A conjunction joins words, phrases or clauses. Coordinating conjunctions join parts of equal importance. There are seven: for, and, nor, but, or, yet and so.

Subordinating conjunctions join a less important clause to the main clause. They include because, although, when, if, while and until.
Example: Tom wanted to play, but it was raining.
Example: We stayed indoors because it was raining.

A common error is to use two conjunctions for one link. Use “although” or “but”, not both.
Example (wrong): Although she was tired, but she finished the work.
Example (right): Although she was tired, she finished the work.
Example (right): She was tired, but she finished the work.

keyPoints: Use at for clock times, on for days and in for months and years.
Learn fixed pairs such as interested in and depend on.
The seven coordinating conjunctions are for, and, nor, but, or, yet and so.
Subordinating conjunctions include because, although and when.
Do not use although and but to make one link.

pcm.title: Prepositions and conjunctions
pcm.short: How to use in, on and at, fixed preposition pairs, and how to join ideas with conjunctions.

sections.heading: Prepositions of time and place
sections.text:
Preposition dey come before noun or pronoun and e dey show how e connect to another word. E dey often show place, time or direction.

For time, use “at” for clock time, “on” for day or date, and “in” for month, year or season. For place, “at” dey mark one point, “on” dey mark surface, and “in” dey mark the inside of space. Pidgin fit use one word, “for”, for all of them, like “for Monday” and “for my bag”. Standard English dey make you choose among the three.
Example: The match starts at 4 o’clock.
Example: Her birthday is on Monday.
Example: We travel in July.
Example: Meet me at the bus stop.
Example: The book is on the table.
Example: The keys are in my bag.

sections.heading: Fixed pairs
sections.text:
Many verbs and adjectives dey take one particular preposition. Learn each pair together with the word.
Example: She is interested in music.
Example: He is good at maths.
Example: Our plan depends on the weather.

sections.heading: Conjunctions
sections.text:
Conjunction dey join words, phrases or clauses (groups of words wey get subject and verb). Coordinating conjunctions dey join parts wey get equal importance. Dem be seven: for, and, nor, but, or, yet and so.

Subordinating conjunctions dey join clause wey no too important to the main clause. Dem include because, although, when, if, while and until.
Example: Tom wanted to play, but it was raining.
Example: We stayed indoors because it was raining.

One common error na to use two conjunctions for one link. Use “although” or “but”, no use both.
Example (wrong): Although she was tired, but she finished the work.
Example (correct): Although she was tired, she finished the work.
Example (correct): She was tired, but she finished the work.

keyPoints: Use “at” for clock times, “on” for days and “in” for months and years.
Learn fixed pairs like “interested in” and “depend on”.
The seven coordinating conjunctions na for, and, nor, but, or, yet and so.
Subordinating conjunctions include because, although and when.
No use “although” and “but” to make one link.

fr.title: Les prépositions et les conjonctions
fr.short: L’emploi de “in”, “on” et “at”, les paires fixes de prépositions, et les conjonctions pour relier les idées.

sections.heading: Les prépositions de temps et de lieu
sections.text:
Une préposition se place devant un nom ou un pronom et montre son lien avec un autre mot. Elle indique souvent le lieu, le temps ou la direction.

Pour le temps, utilise “at” pour une heure, “on” pour un jour ou une date, et “in” pour un mois, une année ou une saison. Pour le lieu, “at” marque un point, “on” marque une surface, et “in” marque l’intérieur d’un espace.
Exemple : The match starts at 4 o’clock.
Exemple : Her birthday is on Monday.
Exemple : We travel in July.
Exemple : Meet me at the bus stop.
Exemple : The book is on the table.
Exemple : The keys are in my bag.

sections.heading: Les paires fixes
sections.text:
Beaucoup de verbes et d’adjectifs sont suivis d’une préposition bien précise. Apprends chaque paire avec le mot.
Exemple : She is interested in music.
Exemple : He is good at maths.
Exemple : Our plan depends on the weather.

sections.heading: Les conjonctions
sections.text:
Une conjonction relie des mots, des groupes de mots ou des propositions (clauses). Les conjonctions de coordination (coordinating conjunctions) relient des éléments d’égale importance. Il y en a sept : “for”, “and”, “nor”, “but”, “or”, “yet” et “so”.

Les conjonctions de subordination (subordinating conjunctions) relient une proposition moins importante à la proposition principale. On y trouve “because”, “although”, “when”, “if”, “while” et “until”.
Exemple : Tom wanted to play, but it was raining.
Exemple : We stayed indoors because it was raining.

Une erreur fréquente consiste à utiliser deux conjonctions pour un seul lien. Utilise “although” ou “but”, pas les deux.
Exemple (faux) : Although she was tired, but she finished the work.
Exemple (correct) : Although she was tired, she finished the work.
Exemple (correct) : She was tired, but she finished the work.

keyPoints: Utilise “at” pour les heures, “on” pour les jours et “in” pour les mois et les années.
Apprends les paires fixes comme “interested in” et “depend on”.
Les sept conjonctions de coordination sont “for”, “and”, “nor”, “but”, “or”, “yet” et “so”.
Les conjonctions de subordination comprennent “because”, “although” et “when”.
N’utilise pas “although” et “but” pour faire un seul lien.

ar.title: حروف الجر وأدوات الربط
ar.short: استخدام in وon وat، والأزواج الثابتة مع حروف الجر، والربط بين الأفكار بأدوات الربط.

sections.heading: حروف الجر للزمان والمكان
sections.text:
حرف الجر ⁦(preposition)⁩ يأتي قبل اسم أو ضمير ويبيّن صلته بكلمة أخرى. وكثيرًا ما يدل على المكان أو الزمان أو الاتجاه.

للزمان، استخدم ⁦“at”⁩ لوقت على الساعة، و⁦“on”⁩ ليوم أو تاريخ، و⁦“in”⁩ لشهر أو سنة أو فصل. وللمكان، تدل ⁦“at”⁩ على نقطة، و⁦“on”⁩ على سطح، و⁦“in”⁩ على داخل حيّز.
مثال: ⁦The match starts at 4 o’clock⁩.
مثال: ⁦Her birthday is on Monday⁩.
مثال: ⁦We travel in July⁩.
مثال: ⁦Meet me at the bus stop⁩.
مثال: ⁦The book is on the table⁩.
مثال: ⁦The keys are in my bag⁩.

sections.heading: الأزواج الثابتة
sections.text:
كثير من الأفعال والصفات يأتي معه حرف جر معيّن. فاحفظ كل زوج مع الكلمة معًا.
مثال: ⁦She is interested in music⁩.
مثال: ⁦He is good at maths⁩.
مثال: ⁦Our plan depends on the weather⁩.

sections.heading: أدوات الربط
sections.text:
أداة الربط ⁦(conjunction)⁩ تربط بين كلمات أو عبارات ⁦(phrases)⁩ أو جمل جزئية ⁦(clauses)⁩. وأدوات الربط التنسيقية ⁦(coordinating conjunctions)⁩ تربط بين أجزاء متساوية في الأهمية. وهي سبع: for وand وnor وbut وor وyet وso.

أما أدوات الربط التبعية ⁦(subordinating conjunctions)⁩ فتربط جملة جزئية أقل أهمية بالجملة الرئيسية ⁦(main clause)⁩. ومنها because وalthough وwhen وif وwhile وuntil.
مثال: ⁦Tom wanted to play, but it was raining⁩.
مثال: ⁦We stayed indoors because it was raining⁩.

ومن الأخطاء الشائعة استخدام أداتي ربط لرابط واحد. استخدم ⁦“although”⁩ أو ⁦“but”⁩، لا كلتيهما.
مثال (خطأ): ⁦Although she was tired, but she finished the work⁩.
مثال (صحيح): ⁦Although she was tired, she finished the work⁩.
مثال (صحيح): ⁦She was tired, but she finished the work⁩.

keyPoints: استخدم at لأوقات الساعة، وon للأيام، وin للشهور والسنوات.
احفظ الأزواج الثابتة مثل ⁦interested in⁩ و⁦depend on⁩.
أدوات الربط التنسيقية السبع هي for وand وnor وbut وor وyet وso.
من أدوات الربط التبعية because وalthough وwhen.
لا تستخدم although وbut معًا لتكوين رابط واحد.

sw.title: Vihusishi na viunganishi
sw.short: Matumizi ya “in”, “on” na “at”, jozi maalum za vihusishi, na kuunganisha mawazo kwa viunganishi.

sections.heading: Vihusishi vya wakati na mahali
sections.text:
Kihusishi (preposition) huja kabla ya nomino au kiwakilishi na huonyesha uhusiano wake na neno jingine. Mara nyingi huonyesha mahali, wakati au mwelekeo.

Kwa wakati, tumia “at” kwa muda wa saa, “on” kwa siku au tarehe, na “in” kwa mwezi, mwaka au msimu. Kwa mahali, “at” huonyesha sehemu mahususi, “on” huonyesha uso wa kitu, na “in” huonyesha ndani ya nafasi.
Mfano: The match starts at 4 o’clock.
Mfano: Her birthday is on Monday.
Mfano: We travel in July.
Mfano: Meet me at the bus stop.
Mfano: The book is on the table.
Mfano: The keys are in my bag.

sections.heading: Jozi maalum
sections.text:
Vitenzi na vivumishi vingi huchukua kihusishi kimoja mahususi. Jifunze kila jozi pamoja na neno lenyewe.
Mfano: She is interested in music.
Mfano: He is good at maths.
Mfano: Our plan depends on the weather.

sections.heading: Viunganishi
sections.text:
Kiunganishi (conjunction) huunganisha maneno, virai (phrases) au vishazi (clauses). Viunganishi vya usawa (coordinating conjunctions) huunganisha sehemu zenye umuhimu sawa. Kuna saba: “for”, “and”, “nor”, “but”, “or”, “yet” na “so”.

Viunganishi tegemezi (subordinating conjunctions) huunganisha kishazi chenye umuhimu mdogo na kishazi kikuu. Ni pamoja na “because”, “although”, “when”, “if”, “while” na “until”.
Mfano: Tom wanted to play, but it was raining.
Mfano: We stayed indoors because it was raining.

Kosa la kawaida ni kutumia viunganishi viwili kwa kiungo kimoja. Tumia “although” au “but”, si vyote viwili.
Mfano (si sahihi): Although she was tired, but she finished the work.
Mfano (sahihi): Although she was tired, she finished the work.
Mfano (sahihi): She was tired, but she finished the work.

keyPoints: Tumia “at” kwa muda wa saa, “on” kwa siku na “in” kwa miezi na miaka.
Jifunze jozi maalum kama “interested in” na “depend on”.
Viunganishi vya usawa saba ni “for”, “and”, “nor”, “but”, “or”, “yet” na “so”.
Viunganishi tegemezi ni pamoja na “because”, “although” na “when”.
Usitumie “although” na “but” kwa kiungo kimoja.

pt.title: Preposições e conjunções
pt.short: Como usar “in”, “on” e “at”, pares fixos com preposição e como ligar ideias com conjunções.

sections.heading: Preposições de tempo e de lugar
sections.text:
Uma preposição vem antes de um nome ou de um pronome e mostra a sua ligação a outra palavra. Indica muitas vezes lugar, tempo ou direção.

Para o tempo, usa “at” para uma hora, “on” para um dia ou uma data, e “in” para um mês, um ano ou uma estação. Para o lugar, “at” marca um ponto, “on” marca uma superfície, e “in” marca o interior de um espaço.
Exemplo: The match starts at 4 o’clock.
Exemplo: Her birthday is on Monday.
Exemplo: We travel in July.
Exemplo: Meet me at the bus stop.
Exemplo: The book is on the table.
Exemplo: The keys are in my bag.

sections.heading: Pares fixos
sections.text:
Muitos verbos e adjetivos levam uma preposição específica. Aprende cada par juntamente com a palavra.
Exemplo: She is interested in music.
Exemplo: He is good at maths.
Exemplo: Our plan depends on the weather.

sections.heading: Conjunções
sections.text:
Uma conjunção liga palavras, grupos de palavras (phrases) ou orações (clauses). As conjunções coordenativas (coordinating conjunctions) ligam partes de igual importância. São sete: for, and, nor, but, or, yet e so.

As conjunções subordinativas (subordinating conjunctions) ligam uma oração menos importante à oração principal. Entre elas estão because, although, when, if, while e until.
Exemplo: Tom wanted to play, but it was raining.
Exemplo: We stayed indoors because it was raining.

Um erro comum é usar duas conjunções para uma só ligação. Usa “although” ou “but”, não as duas.
Exemplo (errado): Although she was tired, but she finished the work.
Exemplo (certo): Although she was tired, she finished the work.
Exemplo (certo): She was tired, but she finished the work.

keyPoints: Usa “at” para as horas, “on” para os dias e “in” para os meses e os anos.
Aprende pares fixos como “interested in” e “depend on”.
As sete conjunções coordenativas são “for”, “and”, “nor”, “but”, “or”, “yet” e “so”.
As conjunções subordinativas incluem “because”, “although” e “when”.
Não uses “although” e “but” para fazer uma só ligação.

es.title: Preposiciones y conjunciones
es.short: El uso de in, on y at, las parejas fijas con preposición y cómo unir ideas con conjunciones.

sections.heading: Preposiciones de tiempo y lugar
sections.text:
Una preposición va delante de un sustantivo o un pronombre y muestra su relación con otra palabra. A menudo indica lugar, tiempo o dirección.

Para el tiempo, usa “at” con una hora del reloj, “on” con un día o una fecha, e “in” con un mes, un año o una estación. Para el lugar, “at” señala un punto, “on” señala una superficie e “in” señala el interior de un espacio.
Ejemplo: The match starts at 4 o’clock.
Ejemplo: Her birthday is on Monday.
Ejemplo: We travel in July.
Ejemplo: Meet me at the bus stop.
Ejemplo: The book is on the table.
Ejemplo: The keys are in my bag.

sections.heading: Parejas fijas
sections.text:
Muchos verbos y adjetivos llevan una preposición concreta. Aprende cada pareja junto con la palabra.
Ejemplo: She is interested in music.
Ejemplo: He is good at maths.
Ejemplo: Our plan depends on the weather.

sections.heading: Conjunciones
sections.text:
Una conjunción une palabras, frases o cláusulas. Las conjunciones coordinantes (coordinating conjunctions) unen partes de igual importancia. Hay siete: for, and, nor, but, or, yet y so.

Las conjunciones subordinantes (subordinating conjunctions) unen una cláusula menos importante a la cláusula principal. Entre ellas están because, although, when, if, while y until.
Ejemplo: Tom wanted to play, but it was raining.
Ejemplo: We stayed indoors because it was raining.

Un error común es usar dos conjunciones para un solo enlace. Usa “although” o “but”, no ambas.
Ejemplo (incorrecto): Although she was tired, but she finished the work.
Ejemplo (correcto): Although she was tired, she finished the work.
Ejemplo (correcto): She was tired, but she finished the work.

keyPoints: Usa “at” para las horas del reloj, “on” para los días e “in” para los meses y los años.
Aprende parejas fijas como “interested in” y “depend on”.
Las siete conjunciones coordinantes son “for”, “and”, “nor”, “but”, “or”, “yet” y “so”.
Las conjunciones subordinantes incluyen “because”, “although” y “when”.
No uses “although” y “but” para hacer un solo enlace.

yo.title: Preposition àti conjunction
yo.short: Lílo in, on àti at, àwọn preposition tó ń bá ọ̀rọ̀ kan rìn, àti síso èrò pọ̀ pẹ̀lú conjunction.

sections.heading: Preposition fún àkókò àti ibi
sections.text:
Preposition (ọ̀rọ̀ atọ́kùn) máa ń wá ṣáájú noun tàbí pronoun, ó sì ń fi bó ṣe tan mọ́ ọ̀rọ̀ mìíràn hàn. Nígbà púpọ̀, ó ń fi ibi, àkókò tàbí ìhà hàn.

Fún àkókò, lo “at” fún aago, “on” fún ọjọ́ tàbí déètì, àti “in” fún oṣù, ọdún tàbí àsìkò ọdún. Fún ibi, “at” ń tọ́ka sí ojú ibì kan, “on” ń tọ́ka sí orí nǹkan, “in” sì ń tọ́ka sí inú àyè kan.
Àpẹẹrẹ: The match starts at 4 o’clock.
Àpẹẹrẹ: Her birthday is on Monday.
Àpẹẹrẹ: We travel in July.
Àpẹẹrẹ: Meet me at the bus stop.
Àpẹẹrẹ: The book is on the table.
Àpẹẹrẹ: The keys are in my bag.

sections.heading: Fixed pairs (àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ tó ń rìn pọ̀)
sections.text:
Ọ̀pọ̀ verb àti adjective máa ń gba preposition kan pàtó. Kọ́ ọ̀kọ̀ọ̀kan pọ̀ mọ́ ọ̀rọ̀ tó ń bá rìn.
Àpẹẹrẹ: She is interested in music.
Àpẹẹrẹ: He is good at maths.
Àpẹẹrẹ: Our plan depends on the weather.

sections.heading: Conjunction
sections.text:
Conjunction (ọ̀rọ̀ àsopọ̀) ń so àwọn ọ̀rọ̀, phrase tàbí clause pọ̀. Coordinating conjunction ń so àwọn apá tó ṣe pàtàkì bákan náà pọ̀. Méje ni wọ́n: for, and, nor, but, or, yet àti so.

Subordinating conjunction ń so clause tí kò ṣe pàtàkì tó main clause (clause pàtàkì) pọ̀ mọ́ ọn. Lára wọn ni because, although, when, if, while àti until.
Àpẹẹrẹ: Tom wanted to play, but it was raining.
Àpẹẹrẹ: We stayed indoors because it was raining.

Àṣìṣe tó wọ́pọ̀ ni lílo conjunction méjì fún ìsopọ̀ kan. Lo “although” tàbí “but”, má ṣe lo àwọn méjèèjì.
Àpẹẹrẹ (àṣìṣe): Although she was tired, but she finished the work.
Àpẹẹrẹ (ó tọ́): Although she was tired, she finished the work.
Àpẹẹrẹ (ó tọ́): She was tired, but she finished the work.

keyPoints: Lo at fún aago, on fún ọjọ́, àti in fún oṣù àti ọdún.
Kọ́ àwọn tó ń rìn pọ̀ bíi interested in àti depend on.
Coordinating conjunction méje ni for, and, nor, but, or, yet àti so.
Lára subordinating conjunction ni because, although àti when.
Má ṣe lo although àti but láti ṣe ìsopọ̀ kan.

ig.title: Prepositions na conjunctions
ig.short: Iji in, on na at, prepositions na-eso okwu ụfọdụ mgbe niile, na ijikọ echiche site na conjunctions.

sections.heading: Prepositions nke oge na ebe
sections.text:
Preposition na-abịa n’ihu noun ma ọ bụ pronoun, ma na-egosi njikọ ya na okwu ọzọ. Ọ na-egosikarị ebe, oge ma ọ bụ ụzọ.

Maka oge, jiri “at” maka oge elekere, “on” maka ụbọchị ma ọ bụ ụbọchị ọnwa, na “in” maka ọnwa, afọ ma ọ bụ oge n’afọ (season). Maka ebe, “at” na-egosi otu ebe, “on” na-egosi elu ihe, “in” na-egosikwa ime ohere.
Ihe atụ: The match starts at 4 o’clock.
Ihe atụ: Her birthday is on Monday.
Ihe atụ: We travel in July.
Ihe atụ: Meet me at the bus stop.
Ihe atụ: The book is on the table.
Ihe atụ: The keys are in my bag.

sections.heading: Okwu na-aga ọnụ mgbe niile
sections.text:
Ọtụtụ verbs na adjectives na-eji otu preposition a kapịrị ọnụ. Mụta preposition ọ bụla ọnụ na okwu ya.
Ihe atụ: She is interested in music.
Ihe atụ: He is good at maths.
Ihe atụ: Our plan depends on the weather.

sections.heading: Conjunctions
sections.text:
Conjunction na-ejikọ okwu, phrases ma ọ bụ clauses. Coordinating conjunctions na-ejikọ akụkụ ndị dị mkpa nhata. Ha dị asaa: for, and, nor, but, or, yet na so.

Subordinating conjunctions na-ejikọ clause nke mkpa ya na-erughị nke main clause na main clause ahụ. Ha gụnyere because, although, when, if, while na until.
Ihe atụ: Tom wanted to play, but it was raining.
Ihe atụ: We stayed indoors because it was raining.

Otu mmejọ a na-emekarị bụ iji conjunctions abụọ maka otu njikọ. Jiri “although” ma ọ bụ “but”, ọ bụghị ha abụọ.
Ihe atụ (nke na-ezighị ezi): Although she was tired, but she finished the work.
Ihe atụ (nke ziri ezi): Although she was tired, she finished the work.
Ihe atụ (nke ziri ezi): She was tired, but she finished the work.

keyPoints: Jiri “at” maka oge elekere, “on” maka ụbọchị, “in” maka ọnwa na afọ.
Mụta okwu na-aga ọnụ dị ka “interested in” na “depend on”.
Coordinating conjunctions asaa ahụ bụ for, and, nor, but, or, yet na so.
Subordinating conjunctions gụnyere because, although na when.
Ejila “although” na “but” ọnụ mee otu njikọ.

ha.title: Prepositions da conjunctions (mahaɗai)
ha.short: Amfani da in, on da at, ƙayyadaddun haɗe-haɗen prepositions, da haɗa tunani da conjunctions.

sections.heading: Prepositions na lokaci da wuri
sections.text:
Preposition yana zuwa kafin noun ko pronoun, kuma yana nuna alaƙarsa da wata kalma. Sau da yawa yana nuna wuri, lokaci ko hanya (direction).

Don lokaci, ka yi amfani da “at” don lokacin agogo, “on” don rana ko kwanan wata, “in” kuma don wata, shekara ko yanayi na shekara (season). Don wuri, “at” yana nuna wani wuri guda (a point), “on” yana nuna saman abu (a surface), “in” kuma yana nuna cikin wani fili ko abu (the inside of a space).
Misali: The match starts at 4 o’clock.
Misali: Her birthday is on Monday.
Misali: We travel in July.
Misali: Meet me at the bus stop.
Misali: The book is on the table.
Misali: The keys are in my bag.

sections.heading: Ƙayyadaddun haɗe-haɗe
sections.text:
Verbs da adjectives da yawa suna ɗaukar wani preposition na musamman. Ka koyi kowane haɗi tare da kalmar.
Misali: She is interested in music.
Misali: He is good at maths.
Misali: Our plan depends on the weather.

sections.heading: Conjunctions
sections.text:
Conjunction (mahaɗi) yana haɗa kalmomi, phrases (rukunan kalmomi) ko clauses (rukunan kalmomi masu ɗauke da verb). Coordinating conjunctions suna haɗa sassan da muhimmancinsu ya yi daidai. Guda bakwai ne: for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so.

Subordinating conjunctions suna haɗa clause mai ƙarancin muhimmanci da main clause (babban clause). Daga cikinsu akwai because, although, when, if, while da until.
Misali: Tom wanted to play, but it was raining.
Misali: We stayed indoors because it was raining.

Wani kuskure da aka saba yi shi ne amfani da conjunctions biyu don haɗi ɗaya. Ka yi amfani da “although” ko “but”, ba duka biyun ba.
Misali (ba daidai ba): Although she was tired, but she finished the work.
Misali (daidai): Although she was tired, she finished the work.
Misali (daidai): She was tired, but she finished the work.

keyPoints: Ka yi amfani da at don lokacin agogo, on don ranaku, in kuma don watanni da shekaru.
Ka koyi ƙayyadaddun haɗe-haɗe kamar interested in da depend on.
Coordinating conjunctions guda bakwai su ne for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so.
Daga cikin subordinating conjunctions akwai because, although da when.
Kada ka yi amfani da although da but don yin haɗi ɗaya.

en.title: Building a sentence
en.short: Subject, predicate and object, the four kinds of sentence, and how to avoid incomplete sentences.

sections.heading: The parts of a sentence
sections.text:
A sentence is a group of words that makes complete sense. It usually has two parts. The subject tells us who or what the sentence is about. The predicate tells us something about the subject, and it contains the verb. Many sentences also have an object, which receives the action of the verb.

English statements normally follow the order subject, then verb, then object.
Example: Fatima reads a newspaper.

Here “Fatima” is the subject, “reads a newspaper” is the predicate, and “a newspaper” is the object.

sections.heading: Four kinds of sentence
sections.text:
Sentences do four main jobs, and each has its usual end mark.

A statement gives information.
Example: The market opens at seven.

A question asks for information.
Example: When does the market open?

A command tells someone to do something. Its subject, “you”, is usually left out.
Example: Close the window.

An exclamation shows strong feeling.
Example: What a lovely day it is!

sections.heading: Two common errors
sections.text:
A fragment is an incomplete sentence. It may have no verb or no complete idea.
Example (wrong): Because the bus was late.
Example (right): I missed the lesson because the bus was late.

A run-on sentence joins two sentences with no correct link. To fix it, use a full stop, or add a joining word.
Example (wrong): The rain stopped we went outside.
Example (right): The rain stopped. We went outside.
Example (right): The rain stopped, so we went outside.

To test your work, read each sentence alone. If it does not make sense by itself, correct it.

keyPoints: A sentence must make complete sense.
The subject is who or what the sentence is about.
The predicate contains the verb and says something about the subject.
The object receives the action of the verb.
Sentences can be statements, questions, commands or exclamations.
Avoid fragments and run-on sentences.

pcm.title: How to build sentence
pcm.short: Subject, predicate and object, the four kinds of sentence, and how to avoid sentence wey no complete.

sections.heading: The parts of sentence
sections.text:
Sentence na group of words wey make complete sense. E usually get two parts. The subject dey tell us who or wetin the sentence dey talk about. The predicate dey tell us something about the subject, and the verb dey inside am. Many sentences also get object, wey dey receive the action of the verb.

English statements dey normally follow this order: subject, then verb, then object. Pidgin dey follow the same order, like “Fatima dey read newspaper”.
Example: Fatima reads a newspaper.

For here, “Fatima” na the subject, “reads a newspaper” na the predicate, and “a newspaper” na the object.

sections.heading: Four kinds of sentence
sections.text:
Sentences dey do four main work, and each one get the mark wey dey usually end am.

Statement dey give information.
Example: The market opens at seven.

Question dey ask for information.
Example: When does the market open?

Command dey tell person to do something. Im subject, “you”, dey usually comot.
Example: Close the window.

Exclamation dey show strong feeling.
Example: What a lovely day it is!

sections.heading: Two common errors
sections.text:
Fragment na sentence wey no complete. E fit no get verb or complete idea.
Example (wrong): Because the bus was late.
Example (correct): I missed the lesson because the bus was late.

Run-on sentence dey join two sentences without correct link. To fix am, use full stop, or add joining word.
Example (wrong): The rain stopped we went outside.
Example (correct): The rain stopped. We went outside.
Example (correct): The rain stopped, so we went outside.

To test your work, read each sentence alone. If e no make sense by itself, correct am.

keyPoints: Sentence must make complete sense.
The subject na who or wetin the sentence dey talk about.
The predicate get the verb and e dey talk something about the subject.
The object dey receive the action of the verb.
Sentences fit be statements, questions, commands or exclamations.
Avoid fragments and run-on sentences.

fr.title: Construire une phrase
fr.short: Le sujet, le prédicat et le complément d’objet, les quatre sortes de phrases, et comment éviter les phrases incomplètes.

sections.heading: Les parties d’une phrase
sections.text:
Une phrase (sentence) est un groupe de mots qui a un sens complet. Elle a généralement deux parties. Le sujet (subject) nous dit de qui ou de quoi parle la phrase. Le prédicat (predicate) nous dit quelque chose sur le sujet, et il contient le verbe. Beaucoup de phrases ont aussi un complément d’objet (object), qui reçoit l’action du verbe.

Les phrases déclaratives en anglais suivent normalement l’ordre sujet, puis verbe, puis complément d’objet.
Exemple : Fatima reads a newspaper.

Ici, “Fatima” est le sujet, “reads a newspaper” est le prédicat et “a newspaper” est le complément d’objet.

sections.heading: Quatre sortes de phrases
sections.text:
Les phrases ont quatre rôles principaux, et chacune a son signe de fin habituel.

Une phrase déclarative (statement) donne une information.
Exemple : The market opens at seven.

Une question (question) demande une information.
Exemple : When does the market open?

Un ordre (command) dit à quelqu’un de faire quelque chose. Son sujet, “you”, est généralement omis.
Exemple : Close the window.

Une exclamation (exclamation) exprime un sentiment fort.
