Concord pụtara ikwekọ. Singular subject (subject maka otu) na-eji singular verb, plural subject (subject maka karịrị otu) na-ejikwa plural verb. Iji lelee, buru ụzọ chọta ezi subject ahụ. Okwu dị n’etiti subject na verb anaghị agbanwe ya.
Ihe atụ: The box of pens is on the desk.
Ihe atụ: One of the boys has left.

Okwu “each”, “every”, “everyone” na “nobody” na-eji singular verb.
Ihe atụ: Each of the girls is ready.

sections.heading: Subjects e jikọrọ ọnụ
sections.text:
Subjects e ji “and” jikọọ na-ejikarị plural verb. Ọ bụrụ na ha bụ otu echiche, verb ahụ bụ singular. Na “either...or” na “neither...nor”, verb na-ekwekọ na subject kacha nso ya.
Ihe atụ: Otieno and Mei are here.
Ihe atụ: Rice and stew is my favourite meal.
Ihe atụ: Neither the teacher nor the students were late.
Ihe atụ: Neither the students nor the teacher was late.

sections.heading: Subjects siri ike
sections.text:
Collective nouns dị ka team ma ọ bụ family nwere ike iji singular verb ma ọ bụ plural verb na Bekee Britain. Jiri singular verb ma ọ bụrụ na ìgwè ahụ na-eme ihe dị ka otu. Jiri plural verb ma ọ bụrụ na ndị so na ya na-eme ihe iche iche. Bekee America na-ahọrọkarị singular.
Ihe atụ: The team is in first place.
Ihe atụ: The team are arguing among themselves.

Ụfọdụ nouns na-ejedebe na -s mana ha bụ singular. Ego na oge a na-agụ dị ka otu mkpokọta na-ejikwa singular verb.
Ihe atụ: The news is good.
Ihe atụ: Physics is my best subject.
Ihe atụ: Five thousand naira is enough.

Tụnyere phrases abụọ a a na-ejikarị.
Ihe atụ: A number of students are absent.
Ihe atụ: The number of students is falling.

keyPoints: Chọta ezi subject, leghara okwu dị n’etiti ya na verb anya.
Each, every na everyone na-eji singular verb.
Na neither...nor, verb na-ekwekọ na subject kacha nso ya.
“A number of” na-eji plural verb, “the number of” na-ejikwa singular verb.
Collective nouns na-eji singular verb ma ọ bụ plural verb na Bekee Britain, dabere n’ihe ọ pụtara.

ha.title: Concord: dacewar subject da verb
ha.short: Yadda verbs suke dacewa da subjects ɗinsu, har da wurare masu wuya da jarrabawa ta fi gwadawa.

sections.heading: Ƙa’ida ta asali
sections.text:
Concord yana nufin dacewa (agreement). Singular subject (na tilo) yana ɗaukar singular verb, plural subject (na jam’i) kuma yana ɗaukar plural verb. Don dubawa, ka fara nemo ainihin subject. Kalmomin da ke tsakanin subject da verb ba sa canza shi.
Misali: The box of pens is on the desk.
Misali: One of the boys has left.

Kalmomin “each”, “every”, “everyone” da “nobody” suna ɗaukar singular verb.
Misali: Each of the girls is ready.

sections.heading: Subjects da aka haɗa
sections.text:
Subjects da aka haɗa da “and” galibi suna ɗaukar plural verb. Idan suka zama tunani ɗaya, verb singular ne. Tare da “either...or” da “neither...nor”, verb yana dacewa da subject wanda ya fi kusa da shi.
Misali: Otieno and Mei are here.
Misali: Rice and stew is my favourite meal.
Misali: Neither the teacher nor the students were late.
Misali: Neither the students nor the teacher was late.

sections.heading: Subjects masu wuya
sections.text:
Collective nouns (sunayen rukuni) kamar team ko family suna iya ɗaukar ko singular verb ko plural verb a Turancin Birtaniya (British English). Ka yi amfani da singular verb idan rukunin yana aiki a matsayin abu ɗaya. Ka yi amfani da plural verb idan membobin suna aiki daban-daban. Turancin Amurka (American English) galibi ya fi son singular.
Misali: The team is in first place.
Misali: The team are arguing among themselves.

Wasu nouns suna ƙarewa da -s amma singular ne. Haka kuma adadin kuɗi da tsawon lokaci da aka ɗauka a matsayin adadi ɗaya suna ɗaukar singular verb.
Misali: The news is good.
Misali: Physics is my best subject.
Misali: Five thousand naira is enough.

Ka kwatanta waɗannan phrases biyu da aka saba amfani da su.
Misali: A number of students are absent.
Misali: The number of students is falling.

keyPoints: Ka nemo ainihin subject, kuma ka ƙyale kalmomin da ke tsakaninsa da verb.
Each, every da everyone suna ɗaukar singular verb.
Tare da neither...nor, verb yana dacewa da subject wanda ya fi kusa da shi.
A number of yana ɗaukar plural verb, the number of kuma yana ɗaukar singular verb.
Collective nouns suna ɗaukar ko singular verb ko plural verb a Turancin Birtaniya, ya danganta da ma’ana.

en.title: Continuous and perfect tenses
en.short: When to use continuous and perfect forms, and how to choose between present perfect and simple past.

sections.heading: Continuous forms
sections.text:
Tense shows time, and aspect shows how an action unfolds. Continuous forms, also called progressive forms, show an action in progress. They use the verb “be” and a verb ending in -ing.
Example: Nomsa is reading now. (present continuous)
Example: Nomsa was reading when I called. (past continuous)

State verbs such as know, believe and own are not normally used in continuous forms.
Example (wrong): I am knowing the answer.
Example (right): I know the answer.

sections.heading: Perfect forms
sections.text:
Perfect forms link two times. They use “have” and the past participle. The present perfect links the past to now. Use the simple past when a finished time is stated. American English often uses the simple past in some places where British English uses the present perfect.
Example: I have lost my keys. (I still cannot find them.)
Example: I lost my keys yesterday. (finished time)
Example (wrong): I have seen him last week.
Example (right): I saw him last week.

The past perfect shows that one past action happened before another.
Example: The train had left when we arrived.

The future perfect shows an action finished before a future time.
Example: We will have finished by Friday.

sections.heading: Perfect continuous and sequence
sections.text:
Perfect continuous forms stress how long an action has lasted.
Example: She has been studying for two hours.

In a story, keep one main tense. Change it only when the time really changes. After a past verb in the main clause, the next verb usually moves into the past too.
Example: He said that he was tired.

keyPoints: Continuous forms use be with an -ing verb to show an action in progress.
Perfect forms use have with the past participle.
Do not use the present perfect with a finished time such as last week.
The past perfect shows the earlier of two past actions.
State verbs such as know are not normally continuous.

pcm.title: Continuous and perfect tenses
pcm.short: When to use continuous and perfect forms, and how to choose between present perfect and simple past.

sections.heading: Continuous forms
sections.text:
Tense dey show time, and aspect dey show how action dey happen. Continuous forms, wey dem also dey call progressive forms, dey show action wey still dey go on. Dem dey use the verb “be” and verb wey end with -ing. Pidgin “dey” dey do this work, like “Nomsa dey read now”, but Standard English need the two parts.
Example: Nomsa is reading now. (present continuous)
Example: Nomsa was reading when I called. (past continuous)

State verbs (verbs wey show state, no be action) like know, believe and own no dey normally enter continuous forms.
Example (wrong): I am knowing the answer.
Example (correct): I know the answer.

sections.heading: Perfect forms
sections.text:
Perfect forms dey link two times. Dem dey use “have” and the past participle (the verb form like “gone” or “written”). The present perfect dey link the past to now. Pidgin “don” dey close to am, like “I don lose my key”, but the two no be exactly the same. Use the simple past when you state time wey don finish. American English dey often use the simple past for some places where British English dey use the present perfect.
Example: I have lost my keys. (I never still see them.)
Example: I lost my keys yesterday. (time wey don finish)
Example (wrong): I have seen him last week.
Example (correct): I saw him last week.

The past perfect dey show say one past action happen before another one.
Example: The train had left when we arrived.

The future perfect dey show action wey go don finish before one future time.
Example: We will have finished by Friday.

sections.heading: Perfect continuous and sequence
sections.text:
Perfect continuous forms dey stress how long action don last.
Example: She has been studying for two hours.

For story, keep one main tense. Change am only when the time really change. After past verb for the main clause, the next verb dey usually move enter the past too.
Example: He said that he was tired.

keyPoints: Continuous forms dey use “be” with -ing verb to show action wey still dey go on.
Perfect forms dey use “have” with the past participle.
No use the present perfect with time wey don finish, like “last week”.
The past perfect dey show the one wey happen first for two past actions.
State verbs like “know” no dey normally enter continuous form.

fr.title: Les temps continus et parfaits
fr.short: Quand utiliser les formes continues et parfaites, et comment choisir entre le present perfect et le simple past.

sections.heading: Les formes continues
sections.text:
Le temps (tense) indique le moment, et l’aspect (aspect) indique comment une action se déroule. Les formes continues (continuous), aussi appelées formes progressives (progressive), montrent une action en cours. Elles utilisent le verbe “be” et un verbe terminé par -ing.
Exemple : Nomsa is reading now. (present continuous)
Exemple : Nomsa was reading when I called. (past continuous)

Les verbes d’état (state verbs) comme “know”, “believe” et “own” ne s’emploient normalement pas aux formes continues.
Exemple (faux) : I am knowing the answer.
Exemple (correct) : I know the answer.

sections.heading: Les formes parfaites
sections.text:
Les formes parfaites (perfect forms) relient deux moments. Elles utilisent “have” et le participe passé (past participle). Le present perfect relie le passé au présent. Utilise le simple past (prétérit) quand un moment terminé est indiqué. L’anglais américain utilise souvent le simple past à certains endroits où l’anglais britannique utilise le present perfect.
Exemple : I have lost my keys. (Je ne les trouve toujours pas.)
Exemple : I lost my keys yesterday. (moment terminé)
Exemple (faux) : I have seen him last week.
Exemple (correct) : I saw him last week.

Le past perfect (plus-que-parfait) montre qu’une action passée a eu lieu avant une autre.
Exemple : The train had left when we arrived.

Le future perfect (futur antérieur) montre une action terminée avant un moment futur.
Exemple : We will have finished by Friday.

sections.heading: Le perfect continuous et la concordance des temps
sections.text:
Les formes perfect continuous (parfaites continues) soulignent la durée d’une action.
Exemple : She has been studying for two hours.

Dans un récit, garde un seul temps principal. Change-le seulement quand le moment change vraiment. Après un verbe au passé dans la proposition principale, le verbe suivant passe généralement au passé lui aussi.
Exemple : He said that he was tired.

keyPoints: Les formes continues utilisent “be” avec un verbe en -ing pour montrer une action en cours.
Les formes parfaites utilisent “have” avec le participe passé.
N’utilise pas le present perfect avec un moment terminé comme “last week”.
Le past perfect montre la première de deux actions passées.
Les verbes d’état comme “know” ne s’emploient normalement pas à la forme continue.

ar.title: الأزمنة المستمرة والتامة
ar.short: متى تستخدم الصيغ المستمرة والتامة، وكيف تختار بين المضارع التام والماضي البسيط.

sections.heading: الصيغ المستمرة
sections.text:
الزمن ⁦(tense)⁩ يدل على الوقت، والمظهر ⁦(aspect)⁩ يدل على كيفية سير الفعل. والصيغ المستمرة ⁦(continuous forms)⁩، وتسمى أيضًا ⁦progressive forms⁩، تدل على فعل جارٍ. وهي تستخدم الفعل ⁦“be”⁩ وفعلًا ينتهي بـ ⁦-ing⁩.
مثال: ⁦Nomsa is reading now⁩. (المضارع المستمر، ⁦present continuous)⁩
مثال: ⁦Nomsa was reading when I called⁩. (الماضي المستمر، ⁦past continuous)⁩

أفعال الحالة ⁦(state verbs)⁩ مثل know وbelieve وown لا تُستخدم عادةً في الصيغ المستمرة.
مثال (خطأ): ⁦I am knowing the answer⁩.
مثال (صحيح): ⁦I know the answer⁩.

sections.heading: الصيغ التامة
sections.text:
تربط الصيغ التامة ⁦(perfect forms)⁩ بين وقتين. وهي تستخدم ⁦“have”⁩ واسم المفعول ⁦(past participle)⁩. والمضارع التام ⁦(present perfect)⁩ يربط الماضي بالحاضر. واستخدم الماضي البسيط ⁦(simple past)⁩ عندما يُذكر وقت منتهٍ. وكثيرًا ما تستخدم الإنجليزية الأمريكية الماضي البسيط في بعض المواضع التي تستخدم فيها الإنجليزية البريطانية المضارع التام.
مثال: ⁦I have lost my keys⁩. (ما زلت لا أجدها.)
مثال: ⁦I lost my keys yesterday⁩. (وقت منتهٍ)
مثال (خطأ): ⁦I have seen him last week⁩.
مثال (صحيح): ⁦I saw him last week⁩.

الماضي التام ⁦(past perfect)⁩ يدل على أن فعلًا ماضيًا حدث قبل فعل ماضٍ آخر.
مثال: ⁦The train had left when we arrived⁩.

المستقبل التام ⁦(future perfect)⁩ يدل على فعل ينتهي قبل وقت في المستقبل.
مثال: ⁦We will have finished by Friday⁩.

sections.heading: التام المستمر وتتابع الأزمنة
sections.text:
صيغ التام المستمر ⁦(perfect continuous forms)⁩ تؤكد المدة التي استغرقها الفعل.
مثال: ⁦She has been studying for two hours⁩.

في القصة، التزم بزمن رئيسي واحد. ولا تغيّره إلا عندما يتغير الوقت فعلًا. وبعد فعل ماضٍ في الجملة الرئيسية ⁦(main clause)⁩، ينتقل الفعل التالي عادةً إلى الماضي أيضًا.
مثال: ⁦He said that he was tired⁩.

keyPoints: تستخدم الصيغ المستمرة be مع فعل ينتهي بـ ⁦-ing⁩ للدلالة على فعل جارٍ.
تستخدم الصيغ التامة have مع اسم المفعول.
لا تستخدم المضارع التام مع وقت منتهٍ مثل ⁦last week⁩.
يدل الماضي التام على الأسبق من فعلين ماضيين.
أفعال الحالة مثل know لا تأتي عادةً في صيغة مستمرة.

sw.title: Njeo endelevu na timilifu
sw.short: Wakati wa kutumia maumbo endelevu na timilifu, na jinsi ya kuchagua kati ya present perfect na simple past.

sections.heading: Maumbo endelevu
sections.text:
Njeo (tense) huonyesha wakati, na aspect (hali ya kitendo) huonyesha jinsi kitendo kinavyoendelea. Maumbo endelevu (continuous forms), yanayoitwa pia progressive forms, huonyesha kitendo kinachoendelea. Hutumia kitenzi “be” na kitenzi kinachoishia kwa -ing.
Mfano: Nomsa is reading now. (present continuous, wakati uliopo endelevu)
Mfano: Nomsa was reading when I called. (past continuous, wakati uliopita endelevu)

Vitenzi vya hali (state verbs) kama “know”, “believe” na “own” kwa kawaida havitumiwi katika maumbo endelevu.
Mfano (si sahihi): I am knowing the answer.
Mfano (sahihi): I know the answer.

sections.heading: Maumbo timilifu
sections.text:
Maumbo timilifu (perfect forms) huunganisha nyakati mbili. Hutumia “have” na past participle (umbo linalotumiwa baada ya “have” na “be”). Present perfect (wakati uliopo timilifu) huunganisha wakati uliopita na sasa. Tumia simple past (wakati uliopita sahili) wakati uliokwisha unapotajwa. Kiingereza cha Marekani mara nyingi hutumia simple past katika baadhi ya sehemu ambapo Kiingereza cha Uingereza hutumia present perfect.
Mfano: I have lost my keys. (Bado siwezi kuzipata.)
Mfano: I lost my keys yesterday. (wakati uliokwisha)
Mfano (si sahihi): I have seen him last week.
Mfano (sahihi): I saw him last week.

Past perfect (wakati uliopita timilifu) huonyesha kwamba kitendo kimoja cha zamani kilitokea kabla ya kingine.
Mfano: The train had left when we arrived.

Future perfect (wakati ujao timilifu) huonyesha kitendo kitakachokuwa kimekwisha kabla ya wakati fulani ujao.
Mfano: We will have finished by Friday.

sections.heading: Timilifu endelevu na mfuatano
sections.text:
Maumbo ya perfect continuous (timilifu endelevu) husisitiza muda ambao kitendo kimedumu.
Mfano: She has been studying for two hours.

Katika hadithi, tumia njeo kuu moja. Ibadilishe tu wakati unapobadilika kweli. Baada ya kitenzi cha wakati uliopita katika kishazi kikuu (main clause), kitenzi kinachofuata kwa kawaida huhamia wakati uliopita pia.
Mfano: He said that he was tired.

keyPoints: Maumbo endelevu hutumia “be” na kitenzi chenye -ing kuonyesha kitendo kinachoendelea.
Maumbo timilifu hutumia “have” na past participle.
Usitumie present perfect pamoja na wakati uliokwisha kama “last week”.
Past perfect huonyesha kitendo cha mwanzo kati ya vitendo viwili vya zamani.
Vitenzi vya hali kama “know” kwa kawaida havitumiwi katika maumbo endelevu.

pt.title: Tempos contínuos e perfeitos
pt.short: Quando usar as formas contínuas e perfeitas, e como escolher entre o present perfect e o passado simples.

sections.heading: Formas contínuas
sections.text:
O tempo verbal mostra o tempo, e o aspeto (aspect) mostra como uma ação se desenrola. As formas contínuas (continuous), também chamadas progressivas (progressive), mostram uma ação em curso. Usam o verbo “be” e um verbo terminado em -ing.
Exemplo: Nomsa is reading now. (present continuous)
Exemplo: Nomsa was reading when I called. (past continuous)

Os verbos de estado (state verbs), como know, believe e own, não se usam normalmente nas formas contínuas.
Exemplo (errado): I am knowing the answer.
Exemplo (certo): I know the answer.

sections.heading: Formas perfeitas
sections.text:
As formas perfeitas (perfect) ligam dois momentos. Usam “have” e o particípio passado (past participle). O present perfect liga o passado ao presente. Usa o passado simples (simple past) quando é indicado um momento terminado. Em alguns casos em que o inglês britânico usa o present perfect, o inglês americano usa muitas vezes o passado simples.
Exemplo: I have lost my keys. (Continuo sem as encontrar.)
Exemplo: I lost my keys yesterday. (momento terminado)
Exemplo (errado): I have seen him last week.
Exemplo (certo): I saw him last week.

O past perfect mostra que uma ação passada aconteceu antes de outra.
Exemplo: The train had left when we arrived.

O future perfect mostra uma ação terminada antes de um momento futuro.
Exemplo: We will have finished by Friday.

sections.heading: Perfeito contínuo e sequência de tempos
sections.text:
As formas perfeitas contínuas (perfect continuous) realçam quanto tempo uma ação já durou.
Exemplo: She has been studying for two hours.

Numa história, mantém um tempo verbal principal. Muda-o apenas quando o tempo mudar realmente. Depois de um verbo no passado na oração principal, o verbo seguinte passa normalmente também para o passado.
Exemplo: He said that he was tired.

keyPoints: As formas contínuas usam “be” com um verbo em -ing para mostrar uma ação em curso.
As formas perfeitas usam “have” com o particípio passado.
Não uses o present perfect com um momento terminado, como “last week”.
O past perfect mostra a primeira de duas ações passadas.
Os verbos de estado, como “know”, não se usam normalmente nas formas contínuas.

es.title: Tiempos continuos y perfectos
es.short: Cuándo usar las formas continuas y perfectas, y cómo elegir entre el presente perfecto y el pasado simple.

sections.heading: Formas continuas
sections.text:
El tiempo verbal (tense) muestra cuándo ocurre algo, y el aspecto (aspect) muestra cómo se desarrolla una acción. Las formas continuas (continuous), también llamadas progresivas (progressive), muestran una acción en curso. Usan el verbo “be” y un verbo terminado en -ing.
Ejemplo: Nomsa is reading now. (presente continuo)
Ejemplo: Nomsa was reading when I called. (pasado continuo)

Los verbos de estado (state verbs) como “know”, “believe” y “own” no suelen usarse en formas continuas.
Ejemplo (incorrecto): I am knowing the answer.
Ejemplo (correcto): I know the answer.

sections.heading: Formas perfectas
sections.text:
Las formas perfectas (perfect) relacionan dos momentos. Usan “have” y el participio pasado. El presente perfecto (present perfect) relaciona el pasado con el ahora. Usa el pasado simple cuando se indica un tiempo terminado. El inglés americano suele usar el pasado simple en algunos casos en los que el inglés británico usa el presente perfecto.
Ejemplo: I have lost my keys. (Sigo sin encontrarlas.)
Ejemplo: I lost my keys yesterday. (tiempo terminado)
Ejemplo (incorrecto): I have seen him last week.
Ejemplo (correcto): I saw him last week.

El pasado perfecto (past perfect) muestra que una acción pasada ocurrió antes que otra.
Ejemplo: The train had left when we arrived.

El futuro perfecto (future perfect) muestra una acción terminada antes de un momento futuro.
Ejemplo: We will have finished by Friday.

sections.heading: Perfecto continuo y secuencia
sections.text:
Las formas de perfecto continuo (perfect continuous) destacan cuánto ha durado una acción.
Ejemplo: She has been studying for two hours.

En un relato, mantén un tiempo principal. Cámbialo solo cuando cambie de verdad el momento de la acción. Después de un verbo en pasado en la cláusula principal, el verbo siguiente suele pasar también al pasado.
Ejemplo: He said that he was tired.

keyPoints: Las formas continuas usan “be” con un verbo en -ing para mostrar una acción en curso.
Las formas perfectas usan “have” con el participio pasado.
No uses el presente perfecto con un tiempo terminado como “last week”.
El pasado perfecto muestra la primera de dos acciones pasadas.
Los verbos de estado como “know” no suelen ir en forma continua.

yo.title: Continuous àti perfect tense
yo.short: Ìgbà tí a ń lo continuous àti perfect, àti bí a ṣe ń yan láàárín present perfect àti simple past.

sections.heading: Continuous form
sections.text:
Tense ń fi àsìkò hàn, aspect sì ń fi bí iṣẹ́ kan ṣe ń lọ hàn. Continuous form, tí a tún ń pè ní progressive form, ń fi iṣẹ́ tó ń lọ lọ́wọ́ hàn. Wọ́n ń lo verb náà “be” àti verb tó parí pẹ̀lú -ing.
Àpẹẹrẹ: Nomsa is reading now. (present continuous)
Àpẹẹrẹ: Nomsa was reading when I called. (past continuous)

A kì í sábà lo state verb (verb tó ń fi ipò hàn) bíi know, believe àti own nínú continuous form.
Àpẹẹrẹ (àṣìṣe): I am knowing the answer.
Àpẹẹrẹ (ó tọ́): I know the answer.

sections.heading: Perfect form
sections.text:
Perfect form ń so àsìkò méjì pọ̀. Wọ́n ń lo “have” àti past participle. Present perfect ń so ohun tó ti kọjá pọ̀ mọ́ ìsinsìnyí. Lo simple past nígbà tí a bá sọ àsìkò tó ti parí. Ní àwọn ibì kan tí British English ti ń lo present perfect, American English sábà máa ń lo simple past.
Àpẹẹrẹ: I have lost my keys. (Mi ò tíì rí wọn síbẹ̀.)
Àpẹẹrẹ: I lost my keys yesterday. (àsìkò tó ti parí)
Àpẹẹrẹ (àṣìṣe): I have seen him last week.
Àpẹẹrẹ (ó tọ́): I saw him last week.

Past perfect ń fi hàn pé iṣẹ́ kan tó ti kọjá ṣẹlẹ̀ ṣáájú òmíràn.
Àpẹẹrẹ: The train had left when we arrived.

Future perfect ń fi iṣẹ́ tó máa parí ṣáájú àsìkò kan lọ́jọ́ iwájú hàn.
Àpẹẹrẹ: We will have finished by Friday.

sections.heading: Perfect continuous àti ìtẹ̀léra tense
sections.text:
Perfect continuous form ń tẹnu mọ́ bí iṣẹ́ kan ṣe pẹ́ tó.
Àpẹẹrẹ: She has been studying for two hours.

Nínú ìtàn, dúró lórí tense pàtàkì kan. Yí i padà kìkì nígbà tí àsìkò bá yí padà ní ti gidi. Lẹ́yìn past verb nínú main clause (clause pàtàkì), verb tó tẹ̀lé e sábà máa ń bọ́ sí past pẹ̀lú.
Àpẹẹrẹ: He said that he was tired.

keyPoints: Continuous form ń lo be pẹ̀lú verb -ing láti fi iṣẹ́ tó ń lọ lọ́wọ́ hàn.
Perfect form ń lo have pẹ̀lú past participle.
Má ṣe lo present perfect pẹ̀lú àsìkò tó ti parí bíi last week.
Past perfect ń fi èyí tó kọ́kọ́ ṣẹlẹ̀ hàn nínú iṣẹ́ méjì tó ti kọjá.
A kì í sábà lo state verb bíi know ní continuous.

ig.title: Continuous na perfect tenses
ig.short: Mgbe a ga-eji ụdị continuous na perfect, na otú e si ahọrọ n’etiti present perfect na simple past.

sections.heading: Ụdị continuous
sections.text:
Tense na-egosi oge, aspect na-egosikwa otú omume si aga. Ụdị continuous, nke a na-akpọkwa progressive, na-egosi omume na-aga n’ihu. Ha na-eji verb “be” na verb na-ejedebe na -ing. N’asụsụ Igbo, “na-” na-egosikwa omume na-aga n’ihu, dị ka “Nomsa na-agụ akwụkwọ”. Ọ na-egosikwa omume a na-emekarị, mana Bekee na-eji simple present maka nke ahụ.
Ihe atụ: Nomsa is reading now. (present continuous)
Ihe atụ: Nomsa was reading when I called. (past continuous)

A naghị ejikarị state verbs (verbs na-egosi ọnọdụ), dị ka know, believe na own, n’ụdị continuous.
Ihe atụ (nke na-ezighị ezi): I am knowing the answer.
Ihe atụ (nke ziri ezi): I know the answer.

sections.heading: Ụdị perfect
sections.text:
Ụdị perfect na-ejikọ oge abụọ. Ha na-eji “have” na past participle. Present perfect na-ejikọ oge gara aga na ugbu a. Jiri simple past mgbe e kwuru oge gwụrụla. Bekee America na-ejikarị simple past n’ebe ụfọdụ Bekee Britain na-eji present perfect.
Ihe atụ: I have lost my keys. (Achọtabeghị m ha.)
Ihe atụ: I lost my keys yesterday. (oge gwụrụla)
Ihe atụ (nke na-ezighị ezi): I have seen him last week.
Ihe atụ (nke ziri ezi): I saw him last week.

Past perfect na-egosi na otu omume gara aga mere tupu nke ọzọ.
Ihe atụ: The train had left when we arrived.

Future perfect na-egosi omume ga-agwụ tupu otu oge n’ọdịnihu.
Ihe atụ: We will have finished by Friday.

sections.heading: Perfect continuous na usoro tenses
sections.text:
Ụdị perfect continuous na-emesi ike otú omume si were ogologo oge.
Ihe atụ: She has been studying for two hours.

N’akụkọ, debe otu isi tense. Gbanwee ya naanị mgbe oge gbanwere n’ezie. Mgbe verb oge gara aga dị na main clause, verb na-esote ya na-agakarịkwa n’oge gara aga.
Ihe atụ: He said that he was tired.

keyPoints: Ụdị continuous na-eji “be” na verb -ing iji gosi omume na-aga n’ihu.
Ụdị perfect na-eji “have” na past participle.
Ejila present perfect na oge gwụrụla dị ka “last week”.
Past perfect na-egosi nke mbụ n’ime omume abụọ gara aga.
A naghị ejikarị state verbs dị ka “know” n’ụdị continuous.

ha.title: Continuous tenses da perfect tenses
ha.short: Lokacin amfani da siffofin continuous da perfect, da yadda ake zaɓa tsakanin present perfect da simple past.

sections.heading: Continuous forms
sections.text:
Tense yana nuna lokaci, aspect kuma yana nuna yadda aiki yake gudana. Continuous forms, waɗanda ake kira progressive forms, suna nuna aikin da ke gudana. Suna amfani da verb “be” da verb mai ƙarewa da -ing.
Misali: Nomsa is reading now. (present continuous)
Misali: Nomsa was reading when I called. (past continuous)

State verbs (aikatau masu nuna yanayi) kamar know, believe da own a al’ada ba a amfani da su a continuous forms.
Misali (ba daidai ba): I am knowing the answer.
Misali (daidai): I know the answer.

sections.heading: Perfect forms
sections.text:
Perfect forms suna haɗa lokuta biyu. Suna amfani da “have” da past participle. Present perfect yana haɗa lokacin da ya wuce da yanzu. Ka yi amfani da simple past idan an faɗi lokacin da ya ƙare. Turancin Amurka (American English) yakan yi amfani da simple past a wasu wuraren da Turancin Birtaniya (British English) yake amfani da present perfect.
Misali: I have lost my keys. (Har yanzu ban same su ba.)
Misali: I lost my keys yesterday. (lokacin da ya ƙare)
Misali (ba daidai ba): I have seen him last week.
Misali (daidai): I saw him last week.

Past perfect yana nuna cewa wani aiki na baya ya faru kafin wani.
Misali: The train had left when we arrived.

Future perfect yana nuna aikin da zai ƙare kafin wani lokaci na nan gaba.
Misali: We will have finished by Friday.

sections.heading: Perfect continuous da jerin tenses
sections.text:
Perfect continuous forms suna jaddada tsawon lokacin da aiki ya ɗauka.
Misali: She has been studying for two hours.

A cikin labari, ka tsaya a kan babban tense ɗaya. Ka canza shi ne kawai idan lokaci ya canza a zahiri. Bayan past verb a main clause (babban clause), verb na gaba galibi shi ma yana komawa past.
Misali: He said that he was tired.

keyPoints: Continuous forms suna amfani da be tare da verb mai -ing don nuna aikin da ke gudana.
Perfect forms suna amfani da have tare da past participle.
Kada ka yi amfani da present perfect tare da lokacin da ya ƙare, kamar last week.
Past perfect yana nuna aikin da ya fara faruwa a cikin ayyuka biyu na baya.
State verbs kamar know a al’ada ba sa zuwa a continuous.

en.title: Phrases, clauses and sentence types
en.short: Phrases and clauses, simple to complex sentences, and naming a clause and its function.

sections.heading: Phrases and clauses
sections.text:
A phrase is a group of words without its own subject and verb. A clause has both. A main clause can stand alone as a sentence. A subordinate clause cannot, because it depends on a main clause.
Example: in the morning (phrase)
Example: when the sun rose (subordinate clause)
Example: the birds sang (main clause)

sections.heading: Sentence structures
sections.text:
A simple sentence has one main clause. A compound sentence has two or more main clauses. A complex sentence has a main clause and at least one subordinate clause. A compound-complex sentence has at least two main clauses and at least one subordinate clause.
Example: Kemi sang. (simple)
Example: Kemi sang, and Oliver danced. (compound)
Example: Kemi sang while Oliver danced. (complex)
Example: Kemi sang and Oliver danced while the band played. (compound-complex)

sections.heading: Three kinds of subordinate clause
sections.text:
A noun clause does the work of a noun. It can be the subject or the object of a verb. An adjectival clause, also called a relative clause, describes a noun. An adverbial clause does the work of an adverb, showing ideas such as time, reason or condition.
Example: What she said surprised everyone. (noun clause, subject of “surprised”)
Example: The boy who won the prize is my cousin. (adjectival clause, describes “boy”)
Example: We left when the rain stopped. (adverbial clause of time, tells us more about “left”)

Some exams, including WASSCE, ask for the grammatical name and function of a group of words. Name the phrase or clause, then state its job in the sentence.

keyPoints: A clause has a subject and a verb, but a phrase does not.
A main clause can stand alone, but a subordinate clause cannot.
A complex sentence has a main clause and a subordinate clause.
Subordinate clauses can be noun, adjectival or adverbial.
When asked for name and function, give both.

pcm.title: Phrases, clauses and sentence types
pcm.short: Phrases and clauses, simple to complex sentences, and how to name clause and im function.

sections.heading: Phrases and clauses
sections.text:
Phrase na group of words wey no get im own subject and verb. Clause get both. Main clause fit stand alone as sentence. Subordinate clause no fit, because e depend on main clause.
Example: in the morning (phrase)
Example: when the sun rose (subordinate clause)
Example: the birds sang (main clause)

sections.heading: Sentence structures
sections.text:
Simple sentence get one main clause. Compound sentence get two or more main clauses. Complex sentence get main clause and at least one subordinate clause. Compound-complex sentence get at least two main clauses and at least one subordinate clause.
Example: Kemi sang. (simple)
Example: Kemi sang, and Oliver danced. (compound)
Example: Kemi sang while Oliver danced. (complex)
Example: Kemi sang and Oliver danced while the band played. (compound-complex)

sections.heading: Three kinds of subordinate clause
sections.text:
Noun clause dey do the work of noun. E fit be the subject or the object of verb. Adjectival clause, wey dem also dey call relative clause, dey describe noun. Adverbial clause dey do the work of adverb, and e dey show ideas like time, reason or condition.
Example: What she said surprised everyone. (noun clause, subject of “surprised”)
Example: The boy who won the prize is my cousin. (adjectival clause, e describe “boy”)
Example: We left when the rain stopped. (adverbial clause of time, e tell us more about “left”)

Some exams, including WASSCE, dey ask for the grammatical name and function of group of words. Name the phrase or clause, then state the work wey e dey do for the sentence.

keyPoints: Clause get subject and verb, but phrase no get.
Main clause fit stand alone, but subordinate clause no fit.
Complex sentence get main clause and subordinate clause.
Subordinate clauses fit be noun, adjectival or adverbial.
When dem ask for name and function, give both.

fr.title: Les groupes de mots, les propositions et les types de phrases
fr.short: Les groupes de mots et les propositions, de la phrase simple à la phrase complexe, et comment nommer une proposition et sa fonction.

sections.heading: Les groupes de mots et les propositions
sections.text:
Un groupe de mots (en anglais, “phrase”) n’a ni sujet ni verbe propres. Une proposition (clause) a les deux. Une proposition principale (main clause) peut former une phrase à elle seule. Une proposition subordonnée (subordinate clause) ne le peut pas, car elle dépend d’une proposition principale.
Exemple : in the morning (groupe de mots)
Exemple : when the sun rose (proposition subordonnée)
Exemple : the birds sang (proposition principale)

sections.heading: Les structures de phrases
sections.text:
Une phrase simple (simple sentence) a une seule proposition principale. Une phrase composée (compound sentence) a deux propositions principales ou plus. Une phrase complexe (complex sentence) a une proposition principale et au moins une proposition subordonnée. Une phrase composée-complexe (compound-complex sentence) a au moins deux propositions principales et au moins une proposition subordonnée.
Exemple : Kemi sang. (simple)
Exemple : Kemi sang, and Oliver danced. (composée)
Exemple : Kemi sang while Oliver danced. (complexe)
Exemple : Kemi sang and Oliver danced while the band played. (composée-complexe)

sections.heading: Trois sortes de propositions subordonnées
sections.text:
Une proposition nominale (noun clause) joue le rôle d’un nom. Elle peut être le sujet ou le complément d’objet d’un verbe. Une proposition adjectivale (adjectival clause), aussi appelée proposition relative (relative clause), décrit un nom. Une proposition adverbiale (adverbial clause) joue le rôle d’un adverbe et exprime des idées comme le temps, la cause ou la condition.
Exemple : What she said surprised everyone. (proposition nominale, sujet de “surprised”)
Exemple : The boy who won the prize is my cousin. (proposition adjectivale, décrit “boy”)
Exemple : We left when the rain stopped. (proposition adverbiale de temps, en dit plus sur “left”)

Certains examens, dont le WASSCE, demandent le nom grammatical et la fonction d’un groupe de mots. Nomme le groupe de mots ou la proposition, puis indique son rôle dans la phrase.

keyPoints: Une proposition a un sujet et un verbe, mais pas un groupe de mots.
Une proposition principale peut être seule, mais pas une proposition subordonnée.
Une phrase complexe a une proposition principale et une proposition subordonnée.
Les propositions subordonnées peuvent être nominales, adjectivales ou adverbiales.
Quand on te demande le nom et la fonction, donne les deux.

ar.title: العبارات والجمل الجزئية وأنواع الجمل
ar.short: العبارات والجمل الجزئية، والجمل من البسيطة إلى المركبة، وتسمية الجملة الجزئية ووظيفتها.

sections.heading: العبارات والجمل الجزئية
sections.text:
العبارة ⁦(phrase)⁩ مجموعة كلمات ليس لها مسند إليه ⁦(subject)⁩ وفعل خاصان بها. أما الجملة الجزئية ⁦(clause)⁩ ففيها الاثنان. والجملة الرئيسية ⁦(main clause)⁩ يمكن أن تقوم بذاتها جملةً مستقلة. أما الجملة التابعة ⁦(subordinate clause)⁩ فلا يمكنها ذلك، لأنها تعتمد على جملة رئيسية.
مثال: ⁦in the morning⁩ (عبارة)
مثال: ⁦when the sun rose⁩ (جملة تابعة)
مثال: ⁦the birds sang⁩ (جملة رئيسية)

sections.heading: تراكيب الجمل
sections.text:
الجملة البسيطة ⁦(simple sentence)⁩ فيها جملة رئيسية واحدة. والجملة المركبة ⁦(compound sentence)⁩ فيها جملتان رئيسيتان أو أكثر. والجملة المعقدة ⁦(complex sentence)⁩ فيها جملة رئيسية وجملة تابعة واحدة على الأقل. والجملة المركبة المعقدة ⁦(compound-complex sentence)⁩ فيها جملتان رئيسيتان على الأقل وجملة تابعة واحدة على الأقل.
مثال: ⁦Kemi sang⁩. (بسيطة)
مثال: ⁦Kemi sang, and Oliver danced⁩. (مركبة)
مثال: ⁦Kemi sang while Oliver danced⁩. (معقدة)
مثال: ⁦Kemi sang and Oliver danced while the band played⁩. (مركبة معقدة)

sections.heading: ثلاثة أنواع من الجمل التابعة
sections.text:
الجملة الاسمية ⁦(noun clause)⁩ تؤدي عمل الاسم. ويمكن أن تكون المسند إليه أو المفعول به لفعل. والجملة الوصفية ⁦(adjectival clause)⁩، وتسمى أيضًا الجملة الموصولة ⁦(relative clause)⁩، تصف اسمًا. والجملة الظرفية ⁦(adverbial clause)⁩ تؤدي عمل الظرف، فتعبّر عن أفكار مثل الزمان أو السبب أو الشرط.
مثال: ⁦What she said surprised everyone⁩. (جملة اسمية، مسند إليه للفعل ⁦“surprised”)⁩
مثال: ⁦The boy who won the prize is my cousin⁩. (جملة وصفية، تصف ⁦“boy”)⁩
مثال: ⁦We left when the rain stopped⁩. (جملة ظرفية للزمان، تخبرنا بالمزيد عن ⁦“left”)⁩

تطلب بعض الامتحانات، ومنها WASSCE، الاسم النحوي ⁦(grammatical name)⁩ والوظيفة ⁦(function)⁩ لمجموعة من الكلمات. سمِّ العبارة أو الجملة الجزئية، ثم اذكر وظيفتها في الجملة.

keyPoints: الجملة الجزئية فيها مسند إليه وفعل، أما العبارة فلا.
الجملة الرئيسية يمكن أن تقوم بذاتها، أما الجملة التابعة فلا.
الجملة المعقدة فيها جملة رئيسية وجملة تابعة.
قد تكون الجمل التابعة اسمية أو وصفية أو ظرفية.
عندما يُطلب الاسم والوظيفة، اذكرهما معًا.

sw.title: Virai, vishazi na aina za sentensi
sw.short: Virai na vishazi, sentensi kuanzia sahili hadi changamano, na kutaja kishazi pamoja na kazi yake.

sections.heading: Virai na vishazi
sections.text:
Kirai (phrase) ni kundi la maneno lisilo na kiima na kitenzi chake lenyewe. Kishazi (clause) kina vyote viwili. Kishazi kikuu (main clause) kinaweza kusimama peke yake kama sentensi. Kishazi tegemezi (subordinate clause) hakiwezi, kwa sababu kinategemea kishazi kikuu.
Mfano: in the morning (kirai)
Mfano: when the sun rose (kishazi tegemezi)
Mfano: the birds sang (kishazi kikuu)

sections.heading: Miundo ya sentensi
sections.text:
Sentensi sahili (simple sentence) ina kishazi kikuu kimoja. Sentensi ambatano (compound sentence) ina vishazi vikuu viwili au zaidi. Sentensi changamano (complex sentence) ina kishazi kikuu na angalau kishazi tegemezi kimoja. Sentensi ambatano changamano (compound-complex sentence) ina angalau vishazi vikuu viwili na angalau kishazi tegemezi kimoja.
Mfano: Kemi sang. (sahili)
Mfano: Kemi sang, and Oliver danced. (ambatano)
Mfano: Kemi sang while Oliver danced. (changamano)
Mfano: Kemi sang and Oliver danced while the band played. (ambatano changamano)

sections.heading: Aina tatu za kishazi tegemezi
sections.text:
Kishazi nomino (noun clause) hufanya kazi ya nomino. Kinaweza kuwa kiima au yambwa ya kitenzi. Kishazi kivumishi (adjectival clause), kinachoitwa pia relative clause, hueleza nomino. Kishazi kielezi (adverbial clause) hufanya kazi ya kielezi, kikionyesha mawazo kama wakati, sababu au sharti.
Mfano: What she said surprised everyone. (kishazi nomino, kiima cha “surprised”)
Mfano: The boy who won the prize is my cousin. (kishazi kivumishi, hueleza “boy”)
Mfano: We left when the rain stopped. (kishazi kielezi cha wakati, hutuambia zaidi kuhusu “left”)

Baadhi ya mitihani, ikiwemo WASSCE, huuliza jina la kisarufi na kazi (grammatical name and function) ya kundi la maneno. Taja kirai au kishazi, kisha eleza kazi yake katika sentensi.

keyPoints: Kishazi kina kiima na kitenzi, lakini kirai hakina.
Kishazi kikuu kinaweza kusimama peke yake, lakini kishazi tegemezi hakiwezi.
Sentensi changamano ina kishazi kikuu na kishazi tegemezi.
Vishazi tegemezi vinaweza kuwa nomino, vivumishi au vielezi.
Unapoulizwa jina na kazi, toa vyote viwili.

pt.title: Grupos de palavras, orações e tipos de frase
pt.short: Phrases e orações, das frases simples às complexas, e como dizer o nome e a função de uma oração.

sections.heading: Grupos de palavras e orações
sections.text:
Uma phrase (atenção: não significa “frase”) é um grupo de palavras sem sujeito e verbo próprios. Uma oração (clause) tem os dois. Uma oração principal (main clause) pode existir sozinha como frase. Uma oração subordinada (subordinate clause) não pode, porque depende de uma oração principal.
Exemplo: in the morning (phrase)
Exemplo: when the sun rose (oração subordinada)
Exemplo: the birds sang (oração principal)

sections.heading: Estruturas da frase
sections.text:
Uma frase simples (simple sentence) tem uma oração principal. Uma frase composta (compound sentence) tem duas ou mais orações principais. Uma frase complexa (complex sentence) tem uma oração principal e pelo menos uma oração subordinada. Uma frase composta-complexa (compound-complex sentence) tem pelo menos duas orações principais e pelo menos uma oração subordinada.
Exemplo: Kemi sang. (simples)
Exemplo: Kemi sang, and Oliver danced. (composta)
Exemplo: Kemi sang while Oliver danced. (complexa)
Exemplo: Kemi sang and Oliver danced while the band played. (composta-complexa)

sections.heading: Três tipos de oração subordinada
sections.text:
Uma oração substantiva (noun clause) faz o trabalho de um nome. Pode ser o sujeito ou o complemento direto de um verbo. Uma oração adjetiva (adjectival clause), também chamada oração relativa (relative clause), descreve um nome. Uma oração adverbial (adverbial clause) faz o trabalho de um advérbio, indicando ideias como tempo, causa ou condição.
Exemplo: What she said surprised everyone. (oração substantiva, sujeito de “surprised”)
Exemplo: The boy who won the prize is my cousin. (oração adjetiva, descreve “boy”)
Exemplo: We left when the rain stopped. (oração adverbial de tempo, diz-nos mais sobre “left”)

Alguns exames, incluindo o WASSCE, pedem o nome gramatical e a função de um grupo de palavras. Diz o nome da phrase ou da oração e depois indica a sua função na frase.

keyPoints: Uma oração tem sujeito e verbo, mas uma phrase não.
Uma oração principal pode existir sozinha, mas uma oração subordinada não.
Uma frase complexa tem uma oração principal e uma oração subordinada.
As orações subordinadas podem ser substantivas, adjetivas ou adverbiais.
Quando te pedirem o nome e a função, indica os dois.

es.title: Frases, cláusulas y tipos de oración
es.short: Frases y cláusulas, de la oración simple a la compleja, y cómo nombrar una cláusula y su función.

sections.heading: Frases y cláusulas
sections.text:
Una frase (phrase) es un grupo de palabras sin sujeto ni verbo propios. Una cláusula (clause) tiene ambos. Una cláusula principal (main clause) puede funcionar sola como oración. Una cláusula subordinada (subordinate clause) no puede, porque depende de una cláusula principal.
Ejemplo: in the morning (frase)
Ejemplo: when the sun rose (cláusula subordinada)
Ejemplo: the birds sang (cláusula principal)

sections.heading: Estructuras de la oración
sections.text:
Una oración simple (simple sentence) tiene una cláusula principal. Una oración compuesta (compound sentence) tiene dos o más cláusulas principales. Una oración compleja (complex sentence) tiene una cláusula principal y al menos una cláusula subordinada. Una oración compuesta-compleja (compound-complex sentence) tiene al menos dos cláusulas principales y al menos una cláusula subordinada.
Ejemplo: Kemi sang. (simple)
Ejemplo: Kemi sang, and Oliver danced. (compuesta)
Ejemplo: Kemi sang while Oliver danced. (compleja)
Ejemplo: Kemi sang and Oliver danced while the band played. (compuesta-compleja)

sections.heading: Tres tipos de cláusula subordinada
sections.text:
Una cláusula sustantiva (noun clause) hace el trabajo de un sustantivo. Puede ser el sujeto o el objeto de un verbo. Una cláusula adjetiva (adjectival clause), también llamada cláusula de relativo (relative clause), describe un sustantivo. Una cláusula adverbial (adverbial clause) hace el trabajo de un adverbio y expresa ideas como el tiempo, la causa o la condición.
Ejemplo: What she said surprised everyone. (cláusula sustantiva, sujeto de “surprised”)
Ejemplo: The boy who won the prize is my cousin. (cláusula adjetiva, describe “boy”)
Ejemplo: We left when the rain stopped. (cláusula adverbial de tiempo, nos dice más sobre “left”)

Algunos exámenes, incluido el WASSCE, piden el nombre gramatical y la función (grammatical name and function) de un grupo de palabras. Nombra la frase o la cláusula y luego indica su función en la oración.

keyPoints: Una cláusula tiene sujeto y verbo, pero una frase no.
Una cláusula principal puede funcionar sola, pero una subordinada no.
Una oración compleja tiene una cláusula principal y una cláusula subordinada.
Las cláusulas subordinadas pueden ser sustantivas, adjetivas o adverbiales.
Cuando te pidan el nombre y la función, da ambos.

yo.title: Phrase, clause àti àwọn irú gbólóhùn
yo.short: Phrase àti clause, láti simple sí complex sentence, àti sísọ orúkọ clause kan àti iṣẹ́ rẹ̀.

sections.heading: Phrase àti clause
sections.text:
Phrase jẹ́ àkójọ ọ̀rọ̀ tí kò ní subject (olùwà) àti verb (ọ̀rọ̀ ìṣe) tirẹ̀. Clause ní àwọn méjèèjì. Main clause lè dá dúró gẹ́gẹ́ bí gbólóhùn. Subordinate clause kò lè dá dúró, nítorí pé ó gbára lé main clause.
Àpẹẹrẹ: in the morning (phrase)
Àpẹẹrẹ: when the sun rose (subordinate clause)
Àpẹẹrẹ: the birds sang (main clause)

sections.heading: Àwọn ìgbékalẹ̀ gbólóhùn
sections.text:
Simple sentence ní main clause kan. Compound sentence ní main clause méjì tàbí jù bẹ́ẹ̀ lọ. Complex sentence ní main clause kan àti subordinate clause kan, ó kéré tán. Compound-complex sentence ní main clause méjì, ó kéré tán, àti subordinate clause kan, ó kéré tán.
Àpẹẹrẹ: Kemi sang. (simple)
Àpẹẹrẹ: Kemi sang, and Oliver danced. (compound)
Àpẹẹrẹ: Kemi sang while Oliver danced. (complex)
Àpẹẹrẹ: Kemi sang and Oliver danced while the band played. (compound-complex)

sections.heading: Irú subordinate clause mẹ́ta
sections.text:
Noun clause ń ṣe iṣẹ́ noun. Ó lè jẹ́ subject tàbí object (àbọ̀) verb kan. Adjectival clause, tí a tún ń pè ní relative clause, ń ṣàpèjúwe noun. Adverbial clause ń ṣe iṣẹ́ adverb, ó sì ń fi àwọn èrò bíi àkókò, ìdí tàbí condition (ohun tó gbọ́dọ̀ wà kí nǹkan mìíràn tó ṣẹlẹ̀) hàn.
Àpẹẹrẹ: What she said surprised everyone. (noun clause, subject ti “surprised”)
Àpẹẹrẹ: The boy who won the prize is my cousin. (adjectival clause, ó ń ṣàpèjúwe “boy”)
Àpẹẹrẹ: We left when the rain stopped. (adverbial clause ti àkókò, ó ń sọ ohun púpọ̀ sí i fún wa nípa “left”)

Àwọn ìdánwò kan, títí kan WASSCE, máa ń béèrè grammatical name (orúkọ gírámà) àti function (iṣẹ́) àkójọ ọ̀rọ̀ kan. Sọ orúkọ phrase tàbí clause náà, lẹ́yìn náà sọ iṣẹ́ rẹ̀ nínú gbólóhùn náà.

keyPoints: Clause ní subject àti verb, ṣùgbọ́n phrase kò ní wọn.
Main clause lè dá dúró, ṣùgbọ́n subordinate clause kò lè dá dúró.
Complex sentence ní main clause àti subordinate clause.
Subordinate clause lè jẹ́ noun, adjectival tàbí adverbial.
Nígbà tí a bá béèrè name àti function, sọ àwọn méjèèjì.

ig.title: Phrases, clauses na ụdị ahịrịokwu
ig.short: Phrases na clauses, ahịrịokwu simple ruo complex, na ịkpọ aha clause na ọrụ ya.

sections.heading: Phrases na clauses
sections.text:
Phrase bụ ìgwè okwu na-enweghị subject na verb nke ya. Clause nwere ha abụọ. Main clause nwere ike iguzo naanị ya dị ka ahịrịokwu. Subordinate clause enweghị ike, n’ihi na ọ dabere na main clause.
Ihe atụ: in the morning (phrase)
Ihe atụ: when the sun rose (subordinate clause)
Ihe atụ: the birds sang (main clause)

sections.heading: Otú e si ahazi ahịrịokwu
sections.text:
Simple sentence nwere otu main clause. Compound sentence nwere main clauses abụọ ma ọ bụ karịa. Complex sentence nwere main clause na opekata mpe otu subordinate clause. Compound-complex sentence nwere opekata mpe main clauses abụọ na opekata mpe otu subordinate clause.
Ihe atụ: Kemi sang. (simple)
Ihe atụ: Kemi sang, and Oliver danced. (compound)
Ihe atụ: Kemi sang while Oliver danced. (complex)
Ihe atụ: Kemi sang and Oliver danced while the band played. (compound-complex)

sections.heading: Ụdị subordinate clause atọ
sections.text:
Noun clause na-arụ ọrụ noun. O nwere ike ịbụ subject ma ọ bụ object nke verb. Adjectival clause, nke a na-akpọkwa relative clause, na-akọwa noun. Adverbial clause na-arụ ọrụ adverb, na-egosi echiche dị ka oge, ihe kpatara ihe ma ọ bụ ọnọdụ.
Ihe atụ: What she said surprised everyone. (noun clause, subject nke “surprised”)
Ihe atụ: The boy who won the prize is my cousin. (adjectival clause, na-akọwa “boy”)
Ihe atụ: We left when the rain stopped. (adverbial clause nke oge, na-agwakwu anyị ihe banyere “left”)

Ụfọdụ ule, gụnyere WASSCE, na-ajụ grammatical name and function (aha na ọrụ) nke ìgwè okwu. Kpọọ aha phrase ma ọ bụ clause ahụ, wee kwuo ọrụ ya n’ahịrịokwu ahụ.

keyPoints: Clause nwere subject na verb, mana phrase enweghị ha.
Main clause nwere ike iguzo naanị ya, mana subordinate clause enweghị ike.
Complex sentence nwere main clause na subordinate clause.
Subordinate clauses nwere ike ịbụ noun, adjectival ma ọ bụ adverbial.
Mgbe a jụrụ aha na ọrụ, nye ha abụọ.

ha.title: Phrases, clauses da nau’o’in jimla
ha.short: Phrases da clauses, jimloli daga simple zuwa complex, da faɗin sunan clause da aikinsa.

sections.heading: Phrases da clauses
sections.text:
Phrase rukunin kalmomi ne da ba shi da subject da verb nasa. Clause yana da duka biyun. Main clause yana iya tsayawa shi kaɗai a matsayin jimla. Subordinate clause ba zai iya ba, domin ya dogara ne da main clause.
Misali: in the morning (phrase)
Misali: when the sun rose (subordinate clause)
Misali: the birds sang (main clause)

sections.heading: Tsarin jimloli
sections.text:
Simple sentence yana da main clause ɗaya. Compound sentence yana da main clauses biyu ko fiye. Complex sentence yana da main clause da aƙalla subordinate clause ɗaya. Compound-complex sentence yana da aƙalla main clauses biyu da aƙalla subordinate clause ɗaya.
Misali: Kemi sang. (simple)
Misali: Kemi sang, and Oliver danced. (compound)
Misali: Kemi sang while Oliver danced. (complex)
Misali: Kemi sang and Oliver danced while the band played. (compound-complex)

sections.heading: Nau’o’i uku na subordinate clause
sections.text:
Noun clause yana yin aikin noun. Yana iya zama subject ko object na verb. Adjectival clause, wanda ake kira relative clause, yana siffanta noun. Adverbial clause yana yin aikin adverb, yana nuna abubuwa kamar lokaci, dalili ko sharaɗi.
Misali: What she said surprised everyone. (noun clause, subject na “surprised”)
Misali: The boy who won the prize is my cousin. (adjectival clause, yana siffanta “boy”)
Misali: We left when the rain stopped. (adverbial clause na lokaci, yana ƙara mana bayani game da “left”)

Wasu jarrabawoyi, har da WASSCE, suna tambayar grammatical name and function (suna da aikin rukunin kalmomi a nahawu). Ka faɗi sunan phrase ko clause ɗin, sannan ka bayyana aikinsa a cikin jimlar.

keyPoints: Clause yana da subject da verb, amma phrase ba shi da su.
Main clause yana iya tsayawa shi kaɗai, amma subordinate clause ba zai iya ba.
Complex sentence yana da main clause da subordinate clause.
Subordinate clauses suna iya zama noun, adjectival ko adverbial.
Idan aka tambayi name and function, ka ba da duka biyun.

en.title: Active and passive voice
en.short: How to change a sentence between active and passive in any tense, and when to use each.

sections.heading: What voice means
sections.text:
In the active voice, the subject does the action. In the passive voice, the subject receives the action. The meaning stays the same, but the focus changes.

To form the passive, follow three steps. Move the object to the subject position. Use the correct tense of “be” and the past participle of the main verb. Add “by” and the doer only if the doer matters.
Example (active): The farmer harvests the maize.
Example (passive): The maize is harvested by the farmer.

sections.heading: The passive in different tenses
sections.text:
Only the form of “be” changes with the tense. The main verb stays as a past participle.
Example: The maize is harvested. (simple present)
Example: The maize is being harvested. (present continuous)
Example: The maize was harvested. (simple past)
Example: The maize has been harvested. (present perfect)
Example: The maize will be harvested. (future)
Example: The maize must be harvested. (with a modal verb)

Only verbs with an object can normally become passive. A verb such as “arrive” has no object, so it has no passive form.

sections.heading: When to use each voice
sections.text:
The active voice is usually clearer and more direct, so it suits most writing. The passive is useful in three situations. Use it when the doer is unknown, when the doer is not important, or when the action matters more than the doer. Scientific reports and news items use it often.
Example: My phone was stolen.
Example: The solution was heated for five minutes.

keyPoints: In the passive, the subject receives the action.
The passive uses a form of be with a past participle.
The object of the active sentence becomes the passive subject.
Verbs with no object normally have no passive form.
Use the passive when the doer is unknown or unimportant.

pcm.title: Active and passive voice
pcm.short: How to change sentence between active and passive for any tense, and when to use each one.

sections.heading: Wetin voice mean
sections.text:
For the active voice, the subject dey do the action. For the passive voice, the subject dey receive the action. The meaning remain the same, but the focus dey change. Pidgin dey usually talk this kind idea with “dem”, like “Dem harvest the maize”. Standard English get im own special passive form, and exams dey test am.

To form the passive, follow three steps. Move the object go the subject position. Use the correct tense of “be” and the past participle (the verb form like “gone” or “written”) of the main verb. Add “by” and the person wey do am only if that person matter.
Example (active): The farmer harvests the maize.
Example (passive): The maize is harvested by the farmer.

sections.heading: The passive for different tenses
sections.text:
Na only the form of “be” dey change with the tense. The main verb go remain as past participle.
Example: The maize is harvested. (simple present)
Example: The maize is being harvested. (present continuous)
Example: The maize was harvested. (simple past)
Example: The maize has been harvested. (present perfect)
Example: The maize will be harvested. (future)
Example: The maize must be harvested. (with modal verb)

Na only verbs wey get object fit normally become passive. Verb like “arrive” no get object, so e no get passive form.

sections.heading: When to use each voice
sections.text:
The active voice dey usually clear and direct pass, so e fit most writing. The passive dey useful for three situations. Use am when nobody know who do the action, when the person wey do am no important, or when the action matter pass the person wey do am. Scientific reports and news items dey use am often.
Example: My phone was stolen.
Example: The solution was heated for five minutes.

keyPoints: For the passive, the subject dey receive the action.
The passive dey use one form of “be” with past participle.
The object of the active sentence dey become the passive subject.
Verbs wey no get object no dey normally get passive form.
Use the passive when nobody know who do am or the person no important.

fr.title: La voix active et la voix passive
fr.short: Comment passer une phrase de l’actif au passif à n’importe quel temps, et quand utiliser chaque voix.

sections.heading: Ce que signifie la voix
sections.text:
À la voix active (active voice), le sujet fait l’action. À la voix passive (passive voice), le sujet reçoit l’action. Le sens reste le même, mais l’attention se déplace.

Pour former le passif, suis trois étapes. Place le complément d’objet à la position du sujet. Utilise le bon temps de “be” et le participe passé (past participle) du verbe principal. Ajoute “by” et l’auteur de l’action seulement si cet auteur compte.
Exemple (actif) : The farmer harvests the maize.
Exemple (passif) : The maize is harvested by the farmer.

sections.heading: Le passif aux différents temps
sections.text:
Seule la forme de “be” change avec le temps. Le verbe principal reste au participe passé.
Exemple : The maize is harvested. (simple present)
Exemple : The maize is being harvested. (present continuous)
Exemple : The maize was harvested. (simple past)
Exemple : The maize has been harvested. (present perfect)
Exemple : The maize will be harvested. (futur)
Exemple : The maize must be harvested. (avec un verbe modal)

Normalement, seuls les verbes qui ont un complément d’objet peuvent passer au passif. Un verbe comme “arrive” n’a pas de complément d’objet, donc il n’a pas de forme passive.

sections.heading: Quand utiliser chaque voix
sections.text:
La voix active est généralement plus claire et plus directe, donc elle convient à la plupart des écrits. Le passif est utile dans trois situations. Utilise-le quand l’auteur de l’action est inconnu, quand il n’est pas important, ou quand l’action compte plus que son auteur. Les rapports scientifiques et les articles d’actualité l’utilisent souvent.
Exemple : My phone was stolen.
Exemple : The solution was heated for five minutes.

keyPoints: Au passif, le sujet reçoit l’action.
Le passif utilise une forme de “be” avec un participe passé.
Le complément d’objet de la phrase active devient le sujet de la phrase passive.
Normalement, les verbes sans complément d’objet n’ont pas de forme passive.
Utilise le passif quand l’auteur de l’action est inconnu ou sans importance.

ar.title: المبني للمعلوم والمبني للمجهول
ar.short: كيف تحوّل الجملة بين المبني للمعلوم والمبني للمجهول في أي زمن، ومتى تستخدم كلًا منهما.

sections.heading: معنى صيغة البناء
sections.text:
في المبني للمعلوم ⁦(active voice)⁩، يقوم المسند إليه ⁦(subject)⁩ بالفعل. وفي المبني للمجهول ⁦(passive voice)⁩، يقع الفعل على المسند إليه. ويبقى المعنى نفسه، لكن التركيز يتغير.

لتكوين المبني للمجهول، اتبع ثلاث خطوات. انقل المفعول به ⁦(object)⁩ إلى موضع المسند إليه. استخدم الزمن الصحيح من ⁦“be”⁩ واسم المفعول ⁦(past participle)⁩ من الفعل الرئيسي. أضف ⁦“by”⁩ والقائم بالفعل فقط إذا كان القائم بالفعل مهمًا.
مثال (مبني للمعلوم): ⁦The farmer harvests the maize⁩.
مثال (مبني للمجهول): ⁦The maize is harvested by the farmer⁩.

sections.heading: المبني للمجهول في الأزمنة المختلفة
sections.text:
صيغة ⁦“be”⁩ وحدها هي التي تتغير مع الزمن. ويبقى الفعل الرئيسي اسم مفعول.
مثال: ⁦The maize is harvested⁩. (المضارع البسيط، ⁦simple present)⁩
مثال: ⁦The maize is being harvested⁩. (المضارع المستمر، ⁦present continuous)⁩
مثال: ⁦The maize was harvested⁩. (الماضي البسيط، ⁦simple past)⁩
مثال: ⁦The maize has been harvested⁩. (المضارع التام، ⁦present perfect)⁩
مثال: ⁦The maize will be harvested⁩. (المستقبل، ⁦future)⁩
مثال: ⁦The maize must be harvested⁩. (مع فعل مساعد ناقص، ⁦modal verb)⁩

الأفعال التي لها مفعول به هي وحدها التي يمكن عادةً بناؤها للمجهول. فالفعل ⁦“arrive”⁩ مثلًا ليس له مفعول به، ولذلك ليس له صيغة مبني للمجهول.

sections.heading: متى تستخدم كل صيغة
sections.text:
المبني للمعلوم أوضح وأكثر مباشرة في العادة، ولذلك يناسب معظم الكتابة. والمبني للمجهول مفيد في ثلاث حالات. استخدمه عندما يكون القائم بالفعل مجهولًا، أو عندما لا يكون القائم بالفعل مهمًا، أو عندما يكون الفعل أهم من القائم به. وكثيرًا ما تستخدمه التقارير العلمية والأخبار.
مثال: ⁦My phone was stolen⁩.
مثال: ⁦The solution was heated for five minutes⁩.

keyPoints: في المبني للمجهول، يقع الفعل على المسند إليه.
يستخدم المبني للمجهول صيغة من be مع اسم المفعول.
المفعول به في جملة المبني للمعلوم يصبح المسند إليه في جملة المبني للمجهول.
الأفعال التي ليس لها مفعول به ليس لها عادةً صيغة مبني للمجهول.
استخدم المبني للمجهول عندما يكون القائم بالفعل مجهولًا أو غير مهم.

sw.title: Kauli ya kutenda na kauli ya kutendwa
sw.short: Jinsi ya kubadilisha sentensi kati ya kauli ya kutenda na ya kutendwa katika njeo yoyote, na wakati wa kutumia kila moja.

sections.heading: Maana ya kauli
sections.text:
Katika kauli ya kutenda (active voice), kiima hufanya kitendo. Katika kauli ya kutendwa (passive voice), kiima hupokea kitendo. Maana hubaki ile ile, lakini mkazo hubadilika.

Ili kuunda kauli ya kutendwa, fuata hatua tatu. Hamisha yambwa (object) hadi nafasi ya kiima (subject). Tumia njeo sahihi ya “be” na past participle (umbo linalotumiwa baada ya “have” na “be”) ya kitenzi kikuu. Ongeza “by” na mtendaji ikiwa tu mtendaji ni muhimu.
Mfano (kauli ya kutenda): The farmer harvests the maize.
Mfano (kauli ya kutendwa): The maize is harvested by the farmer.

sections.heading: Kauli ya kutendwa katika njeo tofauti
sections.text:
Umbo la “be” pekee ndilo hubadilika kulingana na njeo. Kitenzi kikuu hubaki katika past participle.
Mfano: The maize is harvested. (simple present, wakati uliopo sahili)
Mfano: The maize is being harvested. (present continuous, wakati uliopo endelevu)
Mfano: The maize was harvested. (simple past, wakati uliopita sahili)
Mfano: The maize has been harvested. (present perfect, wakati uliopo timilifu)
Mfano: The maize will be harvested. (future, wakati ujao)
Mfano: The maize must be harvested. (pamoja na modal verb, kitenzi kisaidizi cha uwezo au wajibu)

Vitenzi vyenye yambwa pekee ndivyo kwa kawaida vinaweza kuwa katika kauli ya kutendwa. Kitenzi kama “arrive” hakina yambwa, kwa hiyo hakina umbo la kauli ya kutendwa.

sections.heading: Wakati wa kutumia kila kauli
sections.text:
Kauli ya kutenda kwa kawaida ni wazi zaidi na ya moja kwa moja, kwa hiyo inafaa maandishi mengi. Kauli ya kutendwa ni muhimu katika hali tatu. Itumie wakati mtendaji hajulikani, wakati mtendaji si muhimu, au wakati kitendo ni muhimu kuliko mtendaji. Ripoti za kisayansi na habari huitumia mara nyingi.
Mfano: My phone was stolen.
Mfano: The solution was heated for five minutes.

keyPoints: Katika kauli ya kutendwa, kiima hupokea kitendo.
Kauli ya kutendwa hutumia umbo la “be” pamoja na past participle.
Yambwa ya sentensi ya kauli ya kutenda huwa kiima cha kauli ya kutendwa.
Vitenzi visivyo na yambwa kwa kawaida havina umbo la kauli ya kutendwa.
Tumia kauli ya kutendwa wakati mtendaji hajulikani au si muhimu.

pt.title: Voz ativa e voz passiva
pt.short: Como passar uma frase da ativa para a passiva, e vice-versa, em qualquer tempo, e quando usar cada uma.

sections.heading: O que significa voz
sections.text:
Na voz ativa (active voice), o sujeito pratica a ação. Na voz passiva (passive voice), o sujeito recebe a ação. O sentido mantém-se, mas o foco muda.

Para formar a passiva, segue três passos. Passa o complemento direto (object) para a posição de sujeito. Usa o tempo correto de “be” e o particípio passado (past participle) do verbo principal. Acrescenta “by” e quem pratica a ação apenas se isso for importante.
Exemplo (ativa): The farmer harvests the maize.
Exemplo (passiva): The maize is harvested by the farmer.

sections.heading: A passiva em diferentes tempos
sections.text:
Só a forma de “be” muda com o tempo verbal. O verbo principal mantém-se no particípio passado.
Exemplo: The maize is harvested. (simple present)
Exemplo: The maize is being harvested. (present continuous)
Exemplo: The maize was harvested. (simple past)
Exemplo: The maize has been harvested. (present perfect)
Exemplo: The maize will be harvested. (futuro)
Exemplo: The maize must be harvested. (com um verbo modal)

Normalmente, só os verbos com complemento direto podem passar para a passiva. Um verbo como “arrive” não tem complemento direto, por isso não tem forma passiva.

sections.heading: Quando usar cada voz
sections.text:
A voz ativa é normalmente mais clara e mais direta, por isso adequa-se à maior parte da escrita. A passiva é útil em três situações. Usa-a quando não se sabe quem praticou a ação, quando quem a praticou não é importante, ou quando a ação importa mais do que quem a praticou. Os relatórios científicos e as notícias usam-na muitas vezes.
Exemplo: My phone was stolen.
Exemplo: The solution was heated for five minutes.

keyPoints: Na passiva, o sujeito recebe a ação.
A passiva usa uma forma de “be” com um particípio passado.
O complemento direto da frase ativa passa a sujeito da passiva.
Os verbos sem complemento direto normalmente não têm forma passiva.
Usa a passiva quando quem pratica a ação é desconhecido ou não é importante.

es.title: Voz activa y voz pasiva
es.short: Cómo pasar una oración de activa a pasiva y viceversa en cualquier tiempo, y cuándo usar cada voz.

sections.heading: Qué significa la voz
sections.text:
En la voz activa (active voice), el sujeto hace la acción. En la voz pasiva (passive voice), el sujeto recibe la acción. El significado sigue siendo el mismo, pero cambia el enfoque.

Para formar la pasiva, sigue tres pasos. Mueve el objeto a la posición del sujeto. Usa el tiempo correcto de “be” y el participio pasado del verbo principal. Añade “by” y quien hace la acción solo si esa persona o cosa importa.
Ejemplo (activa): The farmer harvests the maize.
Ejemplo (pasiva): The maize is harvested by the farmer.

sections.heading: La pasiva en distintos tiempos
sections.text:
Solo la forma de “be” cambia con el tiempo verbal. El verbo principal sigue siendo un participio pasado.
Ejemplo: The maize is harvested. (presente simple)
Ejemplo: The maize is being harvested. (presente continuo)
Ejemplo: The maize was harvested. (pasado simple)
Ejemplo: The maize has been harvested. (presente perfecto)
Ejemplo: The maize will be harvested. (futuro)
Ejemplo: The maize must be harvested. (con un verbo modal)

Normalmente, solo los verbos con objeto pueden pasar a pasiva. Un verbo como “arrive” no tiene objeto, así que no tiene forma pasiva.

sections.heading: Cuándo usar cada voz
sections.text:
La voz activa suele ser más clara y directa, así que conviene para la mayoría de los textos. La pasiva es útil en tres situaciones. Úsala cuando no se sabe quién hace la acción, cuando eso no es importante o cuando la acción importa más que quien la hace. Los informes científicos y las noticias la usan a menudo.
Ejemplo: My phone was stolen.
Ejemplo: The solution was heated for five minutes.

keyPoints: En la pasiva, el sujeto recibe la acción.
La pasiva usa una forma de “be” con un participio pasado.
El objeto de la oración activa pasa a ser el sujeto de la pasiva.
Los verbos sin objeto normalmente no tienen forma pasiva.
Usa la pasiva cuando no se sabe quién hace la acción o eso no es importante.

yo.title: Active àti passive voice
yo.short: Bí a ṣe ń yí gbólóhùn padà láàárín active àti passive ní gbogbo tense, àti ìgbà tí a ń lo ọ̀kọ̀ọ̀kan.

sections.heading: Ohun tí voice túmọ̀ sí
sections.text:
Nínú active voice, subject (olùwà) ló ń ṣe iṣẹ́ náà. Nínú passive voice, subject ni a ń ṣe iṣẹ́ náà sí. Ìtumọ̀ kò yí padà, ṣùgbọ́n ibi tí a tẹnu mọ́ ló ń yí padà.

Láti ṣe passive, tẹ̀lé ìgbésẹ̀ mẹ́ta. Gbé object (àbọ̀) lọ sí ipò subject. Lo tense tó tọ́ fún “be” àti past participle verb pàtàkì náà. Fi “by” àti ẹni tó ṣe iṣẹ́ náà kún un kìkì tí ẹni náà bá ṣe pàtàkì.
Àpẹẹrẹ (active): The farmer harvests the maize.
Àpẹẹrẹ (passive): The maize is harvested by the farmer.

sections.heading: Passive ní àwọn tense ọ̀tọ̀ọ̀tọ̀
sections.text:
Ìrísí “be” nìkan ló ń yí padà pẹ̀lú tense. Verb pàtàkì náà máa ń dúró gẹ́gẹ́ bí past participle.
Àpẹẹrẹ: The maize is harvested. (simple present)
Àpẹẹrẹ: The maize is being harvested. (present continuous)
Àpẹẹrẹ: The maize was harvested. (simple past)
Àpẹẹrẹ: The maize has been harvested. (present perfect)
Àpẹẹrẹ: The maize will be harvested. (future)
Àpẹẹrẹ: The maize must be harvested. (pẹ̀lú modal verb)

Verb tó ní object nìkan ló sábà máa ń lè di passive. Verb bíi “arrive” kò ní object, nítorí náà kò ní ìrísí passive.

sections.heading: Ìgbà tí a ń lo ọ̀kọ̀ọ̀kan
sections.text:
Active voice sábà máa ń ṣe kedere ju passive lọ, ó sì máa ń lọ tààrà jù bẹ́ẹ̀ lọ, nítorí náà ó bá èyí tó pọ̀ jù lọ nínú ìkọ̀wé mu. Passive wúlò ní ipò mẹ́ta. Lò ó nígbà tí a kò mọ ẹni tó ṣe iṣẹ́ náà, nígbà tí ẹni náà kò ṣe pàtàkì, tàbí nígbà tí iṣẹ́ náà ṣe pàtàkì ju ẹni tó ṣe é lọ. Àwọn ìjábọ̀ sáyẹ́ǹsì àti ìròyìn máa ń lò ó léraléra.
Àpẹẹrẹ: My phone was stolen.
Àpẹẹrẹ: The solution was heated for five minutes.

keyPoints: Nínú passive, subject ni a ń ṣe iṣẹ́ náà sí.
Passive ń lo ìrísí be kan pẹ̀lú past participle.
Object gbólóhùn active ló ń di subject passive.
Verb tí kò ní object kì í sábà ní ìrísí passive.
Lo passive nígbà tí a kò mọ ẹni tó ṣe iṣẹ́ náà tàbí tí kò ṣe pàtàkì.

ig.title: Active voice na passive voice
ig.short: Otú e si agbanwe ahịrịokwu n’etiti active na passive na tense ọ bụla, na mgbe a ga-eji nke ọ bụla.

sections.heading: Ihe voice pụtara
sections.text:
Na active voice, subject na-eme omume ahụ. Na passive voice, omume ahụ na-emetụta subject. Ihe ahịrịokwu pụtara na-anọgide otu, mana ihe a na-elekwasị anya na ya na-agbanwe.

Iji mee passive, soro usoro atọ. Bugharịa object gaa n’ọnọdụ subject. Jiri tense ziri ezi nke “be” na past participle nke isi verb. Tinye “by” na onye mere ihe ahụ naanị ma ọ bụrụ na onye ahụ dị mkpa.
Ihe atụ (active): The farmer harvests the maize.
Ihe atụ (passive): The maize is harvested by the farmer.

sections.heading: Passive na tenses dị iche iche
sections.text:
Naanị ụdị “be” na-agbanwe na tense. Isi verb na-anọgide dị ka past participle.
Ihe atụ: The maize is harvested. (simple present)
Ihe atụ: The maize is being harvested. (present continuous)
Ihe atụ: The maize was harvested. (simple past)
Ihe atụ: The maize has been harvested. (present perfect)
Ihe atụ: The maize will be harvested. (future)
Ihe atụ: The maize must be harvested. (na modal verb)

Naanị verbs nwere object nwere ike ịghọ passive n’ọnọdụ nkịtị. Verb dị ka “arrive” enweghị object, ya mere o nweghị ụdị passive.

sections.heading: Mgbe a ga-eji voice nke ọ bụla
sections.text:
Active voice na-edokarị anya karịa ma na-aga ozugbo n’ihe a na-ekwu, ya mere ọ dabara ihe ka ọtụtụ n’ime ide ihe. Passive bara uru n’ọnọdụ atọ. Jiri ya mgbe a na-amaghị onye mere ihe ahụ, mgbe onye mere ya na-adịghị mkpa, ma ọ bụ mgbe omume ahụ dị mkpa karịa onye mere ya. Reports sayensị na akụkọ ozi na-ejikarị ya.
Ihe atụ: My phone was stolen.
Ihe atụ: The solution was heated for five minutes.

keyPoints: Na passive, omume ahụ na-emetụta subject.
Passive na-eji ụdị “be” na past participle.
Object nke ahịrịokwu active na-aghọ subject nke passive.
Verbs na-enweghị object anaghị enwekarị ụdị passive.
Jiri passive mgbe a na-amaghị onye mere ihe ahụ ma ọ bụ mgbe ọ na-adịghị mkpa.

ha.title: Active voice da passive voice
ha.short: Yadda ake canza jimla tsakanin active da passive a kowane tense, da lokacin amfani da kowannensu.

sections.heading: Ma’anar voice
sections.text:
A active voice, subject ne yake yin aikin. A passive voice, subject ne yake karɓar aikin. Ma’anar tana nan yadda take, amma abin da aka fi mayar da hankali a kai yana canzawa.

Don gina passive, ka bi matakai uku. Ka matsar da object zuwa matsayin subject. Ka yi amfani da “be” a tense ɗin da ya dace, da past participle na babban verb. Ka ƙara “by” da wanda ya yi aikin ne kawai idan wanda ya yi aikin yana da muhimmanci.
Misali (active): The farmer harvests the maize.
Misali (passive): The maize is harvested by the farmer.

sections.heading: Passive a tenses daban-daban
sections.text:
Siffar “be” ce kaɗai ke canzawa tare da tense. Babban verb yana tsayawa a matsayin past participle.
Misali: The maize is harvested. (simple present)
Misali: The maize is being harvested. (present continuous)
Misali: The maize was harvested. (simple past)
Misali: The maize has been harvested. (present perfect)
Misali: The maize will be harvested. (future)
Misali: The maize must be harvested. (tare da modal verb)

A al’ada verbs masu object ne kaɗai suke iya zama passive. Verb kamar “arrive” ba shi da object, don haka ba shi da siffar passive.

sections.heading: Lokacin amfani da kowane voice
sections.text:
Active voice galibi ya fi bayyana kuma ya fi zuwa kai tsaye, don haka ya dace da yawancin rubutu. Passive yana da amfani a yanayi uku. Ka yi amfani da shi idan ba a san wanda ya yi aikin ba, idan wanda ya yi aikin ba shi da muhimmanci, ko idan aikin ya fi wanda ya yi shi muhimmanci. Rahotannin kimiyya da labarai suna yawan amfani da shi.
Misali: My phone was stolen.
Misali: The solution was heated for five minutes.

keyPoints: A passive, subject yana karɓar aikin.
Passive yana amfani da wata siffa ta be tare da past participle.
Object na jimlar active yana zama subject na passive.
Verbs marasa object a al’ada ba su da siffar passive.
Ka yi amfani da passive idan ba a san wanda ya yi aikin ba, ko kuma ba shi da muhimmanci.

en.title: Direct and reported speech
en.short: Changing direct speech to reported speech: tenses, pronouns, time words, questions and commands.

sections.heading: Statements
sections.text:
Direct speech gives the exact words of a speaker, inside quotation marks. Reported speech, also called indirect speech, gives the meaning without quotation marks. After a past verb such as “said”, the tense usually moves one step back. Pronouns also change to fit the new speaker.
Example (direct): Kofi said, “I am tired.”
Example (reported): Kofi said that he was tired.

Example: am, is → was
Example: walk → walked
Example: walked → had walked
Example: have walked → had walked
Example: will → would
Example: can → could
Example: may → might
Example: must → had to

If the reporting verb is in the present, the tense does not change. If a statement is still true, modern English often keeps the tense, but school exercises may expect the change.
Example: Kofi says that he is tired.

sections.heading: Time and place words
sections.text:
Time and place words also change.
Example: today → that day
Example: tomorrow → the next day
Example: yesterday → the day before
Example: here → there
Example: this → that

sections.heading: Questions and commands
sections.text:
Reported questions use statement word order, with no question mark. Yes or no questions use “if” or “whether”. Commands usually use “told” or “asked” with “to” and the base form.
Example (direct): She asked, “Where do you live?”
Example (reported): She asked me where I lived.
Example (direct): He asked, “Are you ready?”
Example (reported): He asked if I was ready.
Example (direct): The teacher said, “Close the door.”
Example (reported): The teacher told us to close the door.

keyPoints: After a past reporting verb, tenses usually move one step back.
Pronouns change to fit the new speaker.
Tomorrow becomes the next day, and yesterday becomes the day before.
Reported questions use statement word order and no question mark.
Reported commands use told or asked with to and the base form.

pcm.title: Direct and reported speech
pcm.short: How to change direct speech to reported speech: tenses, pronouns, time words, questions and commands.
keywords: how to report wetin person talk

sections.heading: Statements
sections.text:
Direct speech dey give the exact words of person wey talk, inside quotation marks. Reported speech, wey dem also dey call indirect speech, dey give the meaning without quotation marks. After past verb like “said”, the tense dey usually move one step back. Pronouns dey also change to fit the new person wey dey talk. For Pidgin, the verb fit stay the same, like “Kofi say e tire”. For Standard English, you must move the tense.
Example (direct): Kofi said, “I am tired.”
Example (reported): Kofi said that he was tired.

Example: am, is → was
Example: walk → walked
Example: walked → had walked
Example: have walked → had walked
Example: will → would
Example: can → could
Example: may → might
Example: must → had to

If the reporting verb dey for the present, the tense no dey change. If statement still true, modern English dey often keep the tense, but school exercises fit expect the change.
Example: Kofi says that he is tired.

sections.heading: Time and place words
sections.text:
Time and place words dey also change.
Example: today → that day
Example: tomorrow → the next day
Example: yesterday → the day before
Example: here → there
Example: this → that

sections.heading: Questions and commands
sections.text:
Reported questions dey use statement word order, and dem no get question mark. Yes or no questions dey use “if” or “whether”. Commands dey usually use “told” or “asked” with “to” and the base form.
Example (direct): She asked, “Where do you live?”
Example (reported): She asked me where I lived.
Example (direct): He asked, “Are you ready?”
Example (reported): He asked if I was ready.
Example (direct): The teacher said, “Close the door.”
Example (reported): The teacher told us to close the door.

keyPoints: After past reporting verb, tenses dey usually move one step back.
Pronouns dey change to fit the new person wey dey talk.
“Tomorrow” dey become “the next day”, and “yesterday” dey become “the day before”.
Reported questions dey use statement word order and no question mark.
Reported commands dey use “told” or “asked” with “to” and the base form.

fr.title: Le discours direct et le discours rapporté
fr.short: Passer du discours direct au discours rapporté : les temps, les pronoms, les mots de temps, les questions et les ordres.

sections.heading: Les phrases déclaratives
sections.text:
Le discours direct (direct speech) donne les mots exacts d’une personne, entre guillemets. Le discours rapporté (reported speech), aussi appelé discours indirect (indirect speech), donne le sens sans guillemets. Après un verbe au passé comme “said”, le temps recule généralement d’un cran. Les pronoms changent aussi pour s’adapter au nouveau locuteur.
Exemple (direct) : Kofi said, “I am tired.”
Exemple (rapporté) : Kofi said that he was tired.

Exemple : am, is → was
Exemple : walk → walked
Exemple : walked → had walked
Exemple : have walked → had walked
Exemple : will → would
Exemple : can → could
Exemple : may → might
Exemple : must → had to

Si le verbe introducteur est au présent, le temps ne change pas. Si une affirmation est toujours vraie, l’anglais moderne garde souvent le temps, mais les exercices scolaires peuvent attendre le changement.
Exemple : Kofi says that he is tired.

sections.heading: Les mots de temps et de lieu
sections.text:
Les mots de temps et de lieu changent aussi.
Exemple : today → that day
Exemple : tomorrow → the next day
Exemple : yesterday → the day before
Exemple : here → there
Exemple : this → that

sections.heading: Les questions et les ordres
sections.text:
Les questions rapportées utilisent l’ordre des mots d’une phrase déclarative, sans point d’interrogation. Les questions fermées (réponse “yes” ou “no”) utilisent “if” ou “whether”. Les ordres utilisent généralement “told” ou “asked” avec “to” et la base verbale.
Exemple (direct) : She asked, “Where do you live?”
Exemple (rapporté) : She asked me where I lived.
Exemple (direct) : He asked, “Are you ready?”
Exemple (rapporté) : He asked if I was ready.
Exemple (direct) : The teacher said, “Close the door.”
Exemple (rapporté) : The teacher told us to close the door.

keyPoints: Après un verbe introducteur au passé, les temps reculent généralement d’un cran.
Les pronoms changent pour s’adapter au nouveau locuteur.
“Tomorrow” devient “the next day”, et “yesterday” devient “the day before”.
Les questions rapportées utilisent l’ordre des mots d’une phrase déclarative et pas de point d’interrogation.
Les ordres rapportés utilisent “told” ou “asked” avec “to” et la base verbale.

ar.title: الكلام المباشر والكلام المنقول
ar.short: تحويل الكلام المباشر إلى كلام منقول: الأزمنة والضمائر وكلمات الوقت والأسئلة والأوامر.

sections.heading: الجمل الخبرية
sections.text:
الكلام المباشر ⁦(direct speech)⁩ يعطي كلمات المتحدث نفسها، داخل علامات الاقتباس. والكلام المنقول ⁦(reported speech)⁩، ويسمى أيضًا الكلام غير المباشر ⁦(indirect speech)⁩، يعطي المعنى بلا علامات اقتباس. وبعد فعل ماضٍ مثل ⁦“said”⁩، يرجع الزمن عادةً خطوة واحدة إلى الوراء. وتتغير الضمائر أيضًا لتناسب المتحدث الجديد.
مثال (مباشر): ⁦Kofi said, “I am tired.”⁩
مثال (منقول): ⁦Kofi said that he was tired⁩.

مثال: ⁦am, is → was⁩
مثال: ⁦walk → walked⁩
مثال: ⁦walked → had walked⁩
مثال: ⁦have walked → had walked⁩
مثال: ⁦will → would⁩
مثال: ⁦can → could⁩
مثال: ⁦may → might⁩
مثال: ⁦must → had to⁩

إذا كان فعل النقل ⁦(reporting verb)⁩ في المضارع، فلا يتغير الزمن. وإذا كانت الجملة الخبرية ما زالت صحيحة، فكثيرًا ما تُبقي الإنجليزية الحديثة على الزمن، لكن التمارين المدرسية قد تتوقع التغيير.
مثال: ⁦Kofi says that he is tired⁩.

sections.heading: كلمات الزمان والمكان
sections.text:
تتغير كلمات الزمان والمكان أيضًا.
مثال: ⁦today → that day⁩
مثال: ⁦tomorrow → the next day⁩
مثال: ⁦yesterday → the day before⁩
مثال: ⁦here → there⁩
مثال: ⁦this → that⁩

sections.heading: الأسئلة والأوامر
sections.text:
