Nomsa ta yi atisaye na tsawon wane lokaci? Rubutun ya faɗa: “for months”. Wannan literal ne.
Yaya ta ji a zuciyarta? Rubutun bai taɓa faɗa ba, amma rawar ƙafafu tana nuna cewa tana cikin fargaba (nervous). Wannan inference ne.
Wace kalma ce za ta iya maye gurbin “shook”? “Trembled” ya dace, kuma yana a past tense iri ɗaya.

sections.heading: Kyawawan halaye wajen amsawa
sections.text: Ka yi amfani da kalmominka, sai dai idan tambayar ta ce ka yi ambato (quote). Ka amsa abin da tambayar ta nema kawai. Idan kana maye gurbin kalma, ka ba da part of speech da tense iri ɗaya, don ta dace da jimlar. Wasu takardun jarrabawa, kamar WASSCE, suna neman kalmar da za ta iya maye gurbin wata kamar yadda aka yi amfani da ita a cikin passage. Ka gwada amsarka ta hanyar sanya ta cikin jimlar.

keyPoints: Ka yi skimming don ma’ana ta gaba ɗaya, sannan ka yi scanning don bayanai.
Amsoshin literal a rubuce suke, amsoshin inference kuma ana gano su daga alamu.
Maki yana nuna yawan abin da za ka rubuta.
Dole ne kalmar maye gurbi ta dace da ta asali a part of speech da tense.
Ka yi amfani da kalmominka, sai dai idan tambayar ta ce ka yi ambato (quote).

en.title: Summary writing
en.short: How to find the main points of a passage and write them briefly in your own words.

sections.heading: What a summary is
sections.text:
A summary gives the main points of a passage in far fewer words. It keeps the writer’s meaning and leaves out examples, repeated ideas and your own opinion.

Requirements differ. WASSCE and NECO often ask for a stated number of points, with one sentence for each. South African matric papers ask for seven points. Home Language wants a paragraph of at most 90 words. First Additional Language wants numbered sentences, with at most 70 words in total. Cambridge IGCSE First Language allows at most 120 words, and AQA GCSE uses two texts. Follow your question exactly.

sections.heading: The steps
sections.text:
1. Read the question, and note exactly what information it asks for.
2. Read the passage for its general meaning.
3. Underline only the points that answer the question. A topic sentence, which states the main idea of a paragraph, is often a good clue.
4. Rewrite each point briefly in your own words.
5. Check the number of points, the word limit and your grammar.

sections.heading: A worked example
sections.text:
The question asks for one cause of flooding in cities. Read this passage.
Example (passage): Plastic bags block drains in many cities. When heavy rain falls, the water cannot flow away, and so the streets flood.
Example (summary point): Plastic bags cause flooding by blocking drains.

Copying whole sentences from a passage is called lifting, and it can lose marks. You may keep key words that have no simple replacement, such as “flooding” here. Write each point as a full, clear sentence, unless the question asks for a paragraph or allows notes. A half-sentence may lose marks.

keyPoints: A summary gives only the main points that the question asks for.
Leave out examples, repetition and your own opinion.
Rewrite the points in your own words instead of lifting sentences.
Rules on number of points and word limit differ between exam boards.
Unless told otherwise, write points as complete sentences.

pcm.title: Summary writing
pcm.short: How to find the main points of passage and write them short with your own words.

sections.heading: Wetin summary be
sections.text:
Summary dey give the main points of passage with far fewer words. E dey keep the meaning of the writer and e dey leave out examples, ideas wey repeat and your own opinion.

Requirements no be the same. WASSCE and NECO dey often ask for stated number of points, with one sentence for each. South African matric papers dey ask for seven points. Home Language want paragraph of at most 90 words. First Additional Language want numbered sentences, with at most 70 words in total. Cambridge IGCSE First Language allow at most 120 words, and AQA GCSE dey use two texts. Follow your question exactly.

sections.heading: The steps
sections.text:
1. Read the question, and note exactly the information wey e ask for.
2. Read the passage for im general meaning.
3. Underline only the points wey answer the question. Topic sentence, wey dey state the main idea of paragraph, dey often be good clue.
4. Rewrite each point short with your own words.
5. Check the number of points, the word limit and your grammar.

sections.heading: One worked example
sections.text:
The question ask for one cause of flooding for cities. Read this passage.
Example (passage): Plastic bags block drains in many cities. When heavy rain falls, the water cannot flow away, and so the streets flood.
Example (summary point): Plastic bags cause flooding by blocking drains.

To copy whole sentences from passage, dem dey call am lifting, and e fit make you lose marks. You fit keep key words wey no get simple replacement, like “flooding” for here. Write each point as full, clear sentence, unless the question ask for paragraph or allow notes. Half sentence fit make you lose marks.

keyPoints: Summary dey give only the main points wey the question ask for.
Leave out examples, repetition and your own opinion.
Rewrite the points with your own words, no lift sentences.
Rules on number of points and word limit no be the same for all exam boards.
Unless dem tell you otherwise, write points as complete sentences.

fr.title: Le résumé
fr.short: Comment trouver les idées principales d’un texte et les écrire brièvement avec tes propres mots.

sections.heading: Ce qu’est un résumé
sections.text:
Un résumé (summary) donne les idées principales d’un texte en beaucoup moins de mots. Il garde le sens voulu par l’auteur et laisse de côté les exemples, les idées répétées et ton opinion personnelle.

Les exigences varient. Le WASSCE et le NECO demandent souvent un nombre précis d’idées, avec une phrase pour chacune. Les épreuves du matric sud-africain demandent sept idées. Home Language demande un paragraphe de 90 mots au maximum. First Additional Language demande des phrases numérotées, avec 70 mots au maximum au total. Cambridge IGCSE First Language autorise 120 mots au maximum, et AQA GCSE utilise deux textes. Suis exactement ta consigne.

sections.heading: Les étapes
sections.text:
1. Lis la question et note exactement quelle information elle demande.
2. Lis le texte pour en saisir le sens général.
3. Souligne seulement les idées qui répondent à la question. Une phrase clé (topic sentence), qui énonce l’idée principale d’un paragraphe, est souvent un bon indice.
4. Réécris chaque idée brièvement avec tes propres mots.
5. Vérifie le nombre d’idées, la limite de mots et ta grammaire.

sections.heading: Un exemple corrigé
sections.text:
La question demande une cause des inondations dans les villes. Lis ce texte.
Exemple (texte) : Plastic bags block drains in many cities. When heavy rain falls, the water cannot flow away, and so the streets flood.
Exemple (idée du résumé) : Plastic bags cause flooding by blocking drains.

Recopier des phrases entières d’un texte s’appelle le lifting (copie telle quelle), et cela peut faire perdre des points. Tu peux garder les mots clés qui n’ont pas de remplacement simple, comme “flooding” ici. Écris chaque idée sous forme de phrase complète et claire, sauf si la question demande un paragraphe ou autorise des notes. Une moitié de phrase peut faire perdre des points.

keyPoints: Un résumé donne seulement les idées principales que la question demande.
Laisse de côté les exemples, les répétitions et ton opinion personnelle.
Réécris les idées avec tes propres mots au lieu de recopier des phrases.
Les règles sur le nombre d’idées et la limite de mots varient selon les organismes d’examen.
Sauf consigne contraire, écris les idées sous forme de phrases complètes.

ar.title: كتابة الملخص
ar.short: كيف تجد الأفكار الرئيسية في نص وتكتبها باختصار بكلماتك الخاصة.

sections.heading: ما الملخص
sections.text:
الملخص ⁦(summary)⁩ يعطي الأفكار الرئيسية في نص بكلمات أقل بكثير. وهو يحافظ على معنى الكاتب ويحذف الأمثلة والأفكار المكررة ورأيك الشخصي.

تختلف المتطلبات. فكثيرًا ما تطلب WASSCE وNECO عددًا محددًا من النقاط، بجملة واحدة لكل نقطة. وتطلب أوراق matric في جنوب إفريقيا سبع نقاط. وتطلب ⁦Home Language⁩ (اللغة الأم) فقرة من 90 كلمة على الأكثر. وتطلب ⁦First Additional Language⁩ (اللغة الإضافية الأولى) جملًا مرقمة، من 70 كلمة على الأكثر في المجموع. ويسمح ⁦Cambridge IGCSE First Language⁩ بـ 120 كلمة على الأكثر، ويستخدم ⁦AQA GCSE⁩ نصين. فاتبع سؤالك بدقة.

sections.heading: الخطوات
sections.text:
1. اقرأ السؤال، ولاحظ بالضبط المعلومات التي يطلبها.
2. اقرأ النص لتعرف معناه العام.
3. ضع خطًا تحت النقاط التي تجيب عن السؤال فقط. والجملة الموضوعية ⁦(topic sentence)⁩، وهي التي تذكر الفكرة الرئيسية في الفقرة، كثيرًا ما تكون دليلًا جيدًا.
4. أعد كتابة كل نقطة باختصار بكلماتك الخاصة.
5. راجع عدد النقاط وحد الكلمات وقواعدك.

sections.heading: مثال محلول
sections.text:
يطلب السؤال سببًا واحدًا للفيضانات في المدن. اقرأ هذا النص.
مثال (النص): ⁦Plastic bags block drains in many cities. When heavy rain falls, the water cannot flow away, and so the streets flood⁩.
مثال (نقطة الملخص): ⁦Plastic bags cause flooding by blocking drains⁩.

نسخ جمل كاملة من النص يسمى lifting (النقل الحرفي)، وقد يُفقدك درجات. ويمكنك الإبقاء على الكلمات الأساسية التي ليس لها بديل بسيط، مثل ⁦“flooding”⁩ هنا. واكتب كل نقطة في جملة كاملة واضحة، ما لم يطلب السؤال فقرة أو يسمح بملاحظات. وقد يُفقدك نصف الجملة درجات.

keyPoints: يعطي الملخص فقط النقاط الرئيسية التي يطلبها السؤال.
احذف الأمثلة والتكرار ورأيك الشخصي.
أعد كتابة النقاط بكلماتك الخاصة بدلًا من نقل الجمل نقلًا حرفيًا.
تختلف قواعد عدد النقاط وحد الكلمات من هيئة امتحانات إلى أخرى.
ما لم يُطلب منك غير ذلك، اكتب النقاط في جمل كاملة.

sw.title: Kuandika ufupisho
sw.short: Jinsi ya kupata hoja kuu za kifungu na kuziandika kwa ufupi kwa maneno yako mwenyewe.

sections.heading: Ufupisho ni nini
sections.text:
Ufupisho (summary) hutoa hoja kuu za kifungu kwa maneno machache mno kuliko kifungu chenyewe. Hubakiza maana ya mwandishi na huacha mifano, mawazo yanayojirudia na maoni yako mwenyewe.

Mahitaji hutofautiana. WASSCE na NECO mara nyingi huuliza idadi iliyotajwa ya hoja, na sentensi moja kwa kila hoja. Karatasi za matric za Afrika Kusini huuliza hoja saba. Home Language inataka aya ya maneno yasiyozidi 90. First Additional Language inataka sentensi zenye nambari, zenye jumla ya maneno yasiyozidi 70. Cambridge IGCSE First Language inaruhusu maneno yasiyozidi 120, na AQA GCSE hutumia maandishi mawili. Fuata swali lako kikamilifu.

sections.heading: Hatua
sections.text:
1. Soma swali, na uandike ni habari gani hasa linayouliza.
2. Soma kifungu ili kupata maana yake ya jumla.
3. Pigia mstari hoja zinazojibu swali pekee. Sentensi kuu (topic sentence), inayoeleza wazo kuu la aya, mara nyingi ni kidokezo kizuri.
4. Andika upya kila hoja kwa ufupi kwa maneno yako mwenyewe.
5. Kagua idadi ya hoja, kikomo cha maneno na sarufi yako.

sections.heading: Mfano uliofanyiwa kazi
sections.text:
Swali linauliza sababu moja ya mafuriko mijini. Soma kifungu hiki.
Mfano (kifungu): Plastic bags block drains in many cities. When heavy rain falls, the water cannot flow away, and so the streets flood.
Mfano (hoja ya ufupisho): Plastic bags cause flooding by blocking drains.

Kunakili sentensi nzima kutoka kifungu huitwa lifting, na kunaweza kupoteza alama. Unaweza kubakiza maneno muhimu yasiyo na mbadala rahisi, kama “flooding” hapa. Andika kila hoja kama sentensi kamili iliyo wazi, isipokuwa swali linauliza aya au linaruhusu madokezo. Nusu sentensi inaweza kupoteza alama.

keyPoints: Ufupisho hutoa tu hoja kuu ambazo swali linauliza.
Acha mifano, marudio na maoni yako mwenyewe.
Andika upya hoja kwa maneno yako mwenyewe badala ya kunakili sentensi (lifting).
Kanuni za idadi ya hoja na kikomo cha maneno hutofautiana kati ya bodi za mitihani.
Isipokuwa umeambiwa vinginevyo, andika hoja kama sentensi kamili.

pt.title: Escrever um resumo
pt.short: Como encontrar as ideias principais de um texto e escrevê-las de forma breve pelas tuas próprias palavras.

sections.heading: O que é um resumo
sections.text:
Um resumo (summary) apresenta as ideias principais de um texto em muito menos palavras. Mantém o sentido dado pelo autor e deixa de fora os exemplos, as ideias repetidas e a tua própria opinião.

As exigências variam. O WASSCE e o NECO pedem muitas vezes um número indicado de ideias, com uma frase para cada uma. As provas de matric da África do Sul pedem sete ideias. Home Language exige um parágrafo de 90 palavras, no máximo. First Additional Language exige frases numeradas, com 70 palavras no total, no máximo. O Cambridge IGCSE First Language permite 120 palavras, no máximo, e o AQA GCSE usa dois textos. Segue exatamente o que a tua pergunta pede.

sections.heading: Os passos
sections.text:
1. Lê a pergunta e anota exatamente que informação ela pede.
2. Lê o texto para perceberes o seu sentido geral.
3. Sublinha apenas as ideias que respondem à pergunta. Uma frase-tópico (topic sentence), que indica a ideia principal de um parágrafo, é muitas vezes uma boa pista.
4. Reescreve cada ideia de forma breve, pelas tuas próprias palavras.
5. Verifica o número de ideias, o limite de palavras e a tua gramática.

sections.heading: Um exemplo resolvido
sections.text:
A pergunta pede uma causa das inundações nas cidades. Lê este texto.
Exemplo (texto): Plastic bags block drains in many cities. When heavy rain falls, the water cannot flow away, and so the streets flood.
Exemplo (ideia do resumo): Plastic bags cause flooding by blocking drains.

Copiar frases inteiras de um texto chama-se lifting e pode fazer-te perder pontos. Podes manter palavras-chave que não têm substituto simples, como “flooding” neste caso. Escreve cada ideia numa frase completa e clara, a não ser que a pergunta peça um parágrafo ou permita notas. Uma frase incompleta pode fazer-te perder pontos.

keyPoints: Um resumo apresenta apenas as ideias principais que a pergunta pede.
Deixa de fora os exemplos, as repetições e a tua própria opinião.
Reescreve as ideias pelas tuas próprias palavras em vez de copiares frases (lifting).
As regras sobre o número de ideias e o limite de palavras variam entre entidades examinadoras.
Salvo indicação em contrário, escreve as ideias em frases completas.

es.title: Cómo escribir un resumen
es.short: Cómo encontrar las ideas principales de un texto y escribirlas brevemente con tus propias palabras.

sections.heading: Qué es un resumen
sections.text:
Un resumen (summary) da las ideas principales de un texto en muchas menos palabras. Conserva el significado que da el autor y deja fuera los ejemplos, las ideas repetidas y tu propia opinión.

Los requisitos varían. El WASSCE y el NECO suelen pedir un número determinado de ideas, con una oración para cada una. Los exámenes de matric de Sudáfrica piden siete ideas. Home Language pide un párrafo de 90 palabras como máximo. First Additional Language pide oraciones numeradas, con 70 palabras en total como máximo. Cambridge IGCSE First Language permite 120 palabras como máximo, y AQA GCSE usa dos textos. Sigue exactamente lo que dice tu pregunta.

sections.heading: Los pasos
sections.text:
1. Lee la pregunta y anota exactamente qué información pide.
2. Lee el texto para captar su significado general.
3. Subraya solo las ideas que responden a la pregunta. Una oración temática (topic sentence), que expresa la idea principal de un párrafo, suele ser una buena pista.
4. Reescribe cada idea brevemente con tus propias palabras.
5. Comprueba el número de ideas, el límite de palabras y tu gramática.

sections.heading: Un ejemplo resuelto
sections.text:
La pregunta pide una causa de las inundaciones en las ciudades. Lee este texto.
Ejemplo (texto): Plastic bags block drains in many cities. When heavy rain falls, the water cannot flow away, and so the streets flood.
Ejemplo (idea del resumen): Plastic bags cause flooding by blocking drains.

Copiar oraciones enteras de un texto se llama copia literal (lifting), y puede hacerte perder puntos. Puedes conservar palabras clave que no tienen un sustituto sencillo, como “flooding” aquí. Escribe cada idea como una oración completa y clara, a menos que la pregunta pida un párrafo o permita notas. Una oración a medias puede hacerte perder puntos.

keyPoints: Un resumen da solo las ideas principales que pide la pregunta.
Deja fuera los ejemplos, las repeticiones y tu propia opinión.
Reescribe las ideas con tus propias palabras en lugar de copiar oraciones.
Las reglas sobre el número de ideas y el límite de palabras varían según el organismo examinador.
Salvo que te indiquen otra cosa, escribe las ideas como oraciones completas.

yo.title: Summary writing (kíkọ àkópọ̀)
yo.short: Bí o ṣe lè rí àwọn kókó pàtàkì inú àyọkà, kí o sì kọ wọ́n ní ṣókí ní ọ̀rọ̀ ara rẹ.

sections.heading: Ohun tí summary jẹ́
sections.text:
Summary (àkópọ̀) ń sọ àwọn kókó pàtàkì inú àyọkà kan ní ọ̀rọ̀ tó dín kù gan-an. Ó ń pa ìtumọ̀ òǹkọ̀wé mọ́, ó sì ń fi àwọn àpẹẹrẹ, àwọn èrò tí a tún sọ àti èrò tìrẹ sílẹ̀.

Ohun tí a ń béèrè yàtọ̀ síra. WASSCE àti NECO sábà máa ń béèrè iye kókó kan pàtó, pẹ̀lú gbólóhùn kan fún ọ̀kọ̀ọ̀kan. Àwọn ìwé ìdánwò matric ní Gúúsù Áfíríkà ń béèrè kókó méje. Home Language fẹ́ paragraph (ìpínrọ̀) tí kò ju ọ̀rọ̀ 90 lọ. First Additional Language fẹ́ àwọn gbólóhùn tí a fi nọ́ńbà sí, tí gbogbo wọn kò ju ọ̀rọ̀ 70 lọ. Cambridge IGCSE First Language gba ọ̀rọ̀ tí kò ju 120 lọ, AQA GCSE sì ń lo àyọkà méjì. Tẹ̀lé ìbéèrè rẹ gẹ́lẹ́.

sections.heading: Àwọn ìgbésẹ̀
sections.text:
1. Ka ìbéèrè náà, kí o sì kíyèsí ìsọfúnni tí ó ń béèrè gẹ́lẹ́.
2. Ka àyọkà náà fún ìtumọ̀ gbogbogbò rẹ̀.
3. Fa ìlà sí abẹ́ àwọn kókó tó dáhùn ìbéèrè náà nìkan. Topic sentence, tó ń sọ èrò pàtàkì ìpínrọ̀ kan, sábà máa ń jẹ́ àmì tó dára.
4. Tún kókó kọ̀ọ̀kan kọ ní ṣókí ní ọ̀rọ̀ ara rẹ.
5. Yẹ iye kókó, òdiwọ̀n iye ọ̀rọ̀ àti gírámà rẹ wò.

sections.heading: Àpẹẹrẹ tí a ti ṣiṣẹ́ rẹ̀
sections.text:
Ìbéèrè náà béèrè ohun kan tó ń fa flooding (àkúnya omi) ní àwọn ìlú ńlá. Ka àyọkà yìí.
Àpẹẹrẹ (àyọkà): Plastic bags block drains in many cities. When heavy rain falls, the water cannot flow away, and so the streets flood.
Àpẹẹrẹ (kókó summary): Plastic bags cause flooding by blocking drains.

A ń pe dída odidi gbólóhùn kọ láti inú àyọkà ní lifting, ó sì lè mú kí o pàdánù máàkì. O lè pa àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ pàtàkì tí kò ní ọ̀rọ̀ tó rọrùn láti rọ́pò wọn mọ́, bíi “flooding” níbí. Kọ kókó kọ̀ọ̀kan ní gbólóhùn tó pé, tó sì ṣe kedere, àyàfi tí ìbéèrè bá béèrè ìpínrọ̀ tàbí tó gba notes (àkọsílẹ̀ kúkúrú). Ìdajì gbólóhùn lè mú kí o pàdánù máàkì.

keyPoints: Summary ń sọ àwọn kókó pàtàkì tí ìbéèrè béèrè nìkan.
Yọ àwọn àpẹẹrẹ, àtúnsọ àti èrò tìrẹ kúrò.
Tún àwọn kókó náà kọ ní ọ̀rọ̀ ara rẹ dípò kí o ṣe lifting gbólóhùn.
Òfin nípa iye kókó àti òdiwọ̀n iye ọ̀rọ̀ yàtọ̀ láàárín àwọn àjọ ìdánwò.
Àyàfi tí a bá sọ ohun mìíràn fún ọ, kọ àwọn kókó ní gbólóhùn tó pé.

ig.title: Ide summary (nchịkọta)
ig.short: Otú e si achọta isi ihe dị na passage wee dee ha nkenke n’okwu nke gị.

sections.heading: Ihe summary bụ
sections.text:
Summary (nchịkọta) na-enye isi ihe dị na passage (akụkụ ederede) n’okwu dị nnọọ ole na ole karịa. Ọ na-edebe ihe onye dere ya pụtara, ma na-ahapụ ihe atụ, echiche e kwughachiri na echiche nke gị.

Ihe a chọrọ dị iche iche. WASSCE na NECO na-ajụkarị ọnụọgụ isi ihe a kapịrị ọnụ, otu ahịrịokwu maka nke ọ bụla. Akwụkwọ ule matric nke South Africa na-ajụ isi ihe asaa. Home Language chọrọ paragraph (nkeji edemede) nke na-agafeghị okwu 90. First Additional Language chọrọ ahịrịokwu e dere ọnụọgụ n’akụkụ ha, nke na-agafeghị okwu 70 n’ozuzu. Cambridge IGCSE First Language na-anabata ihe na-agafeghị okwu 120, AQA GCSE na-ejikwa ederede abụọ. Soro ajụjụ gị kpọmkwem.

sections.heading: Usoro ya
sections.text:
1. Gụọ ajụjụ ahụ, rịbakwa ama kpọmkwem ozi ọ na-ajụ.
2. Gụọ passage ahụ iji ghọta ihe ọ pụtara n’ozuzu.
3. Dọọ ahịrị n’okpuru naanị isi ihe ndị na-aza ajụjụ ahụ. Topic sentence, nke na-ekwu isi echiche nke paragraph, na-abụkarị ezigbo ihe ngosi.
4. Degharịa isi ihe ọ bụla nkenke n’okwu nke gị.
5. Lelee ọnụọgụ isi ihe, oke okwu na grammar gị.

sections.heading: Ihe atụ e dozichara
sections.text:
Ajụjụ ahụ na-ajụ otu ihe na-akpata idei mmiri n’obodo ukwu. Gụọ passage a.
Ihe atụ (passage): Plastic bags block drains in many cities. When heavy rain falls, the water cannot flow away, and so the streets flood.
Ihe atụ (isi ihe nchịkọta): Plastic bags cause flooding by blocking drains.

A na-akpọ idepụta ahịrịokwu niile site na passage lifting, ọ nwekwara ike ime ka i tụfuo marks (akara ule). I nwere ike idebe okwu ndị dị mkpa na-enweghị okwu dị mfe na-anọchi ha, dị ka “flooding” ebe a. Dee isi ihe ọ bụla dị ka ahịrịokwu zuru ezu, doro anya, ma ọ bụrụ na ajụjụ ahụ achọghị paragraph ma ọ bụ na o kweghị ka i dee notes (nkenke ndetu). Ọkara ahịrịokwu nwere ike ime ka i tụfuo marks.

keyPoints: Summary na-enye naanị isi ihe ndị ajụjụ ahụ jụrụ.
Hapụ ihe atụ, ihe e kwughachiri na echiche nke gị.
Degharịa isi ihe n’okwu nke gị, kama idepụta ahịrịokwu (lifting).
Iwu banyere ọnụọgụ isi ihe na oke okwu dị iche site n’otu exam board gaa n’ọzọ.
Ọ bụrụ na a gwaghị gị ihe ọzọ, dee isi ihe dị ka ahịrịokwu zuru ezu.

ha.title: Summary writing (rubuta taƙaitawa)
ha.short: Yadda ake nemo muhimman batutuwan passage da rubuta su a taƙaice da kalmominka.

sections.heading: Mene ne summary
sections.text:
Summary (taƙaitawa) yana ba da muhimman batutuwan passage (guntun rubutu) da kalmomi ƙasa da na asali sosai. Yana riƙe ma’anar marubucin, kuma yana cire misalai, tunanin da aka maimaita da ra’ayinka.

Abubuwan da ake buƙata sun bambanta. WASSCE da NECO sukan nemi wani adadi da aka ƙayyade na batutuwa, tare da jimla ɗaya ga kowannensu. Takardun matric na Afirka ta Kudu suna neman batutuwa bakwai. Home Language yana neman sakin layi (paragraph) na kalmomi 90 a mafi yawa. First Additional Language yana neman jimloli masu lamba, kalmomi 70 a mafi yawa gaba ɗaya. Cambridge IGCSE First Language yana ba da izinin kalmomi 120 a mafi yawa, AQA GCSE kuma yana amfani da rubutu biyu. Ka bi tambayarka daidai.

sections.heading: Matakan
sections.text:
1. Ka karanta tambayar, ka lura da ainihin bayanin da take nema.
2. Ka karanta passage ɗin don ma’anarsa ta gaba ɗaya.
3. Ka ja layi a ƙarƙashin batutuwan da ke amsa tambayar kawai. Topic sentence, wanda ke faɗin babban tunanin sakin layi, sau da yawa yana zama alama mai kyau.
4. Ka sake rubuta kowane batu a taƙaice da kalmominka.
5. Ka duba yawan batutuwa, iyakar kalmomi da nahawunka.

sections.heading: Misali da aka warware
sections.text:
Tambayar tana neman dalili ɗaya na ambaliyar ruwa a birane. Ka karanta wannan passage.
Misali (passage): Plastic bags block drains in many cities. When heavy rain falls, the water cannot flow away, and so the streets flood.
Misali (batun summary): Plastic bags cause flooding by blocking drains.

Kwafar cikakkun jimloli daga passage ana kiransa lifting, kuma yana iya sa a rasa maki. Za ka iya riƙe muhimman kalmomin da ba su da sauƙin maye gurbi, kamar “flooding” a nan. Ka rubuta kowane batu a matsayin cikakkiyar jimla a sarari, sai dai idan tambayar ta nemi sakin layi ko ta yarda da taƙaitattun bayanai (notes). Rabin jimla yana iya sa a rasa maki.

keyPoints: Summary yana ba da muhimman batutuwan da tambayar ta nema ne kawai.
Ka cire misalai, maimaitawa da ra’ayinka.
Ka sake rubuta batutuwan da kalmominka maimakon yin lifting na jimloli.
Ƙa’idojin yawan batutuwa da iyakar kalmomi sun bambanta tsakanin hukumomin jarrabawa.
Sai dai idan an ce wani abu daban, ka rubuta batutuwa a matsayin cikakkun jimloli.

en.title: Fact, opinion and persuasive language
en.short: Telling fact from opinion, spotting bias, and explaining how adverts and writers try to persuade.

sections.heading: Fact, opinion and bias
sections.text:
A fact can be checked and shown to be true or false. An opinion is what someone thinks or feels. Words such as best, should and terrible often signal an opinion. A text can present an opinion as if it were a fact, so read with care.
Example: The bridge is 400 metres long. (fact)
Example: The bridge is the most beautiful in the country. (opinion)

Bias means favouring one side unfairly. A biased writer may leave out important facts, or give only one view. Ask who wrote the text, and what they want you to believe.

sections.heading: How writers persuade
sections.text:
Writers use several techniques to influence readers.
Emotive language chooses words that stir feeling.
Example: Helpless children go hungry every night.
A rhetorical question is asked for effect, and it expects no answer.
Example: Who would refuse clean water?
Direct address speaks to the reader as “you”.
Example: You deserve better.
Repetition makes an idea stay in the mind. Numbers can make a claim sound certain, so ask where they come from.
Example: Nine out of ten users agree.

sections.heading: Adverts, cartoons and exam answers
sections.text:
Exams differ in what they test here. South African papers set questions on adverts and cartoons. Cambridge IGCSE asks how writers influence readers, and WASSCE comprehension includes literary terms. With adverts and cartoons, study the pictures and the words together.

A good answer has three steps. Name the technique, quote the words and explain the effect on the reader.
Example: The question “Who would refuse clean water?” is rhetorical. It suggests that any sensible reader must agree.

keyPoints: A fact can be checked, but an opinion is a personal view.
Bias means favouring one side unfairly.
Emotive language aims to stir the reader’s feelings.
A rhetorical question expects no answer.
Name the technique, quote the words and explain the effect.

pcm.title: Fact, opinion and persuasive language
pcm.short: How to separate fact from opinion, spot bias, and explain how adverts and writers dey try persuade people.

sections.heading: Fact, opinion and bias
sections.text:
Fact na something wey you fit check and show say e true or false. Opinion na wetin person think or feel. Words like best, should and terrible dey often signal opinion. Text fit present opinion like say na fact, so read with care.
Example: The bridge is 400 metres long. (fact)
Example: The bridge is the most beautiful in the country. (opinion)

Bias mean to favour one side unfairly. Writer wey get bias fit leave out important facts, or give only one view. Ask who write the text, and wetin dem want make you believe.

sections.heading: How writers dey persuade
sections.text:
Writers dey use different techniques to influence readers.
Emotive language dey choose words wey dey stir feeling.
Example: Helpless children go hungry every night.
Rhetorical question na question wey dem ask for effect, and e no dey expect answer.
Example: Who would refuse clean water?
Direct address dey talk to the reader as “you”.
Example: You deserve better.
Repetition dey make idea stay for mind. Numbers fit make claim sound certain, so ask where dem come from.
Example: Nine out of ten users agree.

sections.heading: Adverts, cartoons and exam answers
sections.text:
Exams no dey test the same thing for here. South African papers dey set questions on adverts and cartoons. Cambridge IGCSE dey ask how writers dey influence readers, and WASSCE comprehension include literary terms. With adverts and cartoons, study the pictures and the words together.

Good answer get three steps. Name the technique, quote the words and explain the effect on the reader.
Example: The question “Who would refuse clean water?” is rhetorical. It suggests that any sensible reader must agree.

keyPoints: You fit check fact, but opinion na person’s own view.
Bias mean to favour one side unfairly.
Emotive language dey try stir the feelings of the reader.
Rhetorical question no dey expect answer.
Name the technique, quote the words and explain the effect.

fr.title: Le fait, l’opinion et le langage persuasif
fr.short: Distinguer le fait de l’opinion, repérer les partis pris et expliquer comment les publicités et les auteurs cherchent à persuader.

sections.heading: Le fait, l’opinion et le parti pris
sections.text:
Un fait (fact) peut être vérifié et se révéler vrai ou faux. Une opinion (opinion) est ce que quelqu’un pense ou ressent. Des mots comme “best”, “should” et “terrible” signalent souvent une opinion. Un texte peut présenter une opinion comme si c’était un fait, alors lis avec attention.
Exemple : The bridge is 400 metres long. (fait)
Exemple : The bridge is the most beautiful in the country. (opinion)

Le parti pris (bias) consiste à favoriser un camp de façon injuste. Un auteur partial peut omettre des faits importants ou ne donner qu’un seul point de vue. Demande-toi qui a écrit le texte et ce que cette personne veut te faire croire.

sections.heading: Comment les auteurs persuadent
sections.text:
Les auteurs utilisent plusieurs techniques pour influencer les lecteurs.
Le langage émotif (emotive language) choisit des mots qui éveillent des sentiments.
Exemple : Helpless children go hungry every night.
Une question rhétorique (rhetorical question) est posée pour produire un effet, et elle n’attend pas de réponse.
Exemple : Who would refuse clean water?
L’adresse directe (direct address) parle au lecteur en disant “you”.
Exemple : You deserve better.
La répétition (repetition) fait rester une idée dans l’esprit. Les chiffres peuvent donner l’impression qu’une affirmation est certaine, alors demande-toi d’où ils viennent.
Exemple : Nine out of ten users agree.

sections.heading: Les publicités, les dessins humoristiques et les réponses d’examen
sections.text:
Les examens n’évaluent pas tous la même chose dans ce domaine. Les épreuves sud-africaines posent des questions sur les publicités et les dessins humoristiques (cartoons). Cambridge IGCSE demande comment les auteurs influencent les lecteurs, et la compréhension du WASSCE comprend des termes littéraires. Pour les publicités et les dessins humoristiques, étudie les images et les mots ensemble.

Une bonne réponse a trois étapes. Nomme la technique, cite les mots et explique l’effet sur le lecteur.
Exemple : The question “Who would refuse clean water?” is rhetorical. It suggests that any sensible reader must agree.

keyPoints: Un fait peut être vérifié, mais une opinion est un point de vue personnel.
Le parti pris consiste à favoriser un camp de façon injuste.
Le langage émotif vise à éveiller les sentiments du lecteur.
Une question rhétorique n’attend pas de réponse.
Nomme la technique, cite les mots et explique l’effet.

ar.title: الحقيقة والرأي ولغة الإقناع
ar.short: التمييز بين الحقيقة والرأي، وكشف التحيز، وشرح كيف يحاول المعلنون والكتّاب الإقناع.

sections.heading: الحقيقة والرأي والتحيز
sections.text:
الحقيقة ⁦(fact)⁩ يمكن التحقق منها وإثبات أنها صحيحة أو خاطئة. والرأي ⁦(opinion)⁩ هو ما يعتقده شخص أو يشعر به. وكثيرًا ما تدل كلمات مثل best وshould وterrible على رأي. وقد يعرض نص رأيًا كأنه حقيقة، فاقرأ بعناية.
مثال: ⁦The bridge is 400 metres long⁩. (حقيقة)
مثال: ⁦The bridge is the most beautiful in the country⁩. (رأي)

التحيز ⁦(bias)⁩ يعني تفضيل جانب واحد بغير إنصاف. وقد يحذف الكاتب المتحيز حقائق مهمة، أو يعرض وجهة نظر واحدة فقط. واسأل من كتب النص، وما الذي يريد منك أن تصدقه.

sections.heading: كيف يقنع الكتّاب
sections.text:
يستخدم الكتّاب عدة أساليب للتأثير في القراء.
اللغة العاطفية ⁦(emotive language)⁩ تختار كلمات تثير الشعور.
مثال: ⁦Helpless children go hungry every night⁩.
السؤال البلاغي ⁦(rhetorical question)⁩ يُطرح لإحداث أثر، ولا يتوقع إجابة.
مثال: ⁦Who would refuse clean water⁩?
الخطاب المباشر ⁦(direct address)⁩ يخاطب القارئ بكلمة ⁦“you”⁩.
مثال: ⁦You deserve better⁩.
التكرار ⁦(repetition)⁩ يجعل الفكرة تبقى في الذهن. وقد تجعل الأرقام ادعاءً يبدو مؤكدًا، فاسأل من أين جاءت.
مثال: ⁦Nine out of ten users agree⁩.

sections.heading: الإعلانات والرسوم الكاريكاتورية وإجابات الامتحان
sections.text:
تختلف الامتحانات في ما تختبره هنا. فأوراق جنوب إفريقيا تضع أسئلة عن الإعلانات والرسوم الكاريكاتورية. ويسأل ⁦Cambridge IGCSE⁩ عن كيفية تأثير الكتّاب في القراء، ويتضمن فهم المقروء في WASSCE المصطلحات الأدبية. ومع الإعلانات والرسوم الكاريكاتورية، ادرس الصور والكلمات معًا.

للإجابة الجيدة ثلاث خطوات. سمِّ الأسلوب، واقتبس الكلمات، واشرح الأثر في القارئ.
مثال: ⁦The question “Who would refuse clean water?” is rhetorical. It suggests that any sensible reader must agree⁩.

keyPoints: يمكن التحقق من الحقيقة، أما الرأي فوجهة نظر شخصية.
التحيز يعني تفضيل جانب واحد بغير إنصاف.
تهدف اللغة العاطفية إلى إثارة مشاعر القارئ.
السؤال البلاغي لا يتوقع إجابة.
سمِّ الأسلوب، واقتبس الكلمات، واشرح الأثر.

sw.title: Ukweli, maoni na lugha ya ushawishi
sw.short: Kutofautisha ukweli na maoni, kutambua upendeleo, na kueleza jinsi matangazo na waandishi wanavyojaribu kushawishi.

sections.heading: Ukweli, maoni na upendeleo
sections.text:
Ukweli (fact) unaweza kukaguliwa na kuonyeshwa kuwa ni kweli au si kweli. Maoni (opinion) ni kile ambacho mtu anafikiri au kuhisi. Maneno kama “best”, “should” na “terrible” mara nyingi huashiria maoni. Maandishi yanaweza kuwasilisha maoni kana kwamba ni ukweli, kwa hiyo soma kwa makini.
Mfano: The bridge is 400 metres long. (ukweli)
Mfano: The bridge is the most beautiful in the country. (maoni)

Upendeleo (bias) ni kupendelea upande mmoja isivyo haki. Mwandishi mwenye upendeleo anaweza kuacha mambo muhimu ya kweli, au kutoa mtazamo mmoja tu. Uliza nani aliandika maandishi hayo, na anataka uamini nini.

sections.heading: Jinsi waandishi wanavyoshawishi
sections.text:
Waandishi hutumia mbinu kadhaa kuwashawishi wasomaji.
Lugha ya kuibua hisia (emotive language) huchagua maneno yanayoamsha hisia.
Mfano: Helpless children go hungry every night.
Swali la balagha (rhetorical question) huulizwa kwa ajili ya athari, na halitarajii jibu.
Mfano: Who would refuse clean water?
Kuzungumza na msomaji moja kwa moja (direct address) humwita msomaji “you”.
Mfano: You deserve better.
Urudiaji (repetition) hufanya wazo libaki akilini. Nambari zinaweza kufanya dai lionekane la uhakika, kwa hiyo uliza zinatoka wapi.
Mfano: Nine out of ten users agree.

sections.heading: Matangazo, vikaragosi na majibu ya mtihani
sections.text:
Mitihani hutofautiana katika inachopima hapa. Karatasi za Afrika Kusini huweka maswali kuhusu matangazo na vikaragosi. Cambridge IGCSE huuliza jinsi waandishi wanavyowashawishi wasomaji, na ufahamu wa WASSCE unajumuisha istilahi za fasihi. Kwa matangazo na vikaragosi, chunguza picha na maneno pamoja.

Jibu zuri lina hatua tatu. Taja mbinu, nukuu maneno na ueleze athari kwa msomaji.
Mfano: The question “Who would refuse clean water?” is rhetorical. It suggests that any sensible reader must agree.

keyPoints: Ukweli unaweza kukaguliwa, lakini maoni ni mtazamo wa mtu binafsi.
Upendeleo ni kupendelea upande mmoja isivyo haki.
Lugha ya kuibua hisia inalenga kuamsha hisia za msomaji.
Swali la balagha halitarajii jibu.
Taja mbinu, nukuu maneno na ueleze athari.

pt.title: Facto, opinião e linguagem persuasiva
pt.short: Como distinguir facto de opinião, detetar parcialidade e explicar como os anúncios e os autores tentam persuadir.

sections.heading: Facto, opinião e parcialidade
sections.text:
Um facto (fact) pode ser verificado e provar-se verdadeiro ou falso. Uma opinião (opinion) é o que alguém pensa ou sente. Palavras como best, should e terrible indicam muitas vezes uma opinião. Um texto pode apresentar uma opinião como se fosse um facto, por isso lê com atenção.
Exemplo: The bridge is 400 metres long. (facto)
Exemplo: The bridge is the most beautiful in the country. (opinião)

Parcialidade (bias) significa favorecer injustamente um dos lados. Um autor parcial pode deixar de fora factos importantes ou apresentar apenas um ponto de vista. Pergunta quem escreveu o texto e em que é que essa pessoa quer que acredites.

sections.heading: Como os autores persuadem
sections.text:
Os autores usam várias técnicas para influenciar os leitores.
A linguagem emotiva (emotive language) escolhe palavras que despertam sentimentos.
Exemplo: Helpless children go hungry every night.
Uma pergunta retórica (rhetorical question) é feita para causar efeito e não espera resposta.
Exemplo: Who would refuse clean water?
A interpelação direta (direct address) fala ao leitor como “you”.
Exemplo: You deserve better.
A repetição (repetition) faz com que uma ideia fique na memória. Os números podem fazer com que uma afirmação pareça certa, por isso pergunta de onde vêm.
Exemplo: Nine out of ten users agree.

sections.heading: Anúncios, cartoons e respostas de exame
sections.text:
Os exames diferem no que avaliam nesta matéria. As provas da África do Sul incluem perguntas sobre anúncios e cartoons. O Cambridge IGCSE pergunta como os autores influenciam os leitores, e a compreensão do WASSCE inclui termos literários. Nos anúncios e nos cartoons, estuda as imagens e as palavras em conjunto.

Uma boa resposta tem três passos. Diz o nome da técnica, cita as palavras e explica o efeito no leitor.
Exemplo: The question “Who would refuse clean water?” is rhetorical. It suggests that any sensible reader must agree.

keyPoints: Um facto pode ser verificado, mas uma opinião é um ponto de vista pessoal.
Parcialidade significa favorecer injustamente um dos lados.
A linguagem emotiva procura despertar os sentimentos do leitor.
Uma pergunta retórica não espera resposta.
Diz o nome da técnica, cita as palavras e explica o efeito.

es.title: Hechos, opiniones y lenguaje persuasivo
es.short: Cómo distinguir un hecho de una opinión, detectar el sesgo y explicar cómo intentan persuadir los anuncios y los autores.

sections.heading: Hechos, opiniones y sesgo
sections.text:
Un hecho (fact) se puede comprobar y demostrar que es verdadero o falso. Una opinión (opinion) es lo que alguien piensa o siente. Palabras como “best”, “should” y “terrible” suelen indicar una opinión. Un texto puede presentar una opinión como si fuera un hecho, así que lee con atención.
Ejemplo: The bridge is 400 metres long. (hecho)
Ejemplo: The bridge is the most beautiful in the country. (opinión)

El sesgo (bias) significa favorecer injustamente a una de las partes. Un autor sesgado puede omitir hechos importantes o dar solo un punto de vista. Pregúntate quién escribió el texto y qué quiere que creas.

sections.heading: Cómo persuaden los autores
sections.text:
Los autores usan varias técnicas para influir en los lectores.
El lenguaje emotivo (emotive language) elige palabras que despiertan sentimientos.
Ejemplo: Helpless children go hungry every night.
Una pregunta retórica (rhetorical question) se hace por su efecto y no espera respuesta.
Ejemplo: Who would refuse clean water?
La interpelación directa (direct address) se dirige al lector como “you”.
Ejemplo: You deserve better.
La repetición (repetition) hace que una idea se quede en la mente. Los números pueden hacer que una afirmación suene segura, así que pregúntate de dónde salen.
Ejemplo: Nine out of ten users agree.

sections.heading: Anuncios, viñetas y respuestas de examen
sections.text:
Lo que se evalúa aquí varía según el examen. Los exámenes sudafricanos incluyen preguntas sobre anuncios y viñetas. Cambridge IGCSE pregunta cómo influyen los autores en los lectores, y la comprensión lectora del WASSCE incluye términos literarios. En los anuncios y las viñetas, estudia juntas las imágenes y las palabras.

Una buena respuesta tiene tres pasos. Nombra la técnica, cita las palabras y explica el efecto en el lector.
Ejemplo: The question “Who would refuse clean water?” is rhetorical. It suggests that any sensible reader must agree.

keyPoints: Un hecho se puede comprobar, pero una opinión es un punto de vista personal.
El sesgo significa favorecer injustamente a una de las partes.
El lenguaje emotivo busca despertar los sentimientos del lector.
Una pregunta retórica no espera respuesta.
Nombra la técnica, cita las palabras y explica el efecto.

yo.title: Fact, opinion àti persuasive language
yo.short: Bí a ṣe ń ya fact sọ́tọ̀ kúrò lára opinion, bí a ṣe ń rí bias, àti bí àwọn ìpolówó ọjà àti òǹkọ̀wé ṣe ń gbìyànjú láti yíni lọ́kàn padà.

sections.heading: Fact, opinion àti bias
sections.text:
Fact (òótọ́ tí a lè yẹ̀wò) jẹ́ ohun tí a lè yẹ̀wò, kí a sì fi hàn pé òótọ́ ni tàbí pé kì í ṣe òótọ́. Opinion (èrò) ni ohun tí ẹnì kan rò tàbí tó ń ṣe é lára. Àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ bíi best, should àti terrible sábà máa ń fi opinion hàn. Àyọkà kan lè gbé opinion kalẹ̀ bí ẹni pé fact ni, nítorí náà kàwé pẹ̀lú ìṣọ́ra.
Àpẹẹrẹ: The bridge is 400 metres long. (fact)
Àpẹẹrẹ: The bridge is the most beautiful in the country. (opinion)

Bias (ojúsàájú) túmọ̀ sí gbígbè sí ẹ̀gbẹ́ kan lọ́nà tí kò tọ́. Òǹkọ̀wé tó ní bias lè fi àwọn fact pàtàkì sílẹ̀, tàbí kó sọ èrò ẹ̀gbẹ́ kan ṣoṣo. Béèrè pé ta ló kọ àyọkà náà, àti pé kí ni ó fẹ́ kí o gbàgbọ́.

sections.heading: Bí àwọn òǹkọ̀wé ṣe ń yíni lọ́kàn padà
sections.text:
Àwọn òǹkọ̀wé ń lo ọ̀pọ̀ ọgbọ́n láti nípa lórí àwọn òǹkàwé.
Emotive language ń yan àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ tó ń ru ìmọ̀lára sókè.
Àpẹẹrẹ: Helpless children go hungry every night.
Rhetorical question jẹ́ ìbéèrè tí a béèrè fún ipa tó máa ní, kò sì retí ìdáhùn.
Àpẹẹrẹ: Who would refuse clean water?
Direct address ń bá òǹkàwé sọ̀rọ̀ nípa lílo “you”.
Àpẹẹrẹ: You deserve better.
Repetition (àtúnsọ) ń mú kí èrò kan dúró sí ọkàn. Nọ́ńbà lè mú kí ọ̀rọ̀ kan dún bí ohun tó dájú, nítorí náà béèrè ibi tí wọ́n ti wá.
Àpẹẹrẹ: Nine out of ten users agree.

sections.heading: Ìpolówó ọjà, cartoon àti ìdáhùn ìdánwò
sections.text:
Ohun tí àwọn ìdánwò ń dán wò níbí yàtọ̀ síra. Àwọn ìwé ìdánwò Gúúsù Áfíríkà máa ń béèrè ìbéèrè lórí ìpolówó ọjà àti cartoon (àwòrán apanilẹ́rìn-ín). Cambridge IGCSE ń béèrè bí àwọn òǹkọ̀wé ṣe ń nípa lórí àwọn òǹkàwé, comprehension WASSCE sì ní àwọn literary term (àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ ẹ̀kọ́ lítírésọ̀) nínú. Pẹ̀lú ìpolówó ọjà àti cartoon, kẹ́kọ̀ọ́ àwòrán àti ọ̀rọ̀ pọ̀.

Ìdáhùn tó dára ní ìgbésẹ̀ mẹ́ta. Sọ orúkọ ọgbọ́n náà, fa ọ̀rọ̀ náà yọ, kí o sì ṣàlàyé ipa rẹ̀ lórí òǹkàwé.
Àpẹẹrẹ: The question “Who would refuse clean water?” is rhetorical. It suggests that any sensible reader must agree.

keyPoints: A lè yẹ fact wò, ṣùgbọ́n opinion jẹ́ èrò ẹnì kan.
Bias túmọ̀ sí gbígbè sí ẹ̀gbẹ́ kan lọ́nà tí kò tọ́.
Emotive language ń fẹ́ ru ìmọ̀lára òǹkàwé sókè.
Rhetorical question kì í retí ìdáhùn.
Sọ orúkọ ọgbọ́n náà, fa ọ̀rọ̀ náà yọ, kí o sì ṣàlàyé ipa rẹ̀.

ig.title: Fact, opinion na persuasive language
ig.short: Ịmata fact na opinion, ịhụ bias, na ịkọwa otú adverts na ndị edemede si anwa ime ka mmadụ kweta.

sections.heading: Fact, opinion na bias
sections.text:
Fact bụ ihe a pụrụ inyocha wee gosi na ọ bụ eziokwu ma ọ bụ ụgha. Opinion (echiche) bụ ihe mmadụ chere ma ọ bụ nwere n’obi. Okwu dị ka best, should na terrible na-egosikarị opinion. Ederede nwere ike igosi opinion dị ka a ga-asị na ọ bụ fact, ya mere jiri nlezianya gụọ.
Ihe atụ: The bridge is 400 metres long. (fact)
Ihe atụ: The bridge is the most beautiful in the country. (opinion)

Bias pụtara ịkwado otu akụkụ n’ụzọ na-ezighị ezi. Onye edemede nwere bias nwere ike ịhapụ eziokwu ndị dị mkpa, ma ọ bụ nye naanị otu echiche. Jụọ onye dere ederede ahụ, na ihe ọ chọrọ ka i kwere.

sections.heading: Otú ndị edemede si eme ka mmadụ kweta
sections.text:
Ndị edemede na-eji ụzọ dị iche iche emetụta ndị na-agụ ihe.
Emotive language na-ahọrọ okwu na-akpali mmetụta.
Ihe atụ: Helpless children go hungry every night.
Rhetorical question bụ ajụjụ a jụrụ iji mee ka o nwee mmetụta, ọ naghị atụ anya azịza.
Ihe atụ: Who would refuse clean water?
Direct address na-agwa onye na-agụ ya okwu dị ka “you”.
Ihe atụ: You deserve better.
Repetition (ikwughachi) na-eme ka echiche nọgide n’uche. Ọnụọgụ nwere ike ime ka ihe a na-ekwu daa ka ihe e ji n’aka, ya mere jụọ ebe ha si.
Ihe atụ: Nine out of ten users agree.

sections.heading: Adverts, cartoons na azịza ule
sections.text:
Ule dị iche n’ihe ha na-anwale ebe a. Akwụkwọ ule South Africa na-ajụ ajụjụ banyere adverts na cartoons. Cambridge IGCSE na-ajụ otú ndị edemede si emetụta ndị na-agụ ihe, comprehension nke WASSCE gụnyekwara literary terms (okwu ọmụmụ Literature). Maka adverts na cartoons, mụọ foto na okwu ndị ahụ ọnụ.

Ezigbo azịza nwere nzọụkwụ atọ. Kpọọ aha ụzọ ahụ e jiri, depụta okwu ndị ahụ, ma kọwaa mmetụta ya n’onye na-agụ ya.
Ihe atụ: The question “Who would refuse clean water?” is rhetorical. It suggests that any sensible reader must agree.

keyPoints: A pụrụ inyocha fact, mana opinion bụ echiche mmadụ n’onwe ya.
Bias pụtara ịkwado otu akụkụ n’ụzọ na-ezighị ezi.
Emotive language na-achọ ịkpali mmetụta onye na-agụ ya.
Rhetorical question anaghị atụ anya azịza.
Kpọọ aha ụzọ ahụ e jiri, depụta okwu ndị ahụ, ma kọwaa mmetụta ya.

ha.title: Fact, opinion da persuasive language (harshen rinjayarwa)
ha.short: Bambance fact da opinion, gano bias, da bayyana yadda tallace-tallace da marubuta suke ƙoƙarin rinjayar mutane.

sections.heading: Fact, opinion da bias
sections.text:
Fact abu ne da za a iya dubawa a nuna cewa gaskiya ne ko ƙarya ne. Opinion (ra’ayi) shi ne abin da wani yake tunani ko yake ji. Kalmomi kamar best, should da terrible sau da yawa suna nuna opinion. Rubutu yana iya gabatar da opinion kamar fact ne, don haka ka karanta a hankali.
Misali: The bridge is 400 metres long. (fact)
Misali: The bridge is the most beautiful in the country. (opinion)

Bias (nuna son kai) yana nufin goyon bayan ɓangare ɗaya ba bisa adalci ba. Marubuci mai bias yana iya cire muhimman facts, ko ya ba da ra’ayi guda kawai. Ka tambayi wa ya rubuta wannan rubutu, da kuma abin da yake so ka yarda da shi.

sections.heading: Yadda marubuta suke rinjayar mai karatu
sections.text:
Marubuta suna amfani da dabaru (techniques) da dama don su yi tasiri a kan masu karatu.
Emotive language yana zaɓar kalmomin da ke motsa zuciya.
Misali: Helpless children go hungry every night.
Rhetorical question ana yin sa ne don tasiri, kuma ba ya sa ran amsa.
Misali: Who would refuse clean water?
Direct address yana magana da mai karatu a matsayin “you”.
Misali: You deserve better.
Maimaitawa (repetition) tana sa tunani ya zauna a zuciya. Lambobi suna iya sa da’awa ta yi kamar tabbas ce, don haka ka tambayi inda suka fito.
Misali: Nine out of ten users agree.

sections.heading: Tallace-tallace, cartoons da amsoshin jarrabawa
sections.text:
Jarrabawoyi sun bambanta a abin da suke gwadawa a nan. Takardun Afirka ta Kudu suna kawo tambayoyi kan tallace-tallace (adverts) da cartoons (zane-zanen ban dariya). Cambridge IGCSE yana tambayar yadda marubuta suke tasiri a kan masu karatu, kuma comprehension na WASSCE ya ƙunshi literary terms (kalmomin nazarin adabi). A tallace-tallace da cartoons, ka yi nazarin hotunan da kalmomin tare.

Amsa mai kyau tana da matakai uku. Ka faɗi sunan dabarar, ka yi ambaton kalmomin, kuma ka bayyana tasirinsu a kan mai karatu.
Misali: The question “Who would refuse clean water?” is rhetorical. It suggests that any sensible reader must agree.

keyPoints: Ana iya duba fact, amma opinion ra’ayin mutum ne.
Bias yana nufin goyon bayan ɓangare ɗaya ba bisa adalci ba.
Emotive language yana da nufin motsa zuciyar mai karatu.
Rhetorical question ba ya sa ran amsa.
Ka faɗi sunan dabarar, ka yi ambaton kalmomin, kuma ka bayyana tasirin.

en.title: Planning an essay and writing paragraphs
en.short: How to read the task, plan quickly, and build clear paragraphs with links between ideas.

sections.heading: Before you write
sections.text:
An essay, or composition, is a connected piece of writing on one subject. Good essays begin with a plan. First, read the question and underline the key words. Decide on the type of essay, the reader and the required length. The WASSCE syllabus sets a minimum of 450 words, and study guides give the same figure for NECO. Other papers differ, so check yours.

Next, spend a few minutes noting your ideas. Choose your best points and put them in a sensible order. Here is a short plan for one topic.
Example: Why every school needs a library
Example: Introduction: what a library offers
Example: Point 1: free access to books
Example: Point 2: a quiet place to study
Example: Point 3: research skills
Example: Conclusion: the main benefit

sections.heading: The parts of an essay
sections.text:
The introduction gains interest and shows what the essay is about. The body develops one main idea in each paragraph. The conclusion brings the ideas together. It should add no new point.

A strong paragraph has a topic sentence, which states its main idea. Further sentences then explain it or give an example. Linking words help the reader to follow your ideas.
Example: A library gives every student free access to books.
Example: Firstly, moreover, however, for example, therefore, finally

sections.heading: After you write
sections.text: Leave time to check your work. Look for spelling, punctuation, concord and tense. Check also that every paragraph answers the question. Do not memorise an essay and force it onto a different question, because examiners mark what the question asks.

keyPoints: Underline key words and identify the type of essay first.
Make a short plan before you start writing.
Give each paragraph one main idea and a topic sentence.
A conclusion adds no new point.
Always leave time to check your work.

pcm.title: How to plan essay and write paragraphs
pcm.short: How to read the task, plan quick, and build clear paragraphs with links between ideas.

Essay, or composition, na connected writing on one subject. Good essays dey begin with plan. First, read the question and underline the key words. Decide the type of essay, the reader and the length wey dem want. The WASSCE syllabus set minimum of 450 words, and study guides dey give the same figure for NECO. Other papers different, so check your own.

Next, use few minutes write down your ideas. Choose your best points and put them for sensible order. This na short plan for one topic.

sections.text:
The introduction dey catch interest and show wetin the essay dey talk about. The body dey develop one main idea for each paragraph. The conclusion dey bring the ideas together. E no suppose add new point.

Strong paragraph get topic sentence, wey dey state im main idea. Other sentences go then explain am or give example. Linking words dey help the reader follow your ideas.

fr.title: Préparer une rédaction et écrire des paragraphes
fr.short: Comment lire le sujet, faire un plan rapide et construire des paragraphes clairs avec des liens entre les idées.

sections.heading: Avant d’écrire
sections.text:
Une rédaction (essay ou composition) est un écrit suivi sur un seul sujet. Les bonnes rédactions commencent par un plan. D’abord, lis la question et souligne les mots clés. Décide du type de rédaction, du lecteur et de la longueur demandée. Le programme du WASSCE fixe un minimum de 450 mots, et les guides d’étude donnent le même chiffre pour le NECO. D’autres épreuves sont différentes, alors vérifie la tienne.

Ensuite, prends quelques minutes pour noter tes idées. Choisis tes meilleures idées et mets-les dans un ordre logique. Voici un court plan pour un sujet.
Exemple : Why every school needs a library
Exemple : Introduction: what a library offers
Exemple : Point 1: free access to books
Exemple : Point 2: a quiet place to study
Exemple : Point 3: research skills
Exemple : Conclusion: the main benefit

sections.heading: Les parties d’une rédaction
sections.text:
L’introduction éveille l’intérêt et montre de quoi parle la rédaction. Le développement traite une idée principale dans chaque paragraphe. La conclusion rassemble les idées. Elle ne doit ajouter aucune idée nouvelle.

Un bon paragraphe a une phrase clé (topic sentence), qui énonce son idée principale. D’autres phrases l’expliquent ensuite ou donnent un exemple. Les mots de liaison (linking words) aident le lecteur à suivre tes idées.
Exemple : A library gives every student free access to books.
Exemple : Firstly, moreover, however, for example, therefore, finally

sections.heading: Après avoir écrit
sections.text: Garde du temps pour vérifier ton travail. Regarde l’orthographe, la ponctuation, l’accord (concord) et les temps. Vérifie aussi que chaque paragraphe répond à la question. N’apprends pas une rédaction par cœur pour la plaquer sur une autre question, car les correcteurs notent ce que la question demande.

keyPoints: Souligne d’abord les mots clés et repère le type de rédaction.
Fais un court plan avant de commencer à écrire.
Donne à chaque paragraphe une idée principale et une phrase clé.
Une conclusion n’ajoute aucune idée nouvelle.
Garde toujours du temps pour vérifier ton travail.

ar.title: تخطيط المقال وكتابة الفقرات
ar.short: كيف تقرأ المطلوب، وتخطط بسرعة، وتبني فقرات واضحة مترابطة الأفكار.

sections.heading: قبل أن تكتب
sections.text:
المقال ⁦(essay)⁩ أو الإنشاء ⁦(composition)⁩ نص مترابط عن موضوع واحد. وتبدأ المقالات الجيدة بخطة. أولًا، اقرأ السؤال وضع خطًا تحت الكلمات الأساسية. وحدد نوع المقال والقارئ والطول المطلوب. ويحدد منهج WASSCE حدًا أدنى قدره 450 كلمة، وتعطي أدلة المذاكرة الرقم نفسه لامتحان NECO. وتختلف الأوراق الأخرى، فتحقق من ورقتك.

بعد ذلك، اقضِ بضع دقائق في تدوين أفكارك. واختر أفضل نقاطك وضعها في ترتيب منطقي. إليك خطة قصيرة لموضوع واحد.
مثال: ⁦Why every school needs a library⁩
مثال: ⁦Introduction: what a library offers⁩
مثال: ⁦Point 1: free access to books⁩
مثال: ⁦Point 2: a quiet place to study⁩
مثال: ⁦Point 3: research skills⁩
مثال: ⁦Conclusion: the main benefit⁩

sections.heading: أجزاء المقال
sections.text:
المقدمة ⁦(introduction)⁩ تجذب الاهتمام وتبيّن موضوع المقال. وصلب المقال ⁦(body)⁩ يطوّر فكرة رئيسية واحدة في كل فقرة. والخاتمة ⁦(conclusion)⁩ تجمع الأفكار. ولا ينبغي أن تضيف نقطة جديدة.

الفقرة القوية فيها جملة موضوعية ⁦(topic sentence)⁩، تذكر فكرتها الرئيسية. ثم تشرحها جمل أخرى أو تعطي مثالًا. وتساعد كلمات الربط ⁦(linking words)⁩ القارئ على تتبع أفكارك.
مثال: ⁦A library gives every student free access to books⁩.
مثال: ⁦Firstly, moreover, however, for example, therefore, finally⁩

sections.heading: بعد أن تكتب
sections.text: اترك وقتًا لمراجعة عملك. ابحث عن أخطاء التهجئة وعلامات الترقيم والتوافق ⁦(concord)⁩ والزمن. وتحقق أيضًا من أن كل فقرة تجيب عن السؤال. ولا تحفظ مقالًا عن ظهر قلب وتفرضه على سؤال مختلف، لأن المصححين يقيّمون ما يطلبه السؤال.

keyPoints: ضع خطًا تحت الكلمات الأساسية وحدد نوع المقال أولًا.
ضع خطة قصيرة قبل أن تبدأ الكتابة.
اجعل لكل فقرة فكرة رئيسية واحدة وجملة موضوعية.
لا تضيف الخاتمة نقطة جديدة.
اترك دائمًا وقتًا لمراجعة عملك.

sw.title: Kupanga insha na kuandika aya
sw.short: Jinsi ya kusoma kazi uliyopewa, kupanga haraka, na kujenga aya zilizo wazi zenye viungo kati ya mawazo.

sections.heading: Kabla ya kuandika
sections.text:
Insha (essay au composition) ni maandishi yaliyounganika kuhusu mada moja. Insha nzuri huanza na mpango. Kwanza, soma swali na upigie mstari maneno muhimu. Amua aina ya insha, msomaji na urefu unaohitajika. Muhtasari (syllabus) wa WASSCE unaweka kiwango cha chini cha maneno 450, na miongozo ya kujisomea hutoa kiasi hicho hicho kwa NECO. Karatasi nyingine hutofautiana, kwa hiyo angalia yako.

Kisha, tumia dakika chache kuandika mawazo yako. Chagua hoja zako bora na uziweke katika mpangilio wenye mantiki. Huu hapa ni mpango mfupi wa mada moja.
Mfano: Why every school needs a library
Mfano: Introduction: what a library offers
Mfano: Point 1: free access to books
Mfano: Point 2: a quiet place to study
Mfano: Point 3: research skills
Mfano: Conclusion: the main benefit

sections.heading: Sehemu za insha
sections.text:
Utangulizi (introduction) huvuta shauku na huonyesha insha inahusu nini. Kiini (body) hukuza wazo kuu moja katika kila aya. Hitimisho (conclusion) huleta mawazo pamoja. Halipaswi kuongeza hoja mpya.

Aya imara ina sentensi kuu (topic sentence), inayoeleza wazo lake kuu. Sentensi zinazofuata kisha hulifafanua au kutoa mfano. Maneno ya kuunganisha (linking words) humsaidia msomaji kufuata mawazo yako.
Mfano: A library gives every student free access to books.
Mfano: Firstly, moreover, however, for example, therefore, finally

sections.heading: Baada ya kuandika
sections.text: Acha muda wa kukagua kazi yako. Angalia tahajia, uakifishaji, upatanisho (concord) na njeo. Kagua pia kwamba kila aya inajibu swali. Usikariri insha na kuilazimisha katika swali tofauti, kwa sababu wasahihishaji hutoa alama kwa kile ambacho swali linauliza.

keyPoints: Pigia mstari maneno muhimu na utambue aina ya insha kwanza.
Andaa mpango mfupi kabla ya kuanza kuandika.
Kila aya iwe na wazo kuu moja na sentensi kuu.
Hitimisho haliongezi hoja mpya.
Daima acha muda wa kukagua kazi yako.

pt.title: Planear uma composição e escrever parágrafos
pt.short: Como ler a tarefa, planear depressa e construir parágrafos claros, com ligações entre as ideias.

sections.heading: Antes de escreveres
sections.text:
Uma composição (essay ou composition) é um texto contínuo sobre um único assunto. As boas composições começam com um plano. Primeiro, lê a pergunta e sublinha as palavras-chave. Decide qual é o tipo de composição, quem é o leitor e qual é a extensão exigida. O programa do WASSCE fixa um mínimo de 450 palavras, e os guias de estudo indicam o mesmo número para o NECO. Outras provas são diferentes, por isso confirma a tua.

A seguir, passa alguns minutos a anotar as tuas ideias. Escolhe as melhores e coloca-as numa ordem lógica. Eis um plano curto para um tema.
Exemplo: Why every school needs a library
Exemplo: Introduction: what a library offers
Exemplo: Point 1: free access to books
Exemplo: Point 2: a quiet place to study
Exemplo: Point 3: research skills
Exemplo: Conclusion: the main benefit

sections.heading: As partes de uma composição
sections.text:
A introdução desperta o interesse e mostra de que trata a composição. O desenvolvimento apresenta uma ideia principal em cada parágrafo. A conclusão reúne as ideias. Não deve acrescentar nenhuma ideia nova.

Um bom parágrafo tem uma frase-tópico (topic sentence), que indica a sua ideia principal. As frases seguintes explicam-na ou dão um exemplo. As palavras de ligação (linking words) ajudam o leitor a seguir as tuas ideias.
Exemplo: A library gives every student free access to books.
Exemplo: Firstly, moreover, however, for example, therefore, finally

sections.heading: Depois de escreveres
sections.text: Deixa tempo para rever o teu trabalho. Procura erros de ortografia, de pontuação, de concordância e de tempos verbais. Verifica também se todos os parágrafos respondem à pergunta. Não decores uma composição para a forçares a encaixar noutra pergunta, porque os examinadores classificam o que a pergunta pede.

keyPoints: Sublinha as palavras-chave e identifica primeiro o tipo de composição.
Faz um plano curto antes de começares a escrever.
Dá a cada parágrafo uma ideia principal e uma frase-tópico.
Uma conclusão não acrescenta nenhuma ideia nova.
Deixa sempre tempo para rever o teu trabalho.

es.title: Cómo planificar un ensayo y escribir párrafos
es.short: Cómo leer la tarea, planificar con rapidez y construir párrafos claros con enlaces entre las ideas.

sections.heading: Antes de escribir
sections.text:
Un ensayo (essay), o redacción (composition), es un texto cohesionado sobre un solo tema. Los buenos ensayos empiezan con un plan. Primero, lee la pregunta y subraya las palabras clave. Decide el tipo de ensayo, el lector y la extensión que se pide. El programa del WASSCE fija un mínimo de 450 palabras, y las guías de estudio dan la misma cifra para el NECO. Otros exámenes son distintos, así que comprueba el tuyo.

Después, dedica unos minutos a anotar tus ideas. Elige tus mejores ideas y ponlas en un orden lógico. Aquí tienes un plan breve para un tema.
Ejemplo: Why every school needs a library
Ejemplo: Introduction: what a library offers
Ejemplo: Point 1: free access to books
Ejemplo: Point 2: a quiet place to study
Ejemplo: Point 3: research skills
Ejemplo: Conclusion: the main benefit

sections.heading: Las partes de un ensayo
sections.text:
La introducción despierta el interés y muestra de qué trata el ensayo. El cuerpo desarrolla una idea principal en cada párrafo. La conclusión reúne las ideas. No debe añadir ninguna idea nueva.

Un buen párrafo tiene una oración temática (topic sentence), que expresa su idea principal. Las demás oraciones la explican o dan un ejemplo. Las palabras de enlace (linking words) ayudan al lector a seguir tus ideas.
Ejemplo: A library gives every student free access to books.
Ejemplo: Firstly, moreover, however, for example, therefore, finally

sections.heading: Después de escribir
sections.text: Deja tiempo para revisar tu trabajo. Busca errores de ortografía, puntuación, concordancia y tiempos verbales. Comprueba también que cada párrafo responde a la pregunta. No memorices un ensayo para forzarlo en una pregunta distinta, porque los examinadores califican lo que pide la pregunta.

keyPoints: Primero subraya las palabras clave e identifica el tipo de ensayo.
Haz un plan breve antes de empezar a escribir.
Da a cada párrafo una idea principal y una oración temática.
La conclusión no añade ninguna idea nueva.
Deja siempre tiempo para revisar tu trabajo.

yo.title: Ṣíṣètò àròkọ àti kíkọ paragraph
yo.short: Bí a ṣe ń ka iṣẹ́ náà, tí a ń ṣètò kíákíá, tí a sì ń kọ paragraph tó ṣe kedere pẹ̀lú ìsopọ̀ láàárín àwọn èrò.

sections.heading: Kí o tó kọ̀wé
sections.text:
Essay (àròkọ), tàbí composition, jẹ́ ìkọ̀wé tó so pọ̀ lórí kókó ọ̀rọ̀ kan. Àròkọ tó dára máa ń bẹ̀rẹ̀ pẹ̀lú ètò. Kọ́kọ́ ka ìbéèrè náà, kí o sì fa ìlà sí abẹ́ àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ pàtàkì. Pinnu irú àròkọ náà, ẹni tí yóò kà á àti gígùn tí a béèrè. Syllabus (ìlànà ẹ̀kọ́) WASSCE sọ pé ó kéré tán ọ̀rọ̀ 450, àwọn ìwé ìtọ́sọ́nà ẹ̀kọ́ sì fi iye kan náà hàn fún NECO. Àwọn ìwé ìdánwò mìíràn yàtọ̀, nítorí náà yẹ tìrẹ wò.

Lẹ́yìn náà, lo ìṣẹ́jú díẹ̀ láti kọ àwọn èrò rẹ sílẹ̀. Yan àwọn kókó rẹ tó dára jù lọ, kí o sì tò wọ́n ní ètò tó bọ́gbọ́n mu. Ètò kúkúrú fún kókó ọ̀rọ̀ kan nìyí.
Àpẹẹrẹ: Why every school needs a library
Àpẹẹrẹ: Introduction: what a library offers
Àpẹẹrẹ: Point 1: free access to books
Àpẹẹrẹ: Point 2: a quiet place to study
Àpẹẹrẹ: Point 3: research skills
Àpẹẹrẹ: Conclusion: the main benefit

sections.heading: Àwọn apá àròkọ
sections.text:
Introduction (ìfáàrà) ń fa ìfẹ́ òǹkàwé, ó sì ń fi ohun tí àròkọ náà dá lé hàn. Body (apá àárín) ń ṣàlàyé èrò pàtàkì kan nínú paragraph (ìpínrọ̀) kọ̀ọ̀kan. Conclusion (ìparí) ń kó àwọn èrò náà jọ. Kò yẹ kí ó fi kókó tuntun kún un.

Paragraph tó lágbára ní topic sentence, tó ń sọ èrò pàtàkì rẹ̀. Àwọn gbólóhùn mìíràn á wá ṣàlàyé rẹ̀ tàbí kí wọ́n fúnni ní àpẹẹrẹ. Àwọn linking word (ọ̀rọ̀ ìsopọ̀) ń ran òǹkàwé lọ́wọ́ láti tẹ̀lé àwọn èrò rẹ.
Àpẹẹrẹ: A library gives every student free access to books.
Àpẹẹrẹ: Firstly, moreover, however, for example, therefore, finally

sections.heading: Lẹ́yìn tí o bá kọ̀wé tán
sections.text: Fi àkókò sílẹ̀ láti yẹ iṣẹ́ rẹ wò. Wo spelling, punctuation, concord àti tense. Tún wò ó pé gbogbo paragraph ló dáhùn ìbéèrè náà. Má ṣe há àròkọ kan sórí kí o sì fi tipátipá lò ó fún ìbéèrè mìíràn, nítorí pé ohun tí ìbéèrè béèrè ni àwọn tó ń máàkì ìdánwò máa ń fún ní máàkì.

keyPoints: Kọ́kọ́ fa ìlà sí abẹ́ àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ pàtàkì, kí o sì mọ irú àròkọ náà.
Ṣe ètò kúkúrú kí o tó bẹ̀rẹ̀ sí í kọ̀wé.
Fún paragraph kọ̀ọ̀kan ní èrò pàtàkì kan àti topic sentence.
Conclusion kì í fi kókó tuntun kún un.
Máa fi àkókò sílẹ̀ nígbà gbogbo láti yẹ iṣẹ́ rẹ wò.

ig.title: Ịhazi essay na ide paragraphs
ig.short: Otú e si agụ ajụjụ, ahazi atụmatụ ngwa ngwa, ma wuo paragraphs doro anya nke nwere njikọ n’etiti echiche.

sections.heading: Tupu i dee
sections.text:
Essay (edemede), ma ọ bụ composition, bụ ederede jikọrọ ọnụ banyere otu isiokwu. Ezigbo essays na-amalite n’atụmatụ. Nke mbụ, gụọ ajụjụ ahụ wee dọọ ahịrị n’okpuru okwu ndị dị mkpa. Kpebie ụdị essay, onye ga-agụ ya na ogologo a chọrọ. Syllabus WASSCE na-ekwu opekata mpe okwu 450, akwụkwọ nduzi ọmụmụ na-enyekwa otu ọnụọgụ ahụ maka NECO. Akwụkwọ ule ndị ọzọ dị iche, ya mere lelee nke gị.

Nke ọzọ, were nkeji ole na ole dee echiche gị. Họrọ isi ihe gị kacha mma ma tinye ha n’usoro kwesịrị ekwesị. Lee obere atụmatụ maka otu isiokwu.
Ihe atụ: Why every school needs a library
Ihe atụ: Introduction: what a library offers
Ihe atụ: Point 1: free access to books
Ihe atụ: Point 2: a quiet place to study
Ihe atụ: Point 3: research skills
Ihe atụ: Conclusion: the main benefit

sections.heading: Akụkụ essay
sections.text:
Introduction (mmalite) na-adọta mmasị ma na-egosi ihe essay ahụ bụ maka ya. Body (etiti) na-akọwa otu isi echiche na paragraph (nkeji edemede) ọ bụla. Conclusion (mmechi) na-achịkọta echiche ndị ahụ ọnụ. Ọ kwesịghị ịgbakwunye isi ihe ọhụrụ.

Ezigbo paragraph nwere topic sentence, nke na-ekwu isi echiche ya. Ahịrịokwu ndị ọzọ na-akọwa ya ma ọ bụ na-enye ihe atụ. Okwu njikọ (linking words) na-enyere onye na-agụ ya aka iso echiche gị.
Ihe atụ: A library gives every student free access to books.
Ihe atụ: Firstly, moreover, however, for example, therefore, finally

sections.heading: Mgbe i dechara
sections.text: Hapụ oge iji lelee ọrụ gị. Chọọ mmejọ na spelling, punctuation, concord na tense. Leleekwa na paragraph ọ bụla na-aza ajụjụ ahụ. Ebula essay n’isi wee manye ya n’ajụjụ dị iche, n’ihi na ndị na-akara ule na-enye marks (akara ule) maka ihe ajụjụ ahụ jụrụ.

keyPoints: Buru ụzọ dọọ ahịrị n’okpuru okwu ndị dị mkpa ma chọpụta ụdị essay ahụ.
Mee obere atụmatụ tupu ị malite ide ihe.
Nye paragraph ọ bụla otu isi echiche na topic sentence.
Conclusion anaghị agbakwunye isi ihe ọhụrụ.
Mgbe niile, hapụ oge iji lelee ọrụ gị.

ha.title: Tsara essay da rubuta sakin layi
ha.short: Yadda ake karanta aikin, a yi shiri da sauri, a kuma gina sakin layi bayyanannu tare da haɗi tsakanin tunani.

sections.heading: Kafin ka rubuta
sections.text:
Essay (maƙala), ko composition, rubutu ne mai haɗin kai a kan batu ɗaya. Kyawawan essays suna farawa da shiri. Da farko, ka karanta tambayar, ka ja layi a ƙarƙashin muhimman kalmomi. Ka yanke shawara kan nau’in essay, mai karatu da tsawon da ake buƙata. Tsarin karatun WASSCE (syllabus) ya ƙayyade aƙalla kalmomi 450, kuma littattafan nazari suna ba da wannan adadi ga NECO. Sauran takardun jarrabawa sun bambanta, don haka ka duba naka.

Daga nan, ka ɗauki ’yan mintuna kana rubuta tunaninka. Ka zaɓi mafi kyawun batutuwanka ka sanya su a cikin tsari mai ma’ana. Ga gajeren shiri na wani batu.
Misali: Why every school needs a library
Misali: Introduction: what a library offers
Misali: Point 1: free access to books
Misali: Point 2: a quiet place to study
Misali: Point 3: research skills
Misali: Conclusion: the main benefit

sections.heading: Sassan essay
sections.text:
Introduction (gabatarwa) yana jawo sha’awa kuma yana nuna abin da essay ɗin yake magana a kai. Body (jikin essay) yana bunƙasa babban tunani ɗaya a kowane sakin layi. Conclusion (kammalawa) yana haɗa tunanin tare. Kada ya ƙara wani sabon batu.

Sakin layi mai ƙarfi yana da topic sentence, wanda ke faɗin babban tunaninsa. Sauran jimloli sai su bayyana shi ko su ba da misali. Linking words (kalmomin haɗawa) suna taimaka wa mai karatu ya bi tunaninka.
Misali: A library gives every student free access to books.
Misali: Firstly, moreover, however, for example, therefore, finally

sections.heading: Bayan ka rubuta
sections.text: Ka bar lokacin duba aikinka. Ka nemi kurakuran spelling, punctuation, concord da tense. Ka kuma duba cewa kowane sakin layi yana amsa tambayar. Kada ka haddace essay ka tilasta shi a kan wata tambaya daban, domin masu duba jarrabawa suna ba da maki kan abin da tambayar ta nema.

keyPoints: Ka fara ja layi a ƙarƙashin muhimman kalmomi, ka gano nau’in essay.
Ka yi gajeren shiri kafin ka fara rubutu.
Ka ba kowane sakin layi babban tunani ɗaya da topic sentence.
Conclusion ba ya ƙara sabon batu.
Ka riƙa barin lokacin duba aikinka a koyaushe.

en.title: Types of essay
en.short: Narrative, descriptive, argumentative and expository essays, and what each one needs.

sections.heading: Narrative and descriptive essays
sections.text:
A narrative essay tells a story. It needs a setting, characters, a problem and an ending. It is usually written in the past tense, and it often uses “I” or “he” and “she”.
Example: As I opened the gate, I heard someone running behind me.

A descriptive essay paints a picture of a person, place or event. It has little plot. It uses details from the five senses: sight, sound, smell, taste and touch.
Example: The market smelled of fried fish, ripe mangoes and wet earth.

sections.heading: Argumentative and persuasive essays
sections.text:
An argumentative essay takes a position on a question and supports it with reasons and evidence. A strong essay also mentions the opposite view and answers it. A persuasive essay also aims to change the reader’s mind. A discursive essay usually gives both sides in a balanced way before reaching a conclusion. Names for these types differ between exam boards, so read the task carefully.
Example: Some people argue that homework wastes time. However, regular practice helps students to remember what they learn.

sections.heading: Expository essays
sections.text:
An expository essay explains a subject or a process. It gives facts in a clear order and does not try to win an argument. The tone is neutral, and the present tense is common.
Example: A bicycle pump pushes air into a tyre through a small valve.

Before you begin, look at what the question asks you to do. “Tell”, “describe”, “argue” and “explain” are the main clues.

keyPoints: Narrative essays tell a story, usually in the past tense.
Descriptive essays use details from the five senses.
Argumentative essays take a position and support it with reasons.
Expository essays explain facts in a neutral tone.
The command word in the question points to the essay type.

pcm.title: Types of essay
pcm.short: Narrative, descriptive, argumentative and expository essays, and wetin each one need.

sections.heading: Narrative and descriptive essays
sections.text:
Narrative essay dey tell story. E need setting, characters, problem and ending. Dem dey usually write am for the past tense, and e dey often use “I” or “he” and “she”.
Example: As I opened the gate, I heard someone running behind me.

Descriptive essay dey paint picture of person, place or event. E no get plenty plot. E dey use details from the five senses: sight, sound, smell, taste and touch.
Example: The market smelled of fried fish, ripe mangoes and wet earth.

sections.heading: Argumentative and persuasive essays
sections.text:
Argumentative essay dey take position on question and support am with reasons and evidence. Strong essay dey also mention the opposite view and answer am. Persuasive essay dey also try change the mind of the reader. Discursive essay dey usually give both sides in balanced way before e reach conclusion. Names for these types no be the same for all exam boards, so read the task with care.
Example: Some people argue that homework wastes time. However, regular practice helps students to remember what they learn.

sections.heading: Expository essays
sections.text:
Expository essay dey explain subject or process. E dey give facts for clear order and e no dey try win argument. The tone dey neutral, and the present tense dey common.

Before you begin, look wetin the question ask you to do. “Tell”, “describe”, “argue” and “explain” na the main clues.

keyPoints: Narrative essays dey tell story, usually for the past tense.
Descriptive essays dey use details from the five senses.
Argumentative essays dey take position and support am with reasons.
Expository essays dey explain facts with neutral tone.
The command word for the question dey point to the essay type.

fr.title: Les types de rédaction
fr.short: Les rédactions narratives, descriptives, argumentatives et explicatives, et ce dont chacune a besoin.

sections.heading: Les rédactions narratives et descriptives
sections.text:
Une rédaction narrative (narrative essay) raconte une histoire. Elle a besoin d’un cadre, de personnages, d’un problème et d’une fin. Elle est généralement écrite au passé, et elle utilise souvent “I”, ou “he” et “she”.
Exemple : As I opened the gate, I heard someone running behind me.

Une rédaction descriptive (descriptive essay) dresse le portrait d’une personne, d’un lieu ou d’un événement. Elle a peu d’intrigue. Elle utilise des détails venant des cinq sens : la vue, l’ouïe, l’odorat, le goût et le toucher.
Exemple : The market smelled of fried fish, ripe mangoes and wet earth.

sections.heading: Les rédactions argumentatives et persuasives
sections.text:
Une rédaction argumentative (argumentative essay) prend position sur une question et défend cette position avec des raisons et des preuves. Une bonne rédaction mentionne aussi le point de vue opposé et y répond. Une rédaction persuasive (persuasive essay) vise en plus à faire changer d’avis le lecteur. Une rédaction discursive (discursive essay) présente généralement les deux côtés de façon équilibrée avant d’arriver à une conclusion. Les noms de ces types varient selon les organismes d’examen, alors lis le sujet avec attention.
Exemple : Some people argue that homework wastes time. However, regular practice helps students to remember what they learn.

sections.heading: Les rédactions explicatives
sections.text:
Une rédaction explicative (expository essay) explique un sujet ou un processus. Elle donne des faits dans un ordre clair et ne cherche pas à gagner un débat. Le ton est neutre, et le présent est fréquent.
Exemple : A bicycle pump pushes air into a tyre through a small valve.

Avant de commencer, regarde ce que la question te demande de faire. “Tell”, “describe”, “argue” et “explain” sont les principaux indices.

keyPoints: Les rédactions narratives racontent une histoire, généralement au passé.
Les rédactions descriptives utilisent des détails venant des cinq sens.
Les rédactions argumentatives prennent position et la défendent avec des raisons.
Les rédactions explicatives expliquent des faits sur un ton neutre.
Le mot de consigne dans la question indique le type de rédaction.

ar.title: أنواع المقال
ar.short: المقال القصصي والوصفي والجدلي والتفسيري، وما يحتاج إليه كل منها.

sections.heading: المقال القصصي والمقال الوصفي
sections.text:
المقال القصصي ⁦(narrative essay)⁩ يروي قصة. وهو يحتاج إلى مكان وزمان للأحداث، وشخصيات، ومشكلة، ونهاية. ويُكتب عادةً بزمن الماضي، وكثيرًا ما يستخدم ⁦“I”⁩ أو ⁦“he”⁩ و⁦“she”⁩.
مثال: ⁦As I opened the gate, I heard someone running behind me⁩.

المقال الوصفي ⁦(descriptive essay)⁩ يرسم صورة لشخص أو مكان أو حدث. وأحداثه قليلة. وهو يستخدم تفاصيل من الحواس الخمس: البصر والسمع والشم والذوق واللمس.
مثال: ⁦The market smelled of fried fish, ripe mangoes and wet earth⁩.

sections.heading: المقال الجدلي والمقال الإقناعي
sections.text:
المقال الجدلي ⁦(argumentative essay)⁩ يتخذ موقفًا من سؤال ويدعمه بالأسباب والأدلة. والمقال القوي يذكر أيضًا الرأي المعارض ويرد عليه. والمقال الإقناعي ⁦(persuasive essay)⁩ يهدف أيضًا إلى تغيير رأي القارئ. والمقال النقاشي ⁦(discursive essay)⁩ يعرض عادةً الجانبين بطريقة متوازنة قبل الوصول إلى خاتمة. وتختلف أسماء هذه الأنواع من هيئة امتحانات إلى أخرى، فاقرأ المطلوب بعناية.
مثال: ⁦Some people argue that homework wastes time. However, regular practice helps students to remember what they learn⁩.

sections.heading: المقال التفسيري
sections.text:
المقال التفسيري ⁦(expository essay)⁩ يشرح موضوعًا أو عملية. وهو يعطي الحقائق في ترتيب واضح ولا يحاول كسب جدال. ونبرته محايدة، وزمن المضارع شائع فيه.
مثال: ⁦A bicycle pump pushes air into a tyre through a small valve⁩.

قبل أن تبدأ، انظر إلى ما يطلب منك السؤال أن تفعله. فكلمات ⁦“Tell”⁩ و⁦“describe”⁩ و⁦“argue”⁩ و⁦“explain”⁩ هي الدلائل الرئيسية.

keyPoints: تروي المقالات القصصية قصة، بزمن الماضي عادةً.
تستخدم المقالات الوصفية تفاصيل من الحواس الخمس.
تتخذ المقالات الجدلية موقفًا وتدعمه بالأسباب.
تشرح المقالات التفسيرية الحقائق بنبرة محايدة.
كلمة الأمر في السؤال تدل على نوع المقال.

sw.title: Aina za insha
sw.short: Insha za masimulizi, wasifu, hoja na ufafanuzi, na kile ambacho kila moja inahitaji.

sections.heading: Insha za masimulizi na za wasifu
sections.text:
Insha ya masimulizi (narrative essay) husimulia hadithi. Inahitaji mandhari, wahusika, tatizo na mwisho. Kwa kawaida huandikwa katika wakati uliopita, na mara nyingi hutumia “I” au “he” na “she”.
Mfano: As I opened the gate, I heard someone running behind me.

Insha ya wasifu (descriptive essay) huchora picha ya mtu, mahali au tukio. Ina msuko mdogo wa matukio. Hutumia maelezo kutoka kwa hisi tano: kuona, kusikia, kunusa, kuonja na kugusa.
Mfano: The market smelled of fried fish, ripe mangoes and wet earth.

sections.heading: Insha za hoja na za ushawishi
sections.text:
Insha ya hoja (argumentative essay) huchukua msimamo kuhusu swali na kuutetea kwa sababu na ushahidi. Insha imara pia hutaja mtazamo wa upande wa pili na kuujibu. Insha ya ushawishi (persuasive essay) pia inalenga kubadilisha mawazo ya msomaji. Insha ya mjadala (discursive essay) kwa kawaida hutoa pande zote mbili kwa usawa kabla ya kufikia hitimisho. Majina ya aina hizi hutofautiana kati ya bodi za mitihani, kwa hiyo soma kazi uliyopewa kwa makini.
Mfano: Some people argue that homework wastes time. However, regular practice helps students to remember what they learn.

sections.heading: Insha za ufafanuzi
sections.text:
Insha ya ufafanuzi (expository essay) hueleza mada au mchakato. Hutoa mambo ya kweli kwa mpangilio ulio wazi na haijaribu kushinda mjadala. Toni (tone) yake haiegemei upande wowote, na wakati uliopo hutumiwa mara nyingi.
Mfano: A bicycle pump pushes air into a tyre through a small valve.

Kabla ya kuanza, angalia swali linakutaka ufanye nini. “Tell”, “describe”, “argue” na “explain” ndizo dalili kuu.

keyPoints: Insha za masimulizi husimulia hadithi, kwa kawaida katika wakati uliopita.
Insha za wasifu hutumia maelezo kutoka kwa hisi tano.
Insha za hoja huchukua msimamo na kuutetea kwa sababu.
Insha za ufafanuzi hueleza mambo ya kweli kwa toni isiyoegemea upande wowote.
Neno la amri katika swali huonyesha aina ya insha.

pt.title: Tipos de composição
pt.short: Composições narrativas, descritivas, argumentativas e expositivas, e o que cada uma exige.

sections.heading: Composições narrativas e descritivas
sections.text:
Uma composição narrativa (narrative essay) conta uma história. Precisa de um cenário, de personagens, de um problema e de um final. Escreve-se normalmente no passado e usa muitas vezes “I” ou “he” e “she”.
Exemplo: As I opened the gate, I heard someone running behind me.

Uma composição descritiva (descriptive essay) pinta um retrato de uma pessoa, de um lugar ou de um acontecimento. Tem pouco enredo. Usa pormenores dos cinco sentidos: visão, audição, olfato, paladar e tato.
Exemplo: The market smelled of fried fish, ripe mangoes and wet earth.

sections.heading: Composições argumentativas e persuasivas
sections.text:
Uma composição argumentativa (argumentative essay) toma uma posição sobre uma questão e defende-a com razões e provas. Uma boa composição também refere o ponto de vista contrário e responde-lhe. Uma composição persuasiva (persuasive essay) procura também mudar a opinião do leitor. Uma composição discursiva (discursive essay) apresenta normalmente os dois lados de forma equilibrada antes de chegar a uma conclusão. Os nomes destes tipos variam entre entidades examinadoras, por isso lê a tarefa com atenção.
Exemplo: Some people argue that homework wastes time. However, regular practice helps students to remember what they learn.

sections.heading: Composições expositivas
sections.text:
Uma composição expositiva (expository essay) explica um assunto ou um processo. Apresenta factos por uma ordem clara e não tenta ganhar uma discussão. O tom é neutro, e o presente é comum.
Exemplo: A bicycle pump pushes air into a tyre through a small valve.

Antes de começares, vê o que a pergunta te pede para fazer. “Tell”, “describe”, “argue” e “explain” são as principais pistas.

keyPoints: As composições narrativas contam uma história, normalmente no passado.
As composições descritivas usam pormenores dos cinco sentidos.
As composições argumentativas tomam uma posição e defendem-na com razões.
As composições expositivas explicam factos num tom neutro.
A palavra de instrução da pergunta indica o tipo de composição.

es.title: Tipos de ensayo
